items.title: A retract is an M-polyfold

book.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), before Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), p. 50 (preprint p. 35)
book.statement: A retract $(O, C, E)$ is an M-polyfold, and $d_O(x) = \min d_{C'}(\varphi(x))$ over germs of sc-diffeomorphisms $\varphi : (O, x) \to (O', \varphi(x))$ into retracts.

lean.statement: A nonempty retract $O$ is an M-polyfold on the subtype $O$ with the single chart $\mathrm{id}$; so is a nonempty relatively open $U \subseteq C$ (the text's $X_C$ for $U = C$). Its degeneracy index is Definition 2.4.1 (preprint 2.22) for this structure; two compatible charts give a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between overlap retracts.

diff: The text's description of $d_O$ as a minimum over germs into retracts is replaced by Definition 2.4.1 (preprint 2.22) for the atlas $\{\mathrm{id}\}$, whose charts are such germs restricted to open subsets.
The text's paracompactness of $O$ (as a metric space) is part of the M-polyfold structure on the subtype.

items.title: Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31): $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_O(x)$

book.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), p. 50 (preprint p. 35) (first statement)
book.statement: For a retract $(O, C, E)$ and a smooth $x \in O$, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_O(x)$.

lean.statement: For every M-polyfold $X$, every chart $\varphi$ around $x$ with $\varphi(x)$ on level $1$, every retraction $r$ onto the model $O$ and every presentation of $C$: $\dim(T_{\varphi(x)}O/T^R_{\varphi(x)}O) \le d_X(x)$. In the text's form, for a retract $O$ as an M-polyfold and $x \in O_1$: $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_O(x)$. The core: along a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms $F$ between retracts, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_{C'}(F(x))$. The second statement holds without the equality: $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ at every smooth $x$ (V2.33).

diff: Stated for every chart of every M-polyfold and for points on level $1$; the text's statement is `theorem_2_4_12_retract`.

The proof does not reduce to a chart realizing $d_O(x)$, as the text does: for every other chart $\psi$, $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ induces $T_xO/T^R_xO \cong T_yO'/T^R_yO'$, which embeds in $E'/E'_y$ of dimension $d_{C'}(y)$.

The second statement (equality makes $C_xO$ a partial quadrant) holds without its hypothesis: $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant at every smooth point of every retract (V2.33; formerly G.11). Updated in the third addendum of this page.
For tame retracts the conclusion of the second statement, $C_xO$ a partial quadrant, is proved directly (V2.42).

items.title: Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32): $d_{X_C} = d_C$

book.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32), p. 51 (preprint p. 37)
book.statement: For a partial quadrant $C$, viewed as the M-polyfold $X_C$, $d_C = d_{X_C}$.

lean.statement: For a nonempty relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$, viewed as the M-polyfold $X_U$ (chart $\mathrm{id}$), $d_{X_U}(x) = d_C(x)$ for every $x \in U$. The inequality $d_C \le d_{X_U}$ is proved at level-$1$ points from the core of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31) and extended by approximation with level-$1$ points of the same index and Lemma 2.4.3 (preprint 2.23).

diff: Proved for every relatively open $U \subseteq C$; $U = C$ is the text's case.
Smooth points are not needed: level-$1$ points $T^{-1}(a, w')$, $w' \in W_1$, of the same index suffice.
Theorem 1.3.5 (preprint 1.25) (boundary recognition, Chapter 1, V1.23) is proved in the same file, `Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex.lean`, by this argument (`theorem_1_3_5`).

items.title: Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33): $C_e$ and $E_e$

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33), p. 53 (preprint p. 39)
book.statement: $C_e := \bigcap_{f \in \mathcal F(e)} H_f$ and $E_e := \bigcap_{f \in \mathcal F(e)} f$; $E_e \subset C_e \subset E$, $E_e$ has codimension $d_C(e)$.

lean.statement: For a presentation $T$ of $C$: $C_e = \{v : (Tv)_i \ge 0 \text{ for } (Te)_i = 0\}$ and $E_e = \{v : (Tv)_i = 0 \text{ for } (Te)_i = 0\}$, convex resp. a closed subspace, $E_e \subseteq C_e$, $\dim(E_0/E_e) = d_C(e)$. $E_e$ is the same for every presentation of $C$.

chips: through a presentation, independent of it
diff: Defined through a presentation (the intrinsic description of the text is G.12); the same objects as V2.31.

$E_e$ does not depend on the presentation: for two presentations $T$, $T'$ of the same $C$ and $e \in C$, the two subspaces agree (`minimalSubspaceWith_eq`, the argument of Lemma 1.3.4 (preprint 1.24)).

items.title: Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34): tame retractions and tame retracts

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34), pp. 53–54 (preprint pp. 39–40)
book.statement: An sc-smooth retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ on $U$ and (2) at every smooth $x \in O$ there is an sc-subspace $A \subset E_x$ with $E = T_xO \oplus A$. A tame retract is the image of a tame retraction.

lean.statement: $r$ is tame for the presentation $T$ if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ for $x \in U$ and (2) for every smooth $x \in O_1$ there is $A \le E_x$ with $E = Dr(x)E \oplus A$ an sc-splitting (both summands sc-subspaces, complementary on every level). $r$ is tame if it is tame for every presentation of $C$, equivalently for one; a tame retract is the retract of a tame retraction. The identity of a relatively open $U \subseteq C$ is tame, and restrictions of tame retractions to $U \cap r^{-1}(V)$, $V$ open, are tame.

diff: `IsTame` asks tameness for every presentation of $C$; tameness for one presentation implies it (`IsTameWith.isTame`, from the independence of $E_x$), so the definition is the text's. The theorems of §2.5 (preprint §2.4) assume tameness for the presentation they compute in.
Tameness passes to the restrictions $r|_{U \cap r^{-1}(V)}$, $V$ open (`IsTameWith.restrict`).
\"$E = T_xO \oplus A$\" is an sc-splitting, as an sc-complement must be.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35): $(1 - Dr(x))E \subseteq E_x$

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35), p. 54 (preprint p. 41) (discussion pp. 54–56 (preprint pp. 40–41))
book.statement: For a tame retraction and a smooth $x \in O$, $(1 - Dr(x))E \subseteq E_x$, so in condition (2) one can take $A = (1 - Dr(x))E$.

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$ and $x \in O_1$ smooth. Then $(1 - Dr(x))E \le E_x$ and $E = Dr(x)E \oplus (1 - Dr(x))E$ is an sc-splitting. In coordinates, $\lambda_j \circ Dr(x) = \lambda_j$ for $j \in I(x)$.

diff: Only condition (2) of tameness is used. The text derives $Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$ from condition (1); the sign argument gives it for every sc-smooth retraction at every point of $O_1$.
The sc-splitting is that of the sc-projection $Dr(x)$ at the smooth point $x$.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36): $d_O = d_C$, $T^R_xO$ an sc-subspace, $C_xO$ a partial quadrant

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36), p. 56 (preprint p. 41)
book.statement: For a tame retract and smooth $x$: $T^R_xO$ has codimension $d_O(x)$, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$ (13), and $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$; for every $x \in O$, $d_O(x) = d_C(x)$ (14).

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$. (13) At a smooth $x \in O_1$: $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x) = d_C(x)$; moreover $T_xO$ and $T^R_xO$ are sc-subspaces of $E$, and $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x$ is a partial quadrant in the sc-Banach space $T_xO$ (with the sc-structure induced from $E$). (14) For every $x \in O$: $d_O(x) = d_C(x)$, $O$ with its single chart. More generally, a chart $\varphi$ of any M-polyfold whose model is a tame retract realizes the degeneracy index: $d_X(y) = d_C(\varphi(y))$ for every $y$ in its domain.

diff: (13) and (14) as in the text; the general form for charts of any M-polyfold is what Proposition 2.5.14's (preprint 2.42) \"$d_V(y) = d_X(y)$\" needs.
The approximants $r(a, w_j)$, $w_j \in W_\infty$, are taken through the presentation (`exists_tendsto_smooth_degIndexWith`).

The text deduces "$C_xO$ is a partial quadrant" from the equality case of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31) (G.11; since proved without the equality, V2.33); here it is proved directly. The smooth vectors $\hat e_j = Dr(x)T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)$ satisfy $\lambda_{i_k}(\hat e_j) = \delta_{jk}$ by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35), and $v \mapsto ((\lambda_{i_j}v)_j, v - \sum_j \lambda_{i_j}(v)\hat e_j)$ is an sc-isomorphism $T_xO \cong \mathbb R^d \oplus T^R_xO$ carrying $C_xO$ onto $[0, \infty)^d \oplus T^R_xO$ (`splitIso`).

The text calls $T^R_xO$ a Banach space; it is proved to be an sc-subspace (the exposition's Lemma 3.A (1) in this case), which the sc-isomorphism needs: $Dr(x)T^{-1}(a, w')$, $w' \in W_\infty$, are smooth points of $T^R_xO$ converging to $u$ on level $m$. Both the sc-subspace property of $T^R_xO$ and the partial quadrant hold without tameness (V2.33); what tameness adds is that the quadrant has dimension $d_O(x) = d_C(x)$. Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 2.5.7 (preprint 2.37): tame M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.7 (preprint 2.37), p. 57 (preprint p. 42)
book.statement: A tame M-polyfold is an M-polyfold with an equivalent atlas whose charts are all modelled on tame sc-smooth retracts.

lean.statement: $X$ is tame if some atlas equivalent to its atlas consists of charts modelled on tame retracts; then every point lies in a chart of the structure with a tame model.

diff: As in the text.

items.title: Definition 2.5.10 (preprint 2.39): faces and face-structured M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.10 (preprint 2.39), p. 57 (preprint p. 43)
book.statement: A face of a tame M-polyfold is the closure of a connected component of $\{d_X = 1\}$; $X$ is face-structured if every $x$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces.

lean.statement: $F$ is a face of $X$ if $F = \overline{G}$ for the connected component $G$ in $\{d_X = 1\}$ of a point with $d_X = 1$; $X$ is face-structured if $\#\{F : F \text{ a face}, x \in F\} = d_X(x)$ for every $x$ (cardinality in $\mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$). Faces are closed and lie in $\partial X$.

diff: Defined for every M-polyfold; the theorems about faces assume tameness, as the text does.

items.title: The local geometry of faces (exposition Lemmas 4.A–4.C)

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), proof of Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40), p. 59 (preprint p. 43)
book.statement: \"There exists an index $i$ such that $\hat F$ must lie in $\{a_i = 0\}$\"; the retraction maps points near a face into the same face (\"using this argument repeatedly, we can connect any two points in $Q$\").

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$. (a) A preconnected subset of $\{z \in C : d_C(z) = 1\}$ meeting $f_i$ lies in $f_i$. (b) Rays stay in their face: for smooth $x \in O$, $i \in I(x)$ and $y$ with $\lambda_i(y) = 0$, $\lambda_l(y) > 0$ for the other $l \in I(x)$, for small $\tau > 0$, $I(x + \tau y) = \{i\}$ and $I(r(x + \tau y)) = \{i\}$. (c) Local structure: for $e \in f_i \cap O$ there are $\varepsilon > 0$ and a component $\hat F(e)$ of $S = \{z \in O : d_C(z) = 1\}$ in $f_i$ such that on $B = B_\varepsilon(e) \cap C$: $B \subseteq U$, $I(z), I(r(z)) \subseteq I(e)$, $r$ maps $\{z \in B : I(z) = \{i\}\}$ into $\hat F(e)$, and $f_i \cap B$ is mapped into $\overline{\hat F(e)}$.

chips: supplies the steps the text skips
diff: Not stated in the text; these are the exposition's Lemmas 4.A–4.C, which supply the step that the retraction maps points of $f_i$ near $f_i \cap O$ into $f_i$.
(b) needs tameness condition (2) through Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) ($\lambda_j \circ Dr(x) = \lambda_j$); condition (1) alone fixes only the number of vanishing coordinates.

items.title: Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40): faces of a tame retract

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40), p. 59 (preprint p. 43)
book.statement: For a tame retract $(O, C, E)$, the faces of $O$ are the connected components of the sets $f \cap O$, $f$ an extended face; the components of $f \cap O$ and $f' \cap O$ through $x$ agree iff $f = f'$.

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$, and call a face of the retract a set $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$, $\hat F$ a connected component of $S = \{z \in O : d_C(z) = 1\}$. Then $G$ is a face iff $G$ is the connected component of $f_i \cap O$ through some $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$. For $x \in O$ with $\lambda_i(x) = 0$, if the components of $f_i \cap O$ and $f_j \cap O$ through $x$ coincide then $i = j$. These are the faces of the M-polyfold $O$.

diff: Extended faces are the coordinate hyperplanes of a presentation; faces are handled in $E_0$ and transferred to the M-polyfold $O$ by `isFace_toMPolyfold_iff` (using $d_O = d_C$, V2.42).
The text's proof is a sketch; the formal proof follows the exposition (Lemma 4.C, V2.45).

items.title: Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41): a tame retract is face-structured

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41), p. 59 (preprint p. 44)
book.statement: If $(O, C, E)$ is a tame retract, every $x \in O$ lies in precisely $d_O(x)$ faces.

lean.statement: For a tame retract $O$ (nonempty), the M-polyfold $O$ is face-structured: every $x \in O$ lies in exactly $d_O(x)$ faces. In $E_0$: $x$ lies in exactly $d_C(x)$ faces of the retract.

diff: As in the text; the faces through $x$ are the components of $f_i \cap O$, $i \in I(x)$, distinct for distinct $i$ by Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40).

items.title: Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42): local face count in a tame M-polyfold

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42), p. 60 (preprint p. 44)
book.statement: In a tame M-polyfold every $x$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ such that each $y \in V$ lies in precisely $d_X(y)$ faces of $V$ and $d_V(y) = d_X(y)$; globally $x$ lies in at most $d_X(x)$ faces.

lean.statement: Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$. There is a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ around $x$ with tame model such that $d_X(y) = d_C(\varphi(y))$ and $d_O(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y)$ for all $y \in V$, and the M-polyfold $O$ is face-structured. Globally, $x$ lies in at most $d_X(x)$ faces of $X$.

diff: The neighbourhood $V$ is represented by the M-polyfold $O$ it is sc-diffeomorphic to through $\varphi$; its faces are those of $O$.
\"$d_V(y) = d_X(y)$\" uses that a tame chart realizes $d_X$ (V2.42), which the text does not say.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43): faces of a tame retract are tame sub-M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43), pp. 61–62 (preprint pp. 44–45)
book.statement: For a tame retraction $r$ onto $O$ and a face $F$ of $O$: there are an open neighbourhood $V^*$ of $F$ in $U$ and an sc-smooth retraction $s : V^* \to V^*$ onto $F$; $s$ restricted to $V = O \cap V^*$ makes $F$ a sub-M-polyfold of $O$. $F$ is tame and $d_F(x) = d_O(x) - 1$ for $x \in F$.

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$ and $F$ a face of the retract, $F \subseteq f_i$. (a) There is an sc-smooth retraction $S$ on $U^* \subseteq U$, relatively open in $C$ with $F \subseteq U^*$, with retract $F$ and $S = r \circ P_i$, $P_i$ the sc-projection onto $f_i$; every face of the M-polyfold $O$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$. (b) With the sc-operators $\iota : \mathbb R^k \oplus W \to f_i$ (insert a zero coordinate) and $\pi : E \to \mathbb R^k \oplus W$ (delete it), $r' = \pi \circ r \circ \iota$ on $\iota^{-1}(U^*)$ is a tame retraction of $[0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ onto $\pi(F)$, and $d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1 = d_C(y)$ on $F$. (c) A face $F$ of a tame retract $O$, with its sub-M-polyfold structure, is a tame M-polyfold and $d_F(x) + 1 = d_O(x)$ for $x \in F$.

diff: The text's model $(F, C \cap f_1, f_1)$ uses the sc-subspace $f_1$; here the extended face is modelled on $\mathbb R^k \oplus W$ through $\iota$, $\pi$, and the retraction is $\pi \circ r \circ \iota$ rather than $r|_{U^* \cap f_1}$ (they correspond under $\iota$). Tameness (2) of $r'$ is proved with the complement $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$, by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) for $r$, not by intersecting with $f_1$.

$U^*$ is the union of the balls $B_e$ intersected with their preimages under $P_i$, because $P_i$ need not be norm-decreasing for the norm of $E_0$ (the exposition's \"$|P_1z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0$\" is false in general).
\"$r(0, b_2, \dots, b_k, v)$ has the first coordinate vanishing\" is the local structure lemma (V2.45). $d_F = d_O - 1$ is stated as $d_F + 1 = d_O$; $F$ is paracompact because faces are closed.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44): local faces and their intersections are tame

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44), p. 62 (preprint p. 46)
book.statement: In a tame M-polyfold every point $x$ has $d_X(x)$ local faces containing $x$; they are tame M-polyfolds with $d_F(x) = d_X(x) - 1$. The intersection $F^\sigma$ of the local faces of $\sigma \subseteq \mathcal F_x$ is a tame M-polyfold of codimension $\#\sigma$ with $d_{F^\sigma}(x) = d_X(x) - \#\sigma$ (stated without proof).

lean.statement: Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$. There is a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ of the structure around $x$, with a tame retraction onto $O$, such that the point $\varphi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$, and every face $F$ of $O$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$ which, with its induced structure, is tame, with $d_F(\varphi(x)) + 1 = d_X(x)$ when $\varphi(x) \in F$. For every set $\sigma$ of face germs at $x$, i.e. $\sigma \subseteq I(\varphi(x))$, there are pairwise distinct faces $F_i \ni \varphi(x)$ of the retract ($i \in \sigma$, $F_i$ in the $i$-th coordinate hyperplane) and an open $B \ni \varphi(x)$ such that $A = \{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in B,\ \varphi(y) \in F_i\ \forall i \in \sigma\}$ (whose germ at $x$ is $F^\sigma_x$) is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$, tame with its induced structure, and $d_A(y) + \#\sigma = d_X(y)$ for all $y \in A$.

chips: face germs = faces of a tame chart
diff: "Local faces" are the faces of the M-polyfold $O$ of a tame chart, as in Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42); the face germs at $x$ are the faces $F_i$, $i \in I(\varphi(x))$, and "$F^\sigma_x$ is the germ of a sub-M-polyfold" is witnessed by the set $A$ itself. Face germs are not defined as germs.

"Codimension $\#\sigma$" is the number of quadrant coordinates removed in the tame model $\pi_\sigma(\varphi(A)) \subseteq [0, \infty)^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$; $d_A + \#\sigma = d_X$ holds on all of $A$, not only at $x$.

The text gives no proof; the exposition argues by induction on $\#\sigma$. The formal proof removes all coordinates of $\sigma$ at once: Lemma 4.C for each $i \in \sigma$ makes $r \circ P_\sigma$ a retraction onto $O \cap B \cap f_\sigma$ near $\varphi(x)$ (`corner_retraction`), with the tame model $\pi_\sigma \circ r \circ \iota_\sigma$ (`corner_tameModel`), as in Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43).

items.title: Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45): interiors of faces and faces of face-structured M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45), p. 62 (preprint p. 46)
book.statement: The interior of a face $F$ in a tame M-polyfold is an sc-smooth sub-M-polyfold of $X$. If $X$ is face-structured, every face is a sub-M-polyfold, its induced structure is tame, and $i : F \to X$ satisfies $d_X(i(x)) = d_F(x) + 1$. Every point has a neighbourhood $U$ in which each $y$ lies in exactly $d_X(y)$ faces of $U$; if $X$ is face-structured, each $x$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of $X$ (stated without proof).

lean.statement: Let $X$ be tame, $G$ the connected component of $\{d_X = 1\}$ through a point, $F = \overline G$. (a) $F \cap \{d_X = 1\} = G$ (the interior of the face), and $G$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$. (b) If $X$ is face-structured, every face $F$ agrees near each of its points, in a tame chart, with a face of the model retract; $F$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$, tame with its induced structure, and $d_X(x) = d_F(x) + 1$ for $x \in F$. A local criterion: $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold if near each point $\varphi(A)$ agrees on an open set with an sc-smooth retract contained in $O$. The face counts of the theorem are Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42) and the definition of face-structured.

diff: \"The interior of a face\" is not defined in the text; it is read as $F \cap \{d_X = 1\}$, which equals $G$.

The text has no proof. In the face-structured case, \"each global face through $x$ contains exactly one local face\" is a counting argument: the map from $I(\varphi x)$ to the faces through $x$ is onto (Lemma 4.C) and, by face-structuredness, injective.

The retraction near a point is $\varphi^{-1} \circ s \circ \varphi$ on $\varphi^{-1}(B \cap s^{-1}(B))$, shrunk so that $s$ maps it into itself; the exposition's \"transport by $\varphi^{-1}$\" omits this.

items.title: Products of M-polyfolds (exposition Lemma 4.D)

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), proof of Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46), preprint p. 47
book.statement: Used without statement in Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46): $X \times Y$ is an M-polyfold (with the product charts) and $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$.

lean.statement: For partial quadrants $C \subseteq E$, $C' \subseteq E'$, $C \times C'$ is a partial quadrant of $E \oplus E'$ with the product presentation $E \oplus E' \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'} \oplus (W \oplus W')$ and $d_{C \times C'}(x, x') = d_C(x) + d_{C'}(x')$; products of sc-smooth retractions are sc-smooth retractions, of tame ones tame. For M-polyfolds $X$, $Y$: $X \times Y$ is paracompact, and the product charts form an atlas of an M-polyfold structure on $X \times Y$; $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) \le d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$, with equality, and $X \times Y$ tame, if $X$ and $Y$ are tame. The projections are sc-smooth and the pairing of sc-smooth maps is sc-smooth.

diff: Not stated in the text; this is the exposition's Lemma 4.D. The text's \"$d_{X \times Y} = d_X + d_Y$\" is proved for tame $X$, $Y$; in general only the inequality, from the product charts.
Paracompactness of $X \times Y$ comes from Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) ($X$, $Y$ metrizable).

items.title: Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46): fibred products

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46), pp. 63–64 (preprint pp. 46–47)
book.statement: For a local sc-diffeomorphism $f : X \to Z$ and an sc-smooth $g : Y \to Z$, $X {}_f\times_g Y$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X \times Y$; if $Y$ is tame, so is the fibred product, with $d(x, y) = d_Y(y)$; with both maps local sc-diffeomorphisms and both spaces tame, $d = \frac12 d_{X \times Y} = d_X(x) = d_Y(y)$.

lean.statement: Let $f : X \to Z$ be a local sc-diffeomorphism (each point has an open neighbourhood mapped sc-diffeomorphically onto an open set) and $g : Y \to Z$ sc-smooth. The fibred product $\{(x, y) : f(x) = g(y)\}$ is closed in $X \times Y$, hence paracompact, and a sub-M-polyfold of $X \times Y$; $d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_Y(y)$; if $Y$ is tame, the fibred product is tame. If $g$ is also a local sc-diffeomorphism, $d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) = d_Y(y)$, and if moreover $X$ and $Y$ are tame, $2\,d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$.

diff: $d_{X {}_f\times_g Y} = d_Y \circ \pi_2$, and in the last statement $d = d_X = d_Y$, hold for arbitrary $X$, $Y$ (Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24) along $\pi_2$, $\pi_1$); tameness is used only for $d_{X \times Y} = d_X + d_Y$ (V2.52), stated as $2d = d_{X \times Y}$.

The inverse of $\pi_2$ near $(x, y)$ is $y' \mapsto ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')$; the exposition's factorization through $y' \mapsto (x, y')$ is not sc-smooth unless $x$ is a smooth point (Findings, Chapter 2, item 15).

The text's $\pi_2 : X {}_f\times_g Y \to X$ is read with target $Y$; paracompactness of the fibred product, which the text does not mention, comes from its being closed in the metrizable $X \times Y$.

items.title: Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47): $U \triangleleft F$, strong bundle maps and retractions

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47), p. 65 (preprint p. 48)
book.statement: $U \triangleleft F$ is $U \times F$ with the double filtration $U_m \oplus F_k$, $0 \le k \le m + 1$, and $(U \triangleleft F)[i]$ with levels $U_m \oplus F_{m+i}$. A strong bundle map $\Phi(u, h) = (\varphi(u), \Gamma(u, h))$, $\Gamma$ linear in $h$, preserves the double filtration and is sc-smooth $(U \triangleleft F)[i] \to (U' \triangleleft F')[i]$, $i = 0, 1$; a strong bundle retraction is one with $R \circ R = R$; $R(u, h) = (r(u), \Gamma(u, h))$ with $r$ an sc-smooth retraction.

lean.statement: $\Phi : E_0 \times F_0 \to E'_0 \times F'_0$ is a strong bundle map on $U \triangleleft F$ if it maps $U \times F$ into $U' \times F'$, its first component does not depend on $h$, its second is linear in $h$ for $u \in U$, it maps $U_m \oplus F_k$ into $U'_m \oplus F'_k$ for $k \le m + 1$, and it is sc-smooth on $U \times F_0$ for $E \oplus F$ and (through the lift of the fibre component to $F'_1$) on $U \times F_1$ for $E \oplus F^1$. A strong bundle retraction is one with $R \circ R = R$; its base $r(u) = R(u, 0)_1$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U$, $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ is a projection for $u \in O$, and $R$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $(U \triangleleft F)[0]$ and on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$. $C \times F$ is a partial quadrant in $E \oplus F$ and $U \times F$ is relatively open in it.

diff: Sc-smoothness on $[1]$ is that of the induced map $U \oplus F_1 \to U' \oplus F'_1$; \"preserves the double filtration\" is read level by level.

Updated (2026-11-09): strong bundle isomorphisms are the project's `IsStrongBundleIso`, which is the text's wording, an invertible strong bundle map with strong bundle inverse (`exists_isStrongBundleIso_iff`), closed under identity, inverse and composition (gap G.14 closed). The remarks after the definition ($r$ a retraction, $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ a projection) are the exposition's Lemma 5.A, proved here.

items.title: Definition 2.6.2 (preprint 2.48): local strong bundle retracts and $K[i]$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.2 (preprint 2.48) and the remarks after it, pp. 65–67 (preprint pp. 49–50)
book.statement: A local strong bundle retract is $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$ for a strong bundle retraction, $p : K \to O$; $K_{m,k} = \{(u, h) \in O_m \oplus F_k : \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$, $K[i] = K_{0,i}$ with the filtration $K_{m,m+i}$; the projections $p : K[i] \to O$ are sc-smooth.

lean.statement: $K \subseteq E_0 \times F_0$ is a local strong bundle retract over $C$ if $K = R(U \times F_0)$ for a strong bundle retraction on some relatively open $U \subseteq C$; then $K = \{(u, h) : u \in O, \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$. Its double filtration $K_{m,k}$ and $K[1] = \{(u, h) \in E_0 \times F_1 : (u, h) \in K\}$ are defined level by level. $K$ is an sc-smooth retract in $(C \times F, E \oplus F)$ and $K[1]$ one in $(C \times F, E \oplus F^1)$, $K[1]$ being the image of $R$ on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$; $p : K[i] \to O$ and the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ are sc-smooth.

diff: $K[1]$ is a subset of $(E \oplus F^1)_0 = E_0 \times F_1$. The text's \"$p$ is sc-smooth\" is proved, with \"sc-smooth bundle map\" read as sc-smooth.
That $K[1]$ is the image of $R$ on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$ uses that $R$ preserves the double filtration at $(m, k) = (0, 1)$ (exposition Lemma 5.B).

items.title: Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49): sections of a local strong bundle retract

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49), p. 66 (preprint p. 50)
book.statement: A section of $p : K \to O$ is $f : O \to K$ with $p \circ f = 1_O$; sc-smooth if it is sc-smooth into $K[0]$, sc⁺-smooth if sc-smooth into $K[1]$ (the text writes $K(0)$, $K(1)$); $f(x) = (x, \mathbf f(x))$ with the principal part $\mathbf f$.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth section is $f$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ on $O$ and $f$ sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to $(K, C \times F, E \oplus F)$; an sc⁺-section is $f : E_0 \to E_0 \times F_1$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ on $O$, sc-smooth into $(K[1], C \times F, E \oplus F^1)$. An sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section.

diff: The principal part is not named separately; an sc⁺-section takes its fibre values in $F_1$ by type.

Updated (2026-11-09): the category $\mathcal{SBR}$ is `SBR`, its morphisms the maps $K \to K'$ with an extension that is fibrewise linear, preserves the double filtration and is sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$; strong bundle maps are morphisms and strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms (`IsStrongBundleMap.isHom`, `IsStrongBundleIso.toIso`). The functors $\mathrm{forget}[i]$, $i = 0, 1$, land in the category `ScRetr` of sc-smooth retracts, the bundle retracts $\mathcal{BR}$ of §2.1 not being formalized (gap G.5) (gap G.14 closed).

items.title: Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50): strong bundle charts, compatibility, atlases

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50), pp. 67–68 (preprint pp. 51–52)
book.statement: For $P : Y \to X$ (Y paracompact Hausdorff, fibres Banachable), a strong bundle chart $(\Phi, P^{-1}(V), K, U \triangleleft F)$: $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$, $V$ open with a homeomorphism $\varphi : V \to O$, $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K$ a homeomorphism covering $\varphi$, bounded linear on fibres. Charts are compatible if $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[i]$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, $i = 0, 1$; atlases and their equivalence.

lean.statement: A strong bundle chart consists of a chart $\varphi$ *of the M-polyfold $X$*, an sc-Banach space $F$, a strong bundle retraction $R$ on a relatively open $U \subseteq C$ whose base retract is $O$, and a homeomorphism $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K = R(U \times F_0)$ with $\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))$, linear on each fibre $P^{-1}(x)$ (continuity on fibres follows). Two charts are compatible if $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ and $\Phi \circ \Phi'^{-1}$ are sc-smooth between the overlap retracts on $[0]$ and, through the lift to $F_1$, on $[1]$, and map fibre components in $F_1$ to fibre components in $F'_1$. Atlases: pairwise compatible charts covering $Y$; equivalence: the union is an atlas. Equivalence of strong bundle atlases is an equivalence relation, and two atlases are equivalent iff every chart of one is compatible with every chart of the other; this rests on the locality of compatibility. A strong bundle chart restricts to every open $s \subseteq V$ (retraction domain $U \cap r^{-1}(W)$ for $\varphi(s) = O \cap W$, $K_s = \{(u, h) \in K \mid u \in \varphi(s)\}$, $\Phi$ unchanged), and restrictions of compatible charts are compatible.

diff: The base homeomorphism $\varphi$ is required to be a chart of $X$; the text asks only for a homeomorphism onto $O$, under which the strong bundle atlas would define its own structure on $X$.
\"Bounded linear on the fibres\" needs only linearity: continuity follows from $\Phi$ being a homeomorphism (`continuous_fiber`).
For $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ to be defined, the transition must map fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$; the text takes this for granted, the definition states it.

The “equivalence class of strong bundle atlases” of Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) presupposes that the equivalence is transitive. It is: near a point of the overlap the transition $\Phi'' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ factors through a chart $\Phi'$ of the middle atlas, on $[0]$ and on $[1]$, and the $F_1$-condition passes through $\Phi'$; no continuity of $P$ is needed (Findings, Chapter 2, item 40). The restriction of a strong bundle chart to an open subset of the base, which the text uses silently (e.g. in Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2), V5.4), is formalized; a restriction whose retraction domain lies inside a given open $W \ni 0$ of $E$ is not, since $U \cap W$ need not be invariant under $r$ (item 42). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51): strong bundles; $Y[0]$, $Y[1]$, $P[0]$, $P[1]$ and $Y_{m,k}$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) and the remarks after it, preprint p. 52
book.statement: A strong bundle over $X$ is $P : Y \to X$ (continuous surjection, $Y$ paracompact Hausdorff) with an equivalence class of strong bundle atlases. The charts induce a double filtration $Y_{m,k}$ and M-polyfolds $Y[i]$, $Y[i]_m = Y_{m,m+i}$; $P[i] : Y[i] \to X$ are sc-smooth.

lean.statement: A strong bundle is a continuous surjection $P : Y \to X$ ($Y$ Hausdorff paracompact) with Banachable fibres and a strong bundle atlas. The charts $\Phi$ form an sc-smooth atlas of $Y$, making it the M-polyfold $Y[0]$, and $P[0] : Y[0] \to X$ is sc-smooth. $Y_{m,k}$ ($k \le m + 1$) is defined by $\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k$ in all charts around $y$, and one chart suffices. $Y[1]$ is the set $Y_{0,1}$ with the topology generated by the charts $\Phi[1] : y \mapsto (\Phi(y)_1, \Phi(y)_2$ lifted to $F_1)$; these charts, onto the retracts $K[1]$, are pairwise compatible, their transition maps being the $[1]$-transitions, and make $Y[1]$ an M-polyfold; $P[1] : Y[1] \to X$ is sc-smooth. The charts of the strong bundle (`StrongBundle.IsChart`: compatible with the atlas) are those of the maximal atlas, which is equivalent to the given one: a chart is one iff it belongs to some atlas of the class, any two are compatible, restrictions of charts are charts, and equivalent atlases have the same charts.

chips: charts depend only on the class
diff: $Y[0]$ (the text's "the M-polyfold $Y$") and $Y[1]$ are constructed with the charts induced by the given atlas; the equivalence class of atlases is represented by one atlas, as for M-polyfolds. The notions defined through the charts compatible with the atlas therefore depend only on the class (`isChart_congr`, `isChart_iff_exists_equiv`; Findings, Chapter 2, item 43); those defined with the charts of the given atlas itself ($Y_{m,k}$, $Y[1]$ and its atlas, sc$^+$-sections) are not shown invariant. Updated in the third addendum of this page.

$Y[1]$ is the subset $Y_{0,1}$ with the topology generated by the sets $\Phi[1]^{-1}(W)$, as for $X_m$ in §2.3 (preprint §2.2); its paracompactness, required of an M-polyfold and not mentioned in the text, follows from metrizability (V2.64).

Chart independence of $Y_{m,k}$: for $k \le m$ it follows from the $[0]$-transition; for $k = m + 1$, and for the set $Y_{0,1}$ itself, it uses the condition that the $[1]$-transition carries fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$, made explicit in Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) (V2.57).

items.title: Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52): sections of a strong bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52), p. 68 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: A section is $f : X \to Y$ with $P \circ f = 1_X$; sc-smooth if sc-smooth into $Y[0]$, sc⁺ if sc-smooth into $Y[1]$.

lean.statement: A section is $f$ with $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$; it is sc-smooth if it is sc-smooth $X \to Y[0]$ (Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14)); it is an sc⁺-section if in every strong bundle chart of the atlas its fibre values lie in $F_1$ and its representative $z \mapsto \Phi(f(\varphi^{-1}(z)))$, lifted to $E_0 \times F_1$, is sc-smooth from $O$ into $K[1]$. This holds iff $f$ is a section and $f = \iota \circ g$ for an sc-smooth $g : X \to Y[1]$, $\iota : Y[1] \to Y$ the inclusion.

chips: sc⁺ chart by chart = sc-smooth into $Y[1]$
diff: Sc⁺-sections are defined chart by chart through $\Phi[1]$; `isScPlusSection_iff` proves that this is the text's "sc-smooth as a map into $Y[1]$", the section being a map into the type $Y[1]$ followed by the inclusion.

items.title: Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53): the pull-back bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53), p. 69 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: For a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and an sc-smooth $f : Z \to X$, $f^*Y = \{(z, y) : P(y) = f(z)\}$, $P_f(z, y) = z$, $P'(z, y) = y$, and $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$.

lean.statement: $f^*Y = \{(z, y) \in Z \times Y : P(y) = f(z)\}$ with $P_f$, $P'$ the projections; $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$; $P_f$ is continuous, and $f^*Y$ is closed in $Z \times Y$ when $X$ is Hausdorff and $P$, $f$ are continuous.

diff: As in the text, for any maps $P$, $f$.

items.title: Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54): the pull-back of a strong bundle is a strong bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), p. 69 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: $P_f : f^*Y \to Z$ carries a natural structure of a strong bundle over $Z$ (\"the easy proof is left to the reader\").

lean.statement: For a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and an sc-smooth $f : Z \to X$: $f^*Y$ is paracompact (it is metrizable, $Z$ and $Y[0]$ being metrizable by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16)), $P_f$ is a continuous surjection, its fibres $P_f^{-1}(z) \cong P^{-1}(f(z))$ are Banachable, and the pulled-back charts $\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))$, with the strong bundle retractions $R_g(w, h) = (r_Z(w), \Gamma(g(r_Z(w)), h))$, $g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}$, form a strong bundle atlas; so $P_f$ is a strong bundle with this atlas. Locally: $R_g$ is a strong bundle retraction with image $\{(w, h) : w \in O_Z, (g(w), h) \in K\}$; the transition maps of pulled-back charts are $(w, h) \mapsto (\psi_2\psi_1^{-1}(w), \mathrm{pr}_F(\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1})(g_1(w), h))$, sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$.

diff: \"Natural structure\" is the atlas of all pulled-back charts; any two are compatible, so it involves no choice.
The paracompactness of $f^*Y$, required by Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) and not mentioned in the text, is proved from Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) for $Z$ and $Y[0]$.

“Natural” presumably also says that $P' : f^*Y \to Y$ is a strong bundle map (sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$); that is not formalized. In the charts $\Phi_f$, $\Phi$ it is $(w, h) \mapsto (g(w), h)$ on $K_g$ (Findings, Chapter 2, item 51; round-trip item V2.61). Recorded in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55): Smirnov's metrization theorem

book.label: §2.7.2 (preprint §2.6.2), Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55), p. 72 (preprint p. 56)
book.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space in which every point has a metrizable open neighbourhood is metrizable (quoted from Smirnov).

lean.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space in which every point has a metrizable open neighbourhood is metrizable. More generally: a space $Y$ with open metrizable $V_i$ and a locally finite family of continuous $\rho_i \ge 0$, $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i \subseteq V_i$, not all zero at any point, is metrizable, with the metric $\sum_i |\rho_i(x) - \rho_i(y)| + \min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(y)) \min(d_i(x, y), 1)$; and if $\pi : Y \to X$ is continuous into a paracompact Hausdorff $X$ and every point of $X$ has an open $U$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)$ metrizable, $Y$ is metrizable. Metrizable spaces are paracompact (Stone, from Mathlib).

diff: Quoted in the text; proved here (Mathlib does not have it), in the stronger pull-back form that Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) and Proposition 2.3.15(3) (preprint 2.19) use.

items.title: Restriction and locality of sc$^k$ maps

book.label: §§2.1, 2.3 (preprint §2.1–§2.2), used in Propositions 2.1.11, 2.3.1 (preprint 2.4, 2.10) and Definitions 2.3.4–2.3.8 (preprint 2.13–2.14), preprint p. 19
book.statement: Used without statement: an sc-smooth map restricted to a smaller relatively open set is sc-smooth (e.g. \"$r : U \to U \cap U'$ is sc-smooth\"), and sc-smoothness is a local property.

lean.statement: On sc-domains: an $\mathrm{sc}^k$ (sc-smooth) map on $U$ is $\mathrm{sc}^k$ (sc-smooth) on every smaller sc-domain $U'$, with the same tangent map on $TU'$; a map that is $\mathrm{sc}^1$, $\mathrm{sc}^k$ or sc-smooth on $U \cap W$ for an open $W$ around each point of $U$ is so on $U$; sc-smoothness depends only on the values on $U$.

diff: Not stated in the text. The restriction needs the uniqueness of derivatives on the smaller domain, because the tangent map is built from a chosen derivative; the locality glues the local derivatives into one family.

items.title: The space $Y[1]$ and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), after Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51), p. 68 (preprint p. 52)
book.statement: Not stated: the text takes $Y[1]$ to be an M-polyfold on the set $Y_{0,1}$ without discussing its topology, its paracompactness or its inclusion into $Y[0]$.

lean.statement: $Y_{0,1}$ is the set of points whose fibre component lies in $F_1$ in one, equivalently every, chart of the atlas around them. With the topology generated by the charts $\Phi[1]$, the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y$ is continuous, so $Y[1]$ is Hausdorff; $Y[1]$ is metrizable, hence paracompact; and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is sc-smooth (in the charts it is $(u, h) \mapsto (u, \iota h)$).

diff: Not stated in the text. Paracompactness is needed for $Y[1]$ to be an M-polyfold (Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13)); it follows, as in Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16), from the pull-back form of Smirnov's theorem over the paracompact base (V2.62).
The sc-smooth inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is the global form of $K[1] \to K[0]$ (V2.55).

items.title: Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), the 2021 statement

book.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), p. 27 (preprint p. 20)
book.statement: For sc-smooth retractions $r$, $s$ onto $O$ and $f : O \to O'$: (1) $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth iff $f \circ s$ is; (2) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on $TO$; (3) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r)$ maps $TO$ into $TO'$. The hypothesis of (3) is new in the 2021 statement.

lean.statement: For retractions $r$, $s$ onto the same $O$, a retraction $\rho$ onto $O'$ and $f(O) \subseteq O'$: (1) $f \circ r$ sc-smooth iff $f \circ s$ sc-smooth; (2) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on $Tr(TU)$; (3) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r)$ maps $Tr(TU)$ into $T\rho(TU')$.

diff: The Lean statement of (3) in V2.5 already assumed $f \circ r$ sc-smooth; the 2021 text now states it.

items.title: Proposition 2.1.4: complete closed neighbourhoods in a retract

book.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.4, p. 22 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: With $d_O(x, y) = |x - y|_0$, every $x$ in an sc-smooth retract $O$ has open neighbourhoods $W(x)$, $V(x)$ with $\mathrm{cl}_O(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$ and $d_O$ complete on $\mathrm{cl}_O(V(x))$.

lean.statement: Every $x \in O$ has open $V \subseteq W$ in $O$ with $\mathrm{cl}_O(V) \subseteq W$ and $\mathrm{cl}_O(V)$ complete for the metric of $E_0$, with $W$ inside any given neighbourhood of $x$; $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ is closed in $E_0$ for small $\varepsilon$.

diff: The proof uses $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ in place of the text's set $V'$ with $r(V') \subseteq V'$.

items.title: Definition 2.1.5: locally complete spaces

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.5, p. 23 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: A Hausdorff space $X$ is locally complete if every $x$ has open neighbourhoods $W(x)$, $V(x)$ such that $W(x)$ carries a metric inducing its topology, $V(x) \subseteq W(x)$, $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$, and $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ is complete for that metric.

lean.statement: Every $x$ has open $V \ni x$ and $W$ with $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ and a metric on $W$ inducing its subspace topology for which $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ is complete. Such a space is regular, $T_1$ and Hausdorff, and $W$ can be chosen inside any neighbourhood of $x$; complete metric spaces, $\mathbb R$ in particular, are locally complete.

diff: The Hausdorff assumption is not part of the definition: it follows ($T_1$ from the metrizable $W$, regularity from $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$). So Proposition 2.1.8, Lemma 2.1.9 and Proposition 2.1.10 need no Hausdorff hypothesis (except for the $T_{3\frac12}$ conclusion).

items.title: Remark 2.1.6: the modified definition is weaker

book.label: §2.1, Remark 2.1.6, p. 23 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: The condition $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$ is global; replacing $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ by the closure $\mathrm{cl}_{W(x)}(V(x))$ gives a weaker notion, since $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ implies $\mathrm{cl}_W(V) = \mathrm{cl}_X(V)$.

lean.statement: `remark_2_1_6_book`: if $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ then $\mathrm{cl}_W(V) = \mathrm{cl}_X(V)$. Local completeness implies the modified notion ($V \subseteq W$, $\mathrm{cl}_W(V)$ complete). Some Hausdorff space ($\mathbb R$ with the K-topology, V2.91) satisfies the modified notion without being locally complete, so the modified notion is strictly weaker.

diff: The text does not say whether "weaker" is meant strictly; both the implication and the strictness are proved, in one statement (`Chapter2/BookFormLocalCompleteness2021.lean`); the example is V2.91 (gap G.76, closed) (Findings, Chapter 2, items 61, 75, 89).

items.title: Corollary 2.1.7: retracts are locally complete

book.label: §2.1, Corollary 2.1.7, p. 23 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: An sc-smooth retract $O$ is locally complete.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth retract $O$ with the topology of $E_0$ is locally complete; so is $E_0$.

items.title: Proposition 2.1.8: permanence of local completeness

book.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.8, p. 24 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: For a Hausdorff locally complete $X$: (1) locally closed subspaces, (2) homeomorphic spaces, (3) open subsets are locally complete; a Hausdorff $Y$ with an open cover $(Y_i)$ by locally complete subspaces such that every $z \in Y_i$ has an open neighbourhood in $Y_i$ whose closure in $Y$ lies in $Y_i$ is locally complete.

items.title: Lemma 2.1.9 and Proposition 2.1.10: first countable, completely regular

book.statement: Points of a locally complete space have countable neighbourhood bases. A Hausdorff locally complete space is completely regular.

items.title: Lemma 2.2.1: the levels of a connected relatively open set are path-connected

book.label: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.1, p. 30 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: If $U \subseteq C$ is relatively open and connected, then for every $k \in \mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$ the level $U_k$ with the $E_k$-topology is path-connected.

lean.statement: For $k \in \mathbb N$, $U_k \subseteq E_k$ is path-connected; $U_\infty$, as the compatible sequences $(v_m) \in \prod_m E_m$ with $v_0 \in U$ (the topology of all the norms), is path-connected. Smooth points are dense in every $C_m$.

items.title: Lemma 2.2.2, Definition 2.2.3, Theorem 2.2.4: retracts are locally path-connected

book.label: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.2, p. 31, Definition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4, p. 32 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: For a retraction $r$ onto $O$, $x \in O$ and an open $V(x)$, $W(x) = V(x) \cap r^{-1}(V(x))$ is relatively open in $C$ with $W(x) \cap O = V(x) \cap O$, $r(W(x)) \subseteq W(x)$, $r(W(x)) = O \cap V(x)$. Locally path-connected: every open neighbourhood contains a path-connected open one. A retract is locally path-connected.

items.title: Definition 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.6: almost local contractibility

book.label: §2.2, Definition 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.6, p. 33 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: $Z$ is almost locally contractible if every $z$ and open $V(z)$ admit an open $W(z) \subseteq V(z)$ and a continuous $\Phi : [0, 1] \times W(z) \to V(z)$ with $\Phi(0, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$, $\Phi(t, z) = z$, $\Phi(1, W(z)) = \{z\}$. A retract is almost locally contractible.

lean.statement: The same definition; sc-smooth retracts and $E_0$ are almost locally contractible.

items.title: Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13), the footnote: paracompactness without Hausdorff

items.title: Definitions 2.5.18 and 2.5.19: tame sub-M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5, Definition 2.5.18, p. 62, and Definition 2.5.19, p. 63 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: The structure induced on a sub-M-polyfold $Y$ is tame if it has an equivalent atlas with tame local models. For a tame $X$, $Y$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold if every $y \in Y$ has an open $V$ and an sc-smooth retraction $r : V \to V$ with (1) $r(V) = Y \cap V$, (2) $d_X \circ r = d_X$ on $V$, (3) at smooth $y \in Y \cap V$ an sc-subspace $A \subseteq T^R_yX$ with $T_yX = T_yY \oplus A$.

lean.statement: `definition_2_5_19_book`: for a sub-M-polyfold $Y$, condition (3) is stated in $T_yX$. $T_yY$ is the image of $Ti : T_yY \to T_yX$ (`subTangentRange`), $T^R_yX$ is the reduced tangent space of Definition 2.5.8, and $T_yX = Ti(T_yY) \oplus A$ is an algebraic splitting with $A \subseteq T^R_yX$, $A$ an sc-subspace with a levelwise splitting in a chart (`HasReducedScComplement`, `TameSubData2021`, `IsTameSubMPolyfold2021`). It is equivalent to the chart form `IsTameSubMPolyfold` (`isTameSubMPolyfold2021_iff`, `hasReducedScComplement_iff`), through `coe_map_range_subInclusionCLM`: $T\varphi(y)$ maps $Ti(T_yY)$ onto the tangent space of $\varphi(W \cap Y)$, and through `fiberCoord_subInclusionCLM`, $T\varphi(y) \circ Ti = T\sigma(y)$ for the sub-chart $\sigma$. It implies the tame induced structure of Definition 2.5.18, and $Y = X$ satisfies it. The chart form, first stated: (3) in some chart around $y$, the tangent space of the chart image of $Y$ having an sc-complement in $T_zO$ inside $T_zO \cap E_z$; a tame sub-M-polyfold is a sub-M-polyfold; $Y = X$ is one, with tame induced structure.

diff: The sc-structure of $T_yX$ at a smooth point is carried by a chart, as in Definition 2.3.14 (V2.19), and is the same through every chart; so "$A$ is an sc-subspace and the sum is sc" is read in the chart that also defines $T^R_yX$, which does not depend on the chart (`reducedTangentFiber_eq`). The chart form first stated is chart independent (V2.99), a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame (V2.100), and the examples in $[0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R$ are V2.101 (gap G.77, closed). Updated (2026-11-09): (3) is restated in $T_yX$ with the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14 (gap G.7 closed, V2.19) (Findings, Chapter 2, items 72, 87, 88).

items.title: Faces of open sets and the corner axioms

book.label: no counterpart in the text (§2.7.4, pp. 78–82, new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: Not stated. §2.7.4 uses the faces of open subsets $V$ of a tame $X$ and the local structure of tame charts.

lean.statement: For $d : X \to \mathbb N$ and an open $V$, a face of $V$ is the closure in $V$ of a component of $V \cap \{d = 1\}$. The corner axioms: $d$ upper semicontinuous, and near every point $d(y)$ separated preconnected pieces of $\{d = 1\}$ accumulating at $y$. A face of $U \subseteq V$ lies in a unique face of $V$. The degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold, and $d \equiv 0$, satisfy the axioms.

items.title: Proposition 2.7.5: face-structured neighbourhoods

book.label: §2.7.4, Proposition 2.7.5, p. 78 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: In a tame $X$ every $x$ has an open $V$ with $d_X \le d_X(x)$ on $V$, every $y \in V$ in exactly $d_X(y)$ faces of $V$, and an open $U(x) \subseteq V$ such that a face of $V$ meeting $U(x)$ contains $x$.

lean.statement: The same, for every $d$ with the corner axioms; the last property for every open $V \ni x$.

items.title: Definition 2.7.6 and Proposition 2.7.7: the families $N_X$, $N_{X,x}$

book.label: §2.7.4, Definition 2.7.6, p. 79, and Proposition 2.7.7, p. 80 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: An open $V$ is face-structured if every $y \in V$ lies in exactly $d_X(y)$ faces of $V$; $N_X$: the nonempty ones with $d_X|V$ bounded; $N_{X,x}$: those containing $x$ with $d_X \le d_X(x)$. $N_{X,x} \ne \emptyset$; nonempty open subsets and nonempty intersections of members of $N_X$ are in $N_X$; $N_{X,x}$ is closed under intersections.

lean.statement: The same, with $N_X = \bigcup_x N_{X,x}$; every open subset of $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ is face-structured.

items.title: Definitions 2.7.8 and 2.7.9: the category $L_X$ and the functor $F_X$

book.label: §2.7.4, Definition 2.7.8, p. 80, and Definition 2.7.9, p. 81 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: Objects $(x, V)$, $x \in \partial X$, $V \in N_{X,x}$; one morphism $(x, V) \to (y, W)$ iff $V \subseteq W$, $x$ lies in $d_X(x)$ faces of $W$ and all contain $y$. $F_X(x, V)$ is the set of faces of $V$ through $x$, and a morphism sends $\theta$ to the face $\theta'$ of $W$ through $x$ and $y$ with $\theta \cap \theta'$ open in $\theta$, an injection (2.43).

lean.statement: The same, $L_X$ as a preorder (thin category), $F_X$ into types, $\theta'$ the union of the faces of $W$ containing $\theta$; morphisms compose, $F_X(\varphi)$ is injective, and bijective over a fixed point.

items.title: Definition 2.7.10: the set $bX$ and the map $B$

book.label: §2.7.4, Definition 2.7.10, p. 81 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: Admissible triples $(x, V, \theta)$, $\theta$ a face of $V \in N_{X,x}$ through $x$; $(x, V, \theta) \sim (x, V', \theta')$ if a smaller $V'' \in N_{X,x}$ has a face sent to $\theta$ and $\theta'$; $bX$ is the set of classes and $B[x, V, \theta] = x$.

lean.statement: The same; $\sim$ is an equivalence relation, $B$ has image $\partial X$, and $B^{-1}(x)$ has exactly $d_X(x)$ points.

items.title: Definition 2.7.11 and (2.44): the sets $U(x, V, \theta)$ and the maps $\Phi$

book.label: §2.7.4, Definition 2.7.11 and (2.44), p. 82 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: $U(x, V, \theta)$: the classes $[y, V', \theta']$ with $y \in \theta$ and a morphism $(y, V') \to (x, V)$ sending $\theta'$ to $\theta$. The canonical bijection $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)} : U(x, V, \theta) \to \theta$, $[y, V', \theta'] \mapsto y$ (2.44).

items.title: Definition 3.1.3 (preprint 3.3): sc-smooth section germs

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.3 (preprint 3.3), p. 91 (preprint p. 63)
book.statement: An sc-smooth section germ $(f, x_0)$ of $P : Y \to X$ is a continuous section $f : V \to P^{-1}(V)$ near the smooth point $x_0$ such that in a strong bundle chart with $\varphi(x_0) = 0$ the principal part $\mathbf f$ of $\Phi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1} : O \to K$ has $\mathbf f \circ r : \mathcal O(C, 0) \to F$ an sc-smooth germ.

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSectionGerm f x₀`: $x_0$ smooth, and for some strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas (`StrongBundle.IsChart`) with $\varphi(x_0) = 0$, $\mathbf f \circ r$ is an sc-smooth germ on some sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$ with $G_0 \subseteq U$, whose levels may shrink with $m$ (the text’s germ reading). An sc-smooth section is an sc-smooth section germ at every smooth point with a centred chart (with the germ $U \cap E_m$).

diff: \"A strong bundle chart\" is read as a chart compatible with the atlas, not a member of it: a chart of the atlas need not be centred at $x_0$, and the notion must not depend on the atlas within its class (Findings, Chapter 3, item 41). That it does not is proved: equivalent atlases have the same compatible charts (`isChart_congr`; V2.58, Findings, Chapter 2, item 43). Updated in the third addendum of this page.
Continuity of $f$ near $x_0$ is not a separate field: it follows near $x_0$ from the continuity of $\mathbf f \circ r$ on level $0$ of the germ.

**Germs.** Since the fourth addendum of this page the definition is in the text’s germ reading: $\mathbf f \circ r$ is an sc-smooth germ on some sc-germ of neighbourhoods inside $U$, whose levels may shrink with $m$, as for Definitions 3.1.4, 3.1.6 and 3.1.11 (preprint 3.4, 3.6 and 3.11) since phase 2. Before, it was required on the whole $U$ of the chart (levels $U \cap E_m$), which is stricter: a function $C^k$ on $(-1/k, 1/k)$ for every $k$ is an sc-smooth germ in the constant scale $\mathbb R$ and sc-smooth on no neighbourhood of $0$ (`exists_isScSmoothGerm_not_isScSmooth`). No theorem assumes the definition. Hence “hypotheses explicit” again (“narrower” from the third addendum until the fourth) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 260; round-trip item V3.5).

items.title: The section algebra and the sum rule

book.label: §3.1, used in Theorems 3.1.13, 3.1.18 (preprint 3.12, 3.15) ("$f + s$ is an sc-smooth section"), p. 98 (preprint p. 71)
book.statement: Not stated: the fibrewise sum of sections, principal parts in a chart, the sum rule of the sc-calculus, and the sc-smoothness of the local representatives of sc$^+$-sections in a chart that is not in the atlas.

lean.statement: The fibrewise sum $f + s$ is a section with principal part $\mathbf f + \mathbf s$ in every chart; $f(x) = 0$ iff $\mathbf f(\varphi(x)) = 0$; the fibres of $K$ are linear. Sums, differences and negatives of sc-smooth maps on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants are sc-smooth. In every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas, $z \mapsto (z, \mathbf f(z))$ is sc-smooth $O \to K$ for an sc-smooth section and $z \mapsto (z, \mathbf s_1(z))$ is sc-smooth $O \to K[1]$ for an sc$^+$-section.

diff: For an sc$^+$-section in a chart outside the atlas the sc-smoothness of the representative is the change of chart $(\Phi \circ \Phi'^{-1})[1]$, i.e. the compatibility on $[1]$ of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50); this is its first use (Findings, Chapter 3, item 41).
The sum rule is pairing followed by the sc-operator $F \oplus F \to F$.

items.title: Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4): fillers

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4), p. 91 (preprint p. 64)
book.statement: For a tame strong local bundle $K = R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$, $R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)$, $r(0) = 0$, an sc-smooth section germ $(f, 0)$ has a filling $(g, 0)$ (an sc-smooth section germ of $U \triangleleft F \to U$) if (1) $f = g$ on $O$ near $0$; (2) $g(y) = \rho(r(y))g(y)$ for $y \in U$ near $0$ forces $y \in O$; (3) the linearization of $y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ at $0$, restricted to $\ker Dr(0)$, is a topological isomorphism onto $\ker\rho(0)$.

lean.statement: `IsFillingGerm` for the principal parts $f, g : E_0 \to F_0$ (the text’s germ reading, also Definition 3.1.6 (preprint 3.6), V3.9): $g$ is an sc-smooth germ on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$ with $G_0 \subseteq U$; (1) and (2) near $0$; (3) the map $y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ (`fillDefect`) is an sc$^1$-germ on $G$ with a derivative family $Dk$, and $Dk(0)$ induces a continuous linear equivalence $\ker Dr(0) \simeq \ker\rho(0)$. Here $r(u) = (R(u, 0))_1$, $\rho(u)h = (R(u, h))_2$, with $R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)$, $r \circ r = r$, $\rho(x)$ a projection for $x \in O$, and $\rho(u)$ a bounded operator. The whole-chart form `IsFillerOf` asks the map in (3) to be sc$^1$ on all of $U$ and says nothing about the regularity of $g$.

chips: sc¹ of the map in (3) required
diff: Condition (3) presupposes that $y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ is differentiable at $0$; it is required to be an sc$^1$-germ with a derivative family, which holds for every sc-smooth germ $g$ (`fillDefect_isScSmoothGerm`); the value of the family at $0$ is unique (Findings, Chapter 3, items 261, 272).
The sc-smoothness of $g$ is part of the filling, as in the text (“$(g, 0)$ an sc-smooth section germ”); tameness of the retraction is not used.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) $g$ and the map in (3) are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (`IsFillingGerm`); the stricter whole-chart filler (`IsFillerOf`, with $g$ sc-smooth on all of $U$ added in `IsFilledVersion`) is kept for the `…WholeChart` notions. Hence “hypotheses explicit” again (“narrower” in the third addendum) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 261, 330; round-trip items V3.7, V3.19). On the text’s domain of definition, tame strong local bundles, it is not broader: tameness is simply not used.

items.title: Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5): the filler and the linearization

book.label: §3.1, the paragraph after Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) and Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5), pp. 91–93 (preprint pp. 64–65)
book.statement: If $f$ has the filling $g$ and $f(0) = 0$, then in the splittings $E = Dr(0)E \oplus \ker Dr(0)$, $F = \rho(0)F \oplus \ker\rho(0)$, $Dg(0) = \begin{pmatrix} Tf(0) & * \\ 0 & C \end{pmatrix}$ with $C$ an isomorphism, and (1) $Tf(0) : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is onto iff $Dg(0)$ is; (2) $Tf(0)$ is Fredholm iff $Dg(0)$ is, with equal index.

lean.statement: For a filler $g$ of $f$ with $g$ sc-smooth, $g(0) = 0$ and $f$ a section of $K \to O$: $D(\rho(r(\cdot))g)(0) = \rho(0)Dg(0)$, $(1 - \rho(0))Dg(0)Dr(0) = 0$, $D(f \circ r)(0) = Dg(0)Dr(0)$; and $Tf(0) := Dg(0)|_{Dr(0)E} : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is onto iff $Dg(0)$ is, Fredholm iff $Dg(0)$ is, and $\mathrm{ind}\,Tf(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0)$. The linear algebra holds for any idempotents $p, q$ and $L$ with $(1 - q)Lp = 0$ and $(1 - q)L : \ker p \to \ker q$ a topological isomorphism. In sc form: if $Dg(0)$ is an sc-Fredholm sc-operator, then $Dr(0)E$, $\rho(0)F$, $\ker Dr(0)$ and $\ker\rho(0)$ are sc-subspaces, $Tf(0) : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0)$ on every level, and $(1 - \rho(0))Dg(0) : \ker Dr(0) \to \ker\rho(0)$ is an sc-isomorphism (condition (3) of the filler on every level). Conversely, for $Dg(0)$ an sc-operator: $Dg(0)$ is sc-Fredholm if and only if $Tf(0)$ is sc-Fredholm and condition (3) holds on every level. The same for a filling germ (V3.7), with $Dg(0)$ the value at $0$ of any derivative family of $g$ on any germ (`IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5`, `IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5_sc`, `IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5_sc_iff`).

chips: sc form: filler (3) on level 0 suffices
sc converse needs (3) on every level
diff: The proof exhibits $\ker Tf(0) \simeq \ker Dg(0)$ and $\mathrm{coker}\,Tf(0) \simeq \mathrm{coker}\,Dg(0)$ directly instead of the text's factorization and additivity of the index, so the index equality holds as $\dim\ker - \dim\mathrm{coker}$ with no finiteness assumption; closedness of the ranges transfers through the continuous $y \mapsto y - LC^{-1}(1 - q)y$, which is where \"topological\" in (3) is used.
The text's \"by linearization at $y = 0$\" needs $(u, h) \mapsto \rho(u)h$ differentiable and $g(0) = 0$; the target \"$(1 - D\rho(0))F$\" is $(1 - \rho(0))F$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 47).

Proposition 3.1.5 (2) (preprint 3.5) is a level-$0$ statement. Its sc form in the direction Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) uses (“$Dg(0)$ sc-Fredholm ⟹ $Tf(0)$ sc-Fredholm”) needs condition (3) of the filler on level $0$ only, as the text states it: the higher levels of $Tf(0)$ come from the regularity of $Dg(0)$ (`IsScFredholm.restrict`), and condition (3) on every level then follows at the zero. The converse in sc form needs condition (3) on every level as a hypothesis; with level $0$ only it fails (an example on a weighted $\ell^2$ with the shift, Findings, Chapter 3, item 238, not formalized). Nothing in the text uses the converse (Findings, Chapter 3, items 234, 237, 238). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

For filling germs (the text’s reading of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4)) the proofs are the same, with the derivative family of the fill defect in place of the derivative on $U$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 272, 289, 314). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Definition 3.1.6 (preprint 3.6): filled versions

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.6 (preprint 3.6), p. 93 (preprint p. 66)
book.statement: $(f, x_0)$ has a filling if in a strong bundle chart with $\varphi(x_0) = 0$ the section germ $\Phi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1} : O \to K$ has a filling $g : U \to U \triangleleft F$ near $0$; $(g, 0)$ is a filled version.

lean.statement: `IsFillingGerm fb g` (V3.7): $g$ is an sc-smooth germ on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$, $G_0 \subseteq U$, whose levels may shrink with $m$, and fills the principal part $\mathbf f$ near $0$; the centred chart is that of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (V3.13). The whole-chart form `IsFilledVersion` ($g$ sc-smooth on all of $U$, filling in the sense of `IsFillerOf`) is a filling (`IsFilledVersion.isFillingGerm`), and a filling sc-smooth on all of $U$ is a filled version (`IsFillingGerm.isFilledVersion`).

chips: local data; the chart in Def. 3.1.11
diff: The text asks for a filling of the section germ in some strong bundle chart centred at $x_0$; the formal notion is the datum in a given chart, for the principal parts, and the centred chart is quantified in Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (V3.13).

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the filling is a germ (`IsFillingGerm`). The earlier filled version, sc-smooth on all of $U$, is stricter (round-trip items V3.9, V3.43) and is kept as `IsFilledVersion`, exactly the fillings sc-smooth on $U$. Hence “restated” again (“narrower” in the third addendum) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 260–262, 330).

items.title: Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7): basic germs

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7), p. 94 (preprint p. 66)
book.statement: A basic germ is an sc-smooth germ $f : \mathcal O([0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k} \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$ with $f(0) = 0$ and $P_W \circ f(a, w) = w - B(a, w)$, $B(0, 0) = 0$, $|B(a, w) - B(a, w')|_m \le \varepsilon|w - w'|_m$ for $(a, w), (a, w')$ close enough to $(0, 0)$ on level $m$, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $m \ge 0$.

lean.statement: `IsBasicGerm C̃ G f B`: $f$ an sc-smooth germ on the germ $G$ around $0$ in $\widetilde C \oplus W$ with $f(0) = 0$, whose $W$-component is $w - B(a, w)$ on $U_0$, with $B$ an sc$^0$-contraction germ (V3.25: $B$ sc$^0$, $B(0, 0) = 0$, and the contraction estimate on balls whose points lie in $U_m$). $\widetilde C$ is a quadrant-like subset of a finite-dimensional $P$, $\mathbb R^N$ any finite-dimensional $Q$.

chips: points of the balls lie in $U_m$
diff: \"Close enough on level $m$\" presupposes that the points lie in the domain $U_m$; this is required. The theorems that use basic germs add \"$\widetilde C$ closed\" or \"a partial quadrant\" where needed.
Remark 3.1.8 (preprint 3.8) (in [21] $f(0) = 0$ was not required) is a historical remark and makes no claim.

items.title: Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9): the fibre derivative of $B$ is small

book.label: §3.1, Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9), p. 94 (preprint p. 67)
book.statement: For $B$ as in Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7), every $\varepsilon > 0$ and $m \ge 0$: $|D_2B(a, w)\zeta|_m \le \varepsilon|\zeta|_m$ for $\zeta \in W_m$ if $(a, w) \in E_{m+1}$ is close enough to $(0, 0)$ in $E_m$; in particular $D_2B(0, 0) = 0$.

lean.statement: Four formal forms: (a) on level $m$, for an sc$^1$-germ $B$ in the working form of a contraction germ, $\|D_2B(a, w)\|_{L(W_m)} \le \tfrac12$ at points $(a, w) \in U_{m+1}$ with $a \in N(m+1)$, $w \in O(m+1)$, $\iota w \in O(m)$; (b) $D_2B(0, 0) = 0$ for an sc$^1$ sc$^0$-contraction germ; (c) on level $0$ with arbitrary $\varepsilon$: $|D_2B(x)\zeta|_0 \le \varepsilon|\zeta|_0$ for $x \in U_1$ small on level $1$. (d) **as stated**: for $B$ an sc$^1$ sc$^0$-contraction germ on a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every $m$ there is $r > 0$ with $|D_2B(x)\zeta|_m \le \varepsilon|\zeta|_m$ for $\zeta \in W_m$ at every $x \in U_{m+1}$ with $|x|_m < r$.

diff: Stronger in regularity: $B$ sc$^1$ suffices (Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) and Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31) apply the lemma to sc$^1$ and sc$^k$ germs).

The general statement (every $\varepsilon$, every level $m$, points of $E_{m+1}$ small in $E_m$) is proved as stated, from the contraction estimate of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) applied at points small on level $0$; smallness on level $m + 1$ is not needed (Findings, Chapter 3, item 215). It is what Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) on level $m$ (V3.12) and Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31) in the sense of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) (V3.28) use. The constant $\tfrac12$ on level $m$ in the working form, the value at $(0, 0)$ and the level-$0$ form are kept for the theorems that use them. Formerly narrower (the general statement not formalized). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10): the linearization of a basic germ plus an sc$^+$-germ

book.label: §3.1, Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10), p. 95 (preprint p. 68)
book.statement: If $f = h + s$ with $h$ a basic germ and $s$ an sc$^+$-germ, $f(0) = 0$, then $Df(0) : \mathbb R^n \oplus W \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$ is sc-Fredholm of index $n - N$; and for every $m$, $Df(a, w)$ on level $m$ is Fredholm of index $n - N$ for $(a, w) \in E_{m+1}$ small in $E_m$.

lean.statement: For a basic germ $h$, an $s$ sc$^1$ into $(\mathbb R^N \oplus W)^1$ and $f = h + s$ sc$^1$: $Df(0)$ is an sc-operator, sc-Fredholm of index $\dim P - \dim Q$; it is $T_0 + S$ with $T_0(\delta a, \delta w) = (0, \delta w)$ (sc-Fredholm of index $n - N$) and an sc$^+$-operator $S$ built level by level. For the data of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) and $x \in U_1$ small on level $1$, $D(h + s)(x) : E_0 \to F_0$ is Fredholm of index $n - N$. **On every level** (the second statement): for every $m$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that at every $x \in U_{m+1}$ with $|x|_m < \delta$ the level-$m$ operator $Df(x)_m : \mathbb R^n \oplus W_m \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W_m$ is Fredholm of index $\dim P - \dim Q$, for $\widetilde C$ quadrant-like (partial quadrants are); $f(0) = 0$ is not used.

diff: First statement as in the text, with $s$ only sc$^1$ into $F^1$ and $f$ only sc$^1$. The verification that $Df(0) - T_0$ is sc$^+$ (finite-rank terms through $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb R^N$ with smooth values because $Dh(0)$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point $0$) is not in the text (Findings, Chapter 3, item 46).

Second statement: on every level $m$, at the points of $U_{m+1}$ small in $E_m$, as in the text, by the text's proof: $Df(x)_m = T_0 + S(x) + K(x)$ with $\|S(x)\| \le \varepsilon$ by Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) on level $m$ (V3.11) and $K(x)$ compact (finite rank, and $\iota\,\mathrm{pr}_W Ds(x)$ through $W_{m+1} \to W_m$). The one identity the text uses silently, the $W$-component of $Df(x)_m$, is proved from the uniqueness of derivatives within $U_1$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 230). With both statements as in the text under weaker hypotheses ($s$ and $f$ only sc$^1$, $f(0) = 0$ unused) the verdict is “stronger”; formerly narrower, the second statement on level $0$ only (G.21). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11): sc-Fredholm germs

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11), p. 96 (preprint p. 69)
book.statement: $(f, x_0)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if it has a filled version $(g, 0)$ and a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ such that $g - s$ is conjugated to a basic germ: a strong bundle isomorphism $\Psi : U \triangleleft F \to U' \triangleleft F'$ covering an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$ with $\Psi \circ (g - s) \circ \psi^{-1}$ a basic germ.

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm f x₀` (the text’s germ reading): in a strong bundle chart of $P$ centred at $x_0$, a filling $g$ (`IsFillingGerm`, an sc-smooth germ on a germ of neighbourhoods inside $U$, V3.9), a local sc$^+$-section $s$ (`IsScPlusGerm`: $s : E_0 \to F_1$ an sc-smooth germ into $F^1$ on a germ inside $U$) with $\iota s(0) = g(0)$, and `IsConjugateToBasicGerm` for $u \mapsto g(u) - \iota s(u)$: strong bundle maps $\Psi, \Psi'$ inverse to each other (`IsStrongBundleIso`), $\psi(0) = 0$, $U'$ relatively open in $\widetilde C \oplus W$ ($\widetilde C$ a partial quadrant of a finite-dimensional space), a basic germ $h$ on a germ inside $U'$, and $(\Psi(u, g(u) - s(u)))_2 = h(\psi(u))$ for $u \in U$ near $0$.

diff: The conjugation identity is required for $u \in U$ near $0$ (Theorem 3.1.18's (preprint 3.15) identity $(g + \tilde t) - (\tilde t + t_0) = g - t_0$ holds on $U$ only). The text's $C' = T\psi(0)C$ (used in Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54)) is not part of the data; it is proved (V3.48).
The index statement after the definition is V3.46 (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), in the chart).
The witnesses of the conjugation are also available as a structure, `ConjugationData`, so that the dimensions of the basic germ can be named (V3.46).

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the filling and the sc$^+$-section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$; $\Psi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism on all of $U$, which is no restriction (on a relatively open $U_0 \subseteq U$ it is the same after restricting the chart on level $0$). The project’s earlier notion, with $g$ and $s$ sc-smooth on the whole $U$, is `IsScFredholmGermWholeChart`: it implies the germ reading and is exactly the germ reading with $g$, $s$ sc-smooth on $U$ (`isScFredholmGerm_iff_germG_wholeChart`). Whether the two agree for sections sc-smooth on $X$ is open, and no theorem depends on it (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 261–264, 330). What remains is the formulation above and the untamed chart (formerly also the stricter germ side, third addendum).

The existential over charts is essential: a filling in a chart gives a topological isomorphism $\ker Dr(0) \cong \ker\rho(0)$ (`IsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv`), a condition on the chart, so a filling in one chart gives none in another unless these normal spaces match; a compatible tame chart of the trivial bundle carries no filling of any section (`TrivialBundle.not_isFillingGerm_evenBundleChart`) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 350–352). Added in the fourth addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12): local compactness for sc-Fredholm germs

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12), p. 97 (preprint p. 70) ("an immediate consequence of Theorem 3.40")
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ with $f(x_0) = 0$. There are nested open neighbourhoods $O(0) \supset O(1) \supset \cdots$ of $x_0$ in $X_0$ such that $\mathrm{cl}_{X_0}\{x \in O(i) \mid f(x) = 0\}$ is a compact subset of $X_i$.

lean.statement: For a section $f$ ($P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$) of any strong bundle with $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ and $f(x_0) = 0$: nested open $O(i) \ni x_0$ such that the closure in $X$ of $\{x \in O(i) \mid f(x) = 0\}$ is the image of a compact subset of $X_i$ (level topology) under the inclusion $X_i \to X$.

items.title: Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13): convergence on every level

book.label: §3.1, Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13), p. 97 (preprint p. 70)
book.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12), if $f(x_k) = 0$ and $x_k \to x$ in $X_0$, then for every $m$, $x_k \in X_m$ for $k$ large and $x_k \to x$ in $X_m$.

items.title: Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14): sc-Fredholm sections

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14), p. 97 (preprint p. 70)
book.statement: A section $f$ of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ is sc-Fredholm if (1) it is sc-smooth; (2) regularizing: $x \in X_m$, $f(x) \in Y_{m,m+1}$ imply $x \in X_{m+1}$; (3) $(f, x)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point $x$.

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection f`: (1)–(3) for a section of any strong bundle, clause (3) in the germ reading of V3.13. A zero of a regularizing section is a smooth point.

diff: As in the text; the bundle is not required to be tame, which plays no role in the definition (Findings, Chapter 3, item 40).

**Germs.** Clause (3) is the germ notion of V3.13, the text’s germ reading since the switch (phase 2); the earlier whole-chart notion, stricter, is `IsScFredholmSectionWholeChart` and implies this one (`IsScFredholmSectionWholeChart.isScFredholmSection`). Hence “as in the book” again (“restated” in the third addendum) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 330).

items.title: Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15): stability under sc$^+$-perturbations

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), p. 98 (preprint p. 71) (proof preprint pp. 72–73)
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold, $f \in \mathrm{Fred}(P)$ and $s \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $f + s \in \mathrm{Fred}(P)$.

lean.statement: For any strong bundle: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section and $s$ an sc$^+$-section, the fibrewise sum $f + s$ is an sc-Fredholm section: sc-smooth (sum rule in the charts), regularizing ($Y_{m,m+1}$ is closed under fibrewise subtraction and $s$ takes values in $Y_{m,m+1}$ over $X_m$), and an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point (filling germ $g + \tilde t$ on the germ of $g$, sc$^+$-germ $\tilde t + t_0$ on the germ of $t_0$, the same conjugation).

In the germ reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (V3.13), with the text’s proof: $\tilde t = \hat s \circ r$ is sc-smooth on the whole $U$ because $s$ is a global sc$^+$-section, and a germ plus a whole-chart map is a germ on the same germ (Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) for germs, V3.19); the whole-chart form is `theorem_3_1_18_wholeChart` (Findings, Chapter 3, item 300). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Lemma 3.1.19 (preprint 3.16): the extension $\tilde s = s \circ r$

book.label: §3.1, Lemma 3.1.19 (preprint 3.16), p. 99 (preprint p. 72)
book.statement: An sc$^+$-section $s : O \to K$ extends to the sc$^+$-section $\tilde s(u) = s(r(u))$ of $U \triangleleft F \to U$ with (1) $\tilde s = s$ on $O$; (2) $R(r(u), \tilde s(u)) = s(r(u))$.

lean.statement: For a section $s$ of $K \to O$ ($(x, s(x)) \in K$ on $O$): $s(r(x)) = s(x)$ on $O$, and $\rho(r(u))s(r(u)) = s(r(u))$, $R(r(u), s(r(u))) = (r(u), s(r(u)))$ for $u \in U$. That $s \circ r$ is sc-smooth into $F^1$ is proved inside Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15).

items.title: Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17): fillers are stable under sc$^+$-sections

book.label: §3.1, Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17), p. 99 (preprint p. 72)
book.statement: If the sc-smooth section $f : O \to K$ has the filler $g$ and $s : O \to K$ is an sc$^+$-section, then $f + s$ has the filler $g + \tilde s$.

lean.statement: If $g$ is a filling of $\mathbf f$ (`IsFillingGerm`, V3.7) and $s$ is a section of $K \to O$, then $g + s \circ r$ is a filling of $\mathbf f + s$, with the same derivative family in (3): for $s$ sc-smooth on $U$ on the same germ (`IsFillingGerm.add_section`), and for $s$ an sc-smooth germ on $G \cap r^{-1}(G_s)$ (`IsFillingGerm.add_section_germ`); (3) because $[1 - \rho(r(y))](g + s \circ r)(y) = [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$. items.title: Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21): good position

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21), pp. 102–103 (preprint pp. 76–77)
book.statement: A finite-dimensional sc-subspace $N \subseteq E$ is in good position to the partial quadrant $C$ if $N \cap C$ has nonempty interior in $N$ and $N$ has an sc-complement $P$ (a good complement) with: for some $\varepsilon > 0$, $|p|_0 \le \varepsilon|n|_0$ implies ($n \in C \iff n + p \in C$). A merely topological complement is allowed for non-smooth $N$.

lean.statement: `IsGoodComplement E C N P`: $E_0 = N \oplus P$ algebraically and the $\varepsilon$-condition; `IsInGoodPosition E C N`: $N \cap C$ has nonempty interior in $N$ and $N$ has a good complement. $N$ finite-dimensional is a separate instance argument. Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21) as written: `IsScGoodComplement` ($E = N \oplus P$ an sc-splitting, with the constant $\varepsilon$) and `IsInGoodPositionSc`; each implies the project's form. On a partial quadrant a smooth finite-dimensional $N$ in good position (algebraic complement) is in good position with an sc-complement, also inside any sc-subspace $T \supseteq N$; for smooth $N$ the text's good complements are the project's closed ones, and Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21) as written is the project's good position together with $N \subseteq E_\infty$.
