As a *conclusion* the algebraic form is weaker than the text's: an algebraic good complement need not be closed (round-trip item V3.20: $C = E_0$ infinite-dimensional, $P$ the kernel of a discontinuous functional; not in the project). The text's definition is therefore formalized as well, and on a partial quadrant the two agree for smooth $N$: a closed good complement of a smooth $N$ is an sc-complement (the projection along $N$ acts on every level), and a closed good complement always exists there (Findings, Chapter 3, items 210, 211). The theorems that conclude good position are given in the sc form in V3.94, V3.95. Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22): $N \cap C$ is a partial quadrant

book.label: §3.1, Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22), p. 103 (preprint p. 77) (proof §3.8.1, pp. 143–153 (preprint pp. 120–126))
book.statement: If the finite-dimensional sc-subspace $N$ is in good position to the partial quadrant $C$, then $N \cap C$ is a partial quadrant in $N$.

lean.statement: For $N$ finite-dimensional in good position to the partial quadrant $C$: $N \cap C$ is a partial quadrant in $N$ (constant sc-structure). The core: for continuous functionals $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_n$ jointly onto $\mathbb R^n$ with $C = \{\ell_i \ge 0\}$, a linear isomorphism $e : N \to \mathbb R^k \times N_0$ with $N \cap C = e^{-1}([0, \infty)^k \times N_0)$, $k = \dim N - \dim(N \cap W)$.

items.title: Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25): the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property

book.label: §3.2, Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25), p. 104 (preprint p. 79)
book.statement: $M \subseteq X$ (tame) has the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property if $M \subseteq X_\infty$ and every $x \in M$ has a chart $\varphi : (U, x) \to (O, 0)$ onto a tame retract $(O, C, E)$, an $n$-dimensional smooth $N \subseteq E$ in good position to $C$ with good complement $Y$, $E = N \oplus Y$, a relatively open $V \ni 0$ in $N \cap C$ and a continuous $\delta : V \to Y$ with (i) $\varphi(M \cap U) = \{v + \delta(v)\}$, (ii) $\delta : \mathcal O(N \cap C, 0) \to (Y, 0)$ an sc$^\infty$-germ, $\delta(0) = 0$, $D\delta(0) = 0$.

lean.statement: `MPolyfold.TangentGermChart2021 M x n`: the data of (b) as written, with $N$ in good position in the sense of Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21), the good complement $Y$ an sc-complement, $\delta$ defined on $V$, and (ii) read as `IsScInftyGermAt`: for every $m$ and $k$ a relatively open $V_{m,k} \ni 0$ in $N \cap C$ with $\delta(V_{m,k}) \subseteq E_m$ and $\delta : V_{m,k} \to E_m$ of class $C^k$. `HasTangentGermProperty2021 M n`: $M \subseteq X_\infty$ and such data at every point. It is the project's `HasTangentGermProperty` (`hasTangentGermProperty2021_iff`), whose datum `TangentGermChart` has $Y$ closed and $\delta$ on all of $E$: an sc-complement is closed and makes $N$ smooth, and $\delta$ is extended by $0$ off $V$. Both other readings of \"sc$^\infty$-germ\" (one fixed germ; sc-smooth on $V$) imply this one.

diff: Updated (2026-11-09): “$Y$ closed” is not an added hypothesis: the book's good complement is an sc-complement (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21)), hence closed, and Definition 3.2.1 as written is the project's notion (`hasTangentGermProperty2021_iff`, `Chapter3/GoodComplementClosed.lean`). The project's datum with $Y$ closed is kept (`TangentGermChart`).

\"sc$^\infty$-germ\" is read with $k$-dependent neighbourhoods, the reading in which Theorem 3.5.6 (1) (preprint 3.43) is proved (V3.38) and the weakest of the three (Findings, Chapter 3, item 80); Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34) now also holds on one germ (V3.31, third addendum).

items.title: Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26): invariance of the tangent germ property

book.label: §3.2, Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), p. 105 (preprint p. 80)
book.statement: For a pair $(X, M)$ with $X$ a tame M-polyfold, and an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : X \to X'$ with $\psi(M) = M'$: $M'$ has the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property iff $M$ has it.

lean.statement: For an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : X \to X'$ of M-polyfolds with inverse $\psi'$ (sc-smooth both ways on all of $X$, $X'$) and $\psi(M) = M'$: $M'$ has the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property iff $M$ has it. The data at $\psi(x)$ are the transported chart $\varphi \circ \psi^{-1}$ with the same $N$, $Y$, $V$, $\delta$; $\psi(M) \subseteq X'_\infty$ because sc-smooth maps preserve the levels.

items.title: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27): subsets with the tangent germ property are sub-M-polyfolds

book.label: §3.2, Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), p. 106 (preprint p. 81) (proof pp. 106–109 (preprint pp. 81–84))
book.statement: If $X$ is a tame M-polyfold and $M \subseteq X$ has the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property, then (1) $M$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and sc-smoothly equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners; (2) with the data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25), $y \mapsto \pi \circ \varphi(y)$ is a smooth chart of $M$ around $x$.

In Mathlib's language, $M$ with the charted space of its induced corner structure is `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞` (`theorem_3_2_3_isManifold_2021`). The form first recorded: `theorem_3_2_3_of_isRegular`, with regular data at every point as a hypothesis; there also every $\pi\varphi$ is a chart modelled on $(V, N \cap C, N)$ and $d_M(y) = d_{N \cap C}(\pi\varphi(y))$.

items.title: Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28): sc$^0$-contraction germs and their working form

book.label: §3.3, Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28), p. 109 (preprint p. 85)
book.statement: An sc$^0$-germ $f : \mathcal O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to (W, 0)$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ if $f(a, w) = w - B(a, w)$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $m \ge 0$, $|B(a, w) - B(a, w')|_m \le \varepsilon|w - w'|_m$ for $(a, w), (a, w')$ on level $m$ sufficiently close to $(0, 0)$.

The working form `ContractionGerm`: the same data with explicit regions $N(m) \subseteq P$ open, $K(m) \subseteq O(m) \subseteq W_m$ ($K$ closed, $O$ open) on which $B_m(a, \cdot)$ is a $\tfrac12$-contraction ($O$) mapping $K$ into itself; every contraction germ has one.

items.title: Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31): the contraction germ $f^{(1)}$

book.label: §3.3, Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31), pp. 111 ff. (preprint pp. 86–87)
book.statement: If $f = w - B(a, w)$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^k$, $k \ge 1$, with solution germ $\delta$ of class sc$^j$, then $f^{(1)}(v, b, u, w) = (u - B(v, u), w - DB(v, \delta(v))(b, w))$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^{\min(k-1, j)}$ with solution germ $T\delta$ (\"from the uniqueness\").

If the working form also satisfies Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) (as the one built from an sc$^0$-contraction germ does) and $B$ is sc$^1$, then $f^{(1)}$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ in the sense of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) on its germ, for every $s$: an $\varepsilon$-contraction near $0$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$ on every level.

diff: Uniqueness holds only in the contraction region, which must contain $T\delta(v, b)$ for every $b$: the regions are unbounded in $b$, $w$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 3). \"As one verifies by comparing $Tf$ with $f^{(1)}$\" is the chain rule for germs with the shifted solution germ $v \mapsto \delta(v) \in W_1$ (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs, item 4). The parameter region $N(2+s)$ comes from $D\delta(v)$ needing $v \in N(2)$.

The text's “$f^{(1)}$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ” in the sense of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) is proved separately (`isSc0ContractionGerm_next`): on level $m$ its first component is Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) for $B$ on level $m + 1$, its second needs Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) on level $m$ with any $\varepsilon$ (V3.11). The working form records only a $\tfrac12$-contraction on the explicit regions, which is all the proof of Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) uses (Findings, Chapter 3, item 252). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Lemma 3.3.5 (preprint 3.32): the iterated contraction germs

book.label: §3.3, Lemma 3.3.5 (preprint 3.32), p. 111 (preprint p. 87)
book.statement: Given an sc$^0$-contraction germ $f$ of class sc$^k$ and a solution germ $\delta$ of class sc$^j$, $j \le k$, there is an sc$^0$-contraction germ $f^{(j)}$ of class sc$^{\min(k-j, 1)}$ with solution germ $T^j\delta$.

lean.statement: As one induction over all contraction germs (any finite-dimensional parameter space): if $B$ is sc$^k$ and $j \le k$, the solution germ $\delta$ is an sc$^j$-germ on $\mathrm{germ}(s)$ for some $s$. The step $j \to j+1$: $\delta$ sc$^j$, so $f^{(1)}$ is sc$^j$, so $T\delta$ is sc$^j$ (the induction hypothesis for $f^{(1)}$), and $\delta$ is sc$^1$ (Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30)); then $\delta$ is sc$^{j+1}$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s + s' + 1)$.

diff: The iterated germs $f^{(j)}$ are not constructed; the content of the lemma (its step $j \to j+1$) is the induction step (Findings, Chapter 3, item 5).

items.title: Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33): the germ implicit function theorem

book.label: §3.3, Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33), p. 112 (preprint p. 88)
book.statement: If $f : \mathcal O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to (W, 0)$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^k$, its solution germ $\delta$, $f(v, \delta(v)) = 0$, is of class sc$^k$.

lean.statement: If $B$ is an sc$^k$-germ, there is $s$ such that $\delta$ is a solution germ and an sc$^k$-germ **on the shrunken germ** $\mathrm{germ}(s) = (N(m+s) \cap \widetilde C)_m$; the proof gives $s = 2^k - 1$. The same from Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) with balls.

chips: sc^k on a germ shrunk by $2^k - 1$
diff: **Proved with the text's hypotheses.** The germ shrinks with $k$: each induction step uses the previous stage twice, so $s_{j+1} = 2s_j + 1$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 2). In the text's reading, where germs are up to shrinking, this is the theorem; with a germ as a fixed sequence of sets the conclusion holds on $\mathrm{germ}(2^k - 1)$, not on the germ of construction.

The statement keeps \"there is $s$\"; $s = 2^k - 1$ is read off the proof. Whether the shrinking is intrinsic is not decided: in the toy model of the exposition the solution germ is sc-smooth on the original germ.

items.title: Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34): $C^k$ on $k$-dependent neighbourhoods

book.label: §3.3, Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34), p. 113 (preprint p. 88)
book.statement: If the sc$^0$-contraction germ $f$ is sc-smooth, then for all $m, k \ge 0$ there is a relatively open $V_{m,k} \ni 0$ in $\widetilde C$ with (1) $\delta(V_{m,k}) \subseteq W_m$, (2) $\delta : V_{m,k} \to W_m$ of class $C^k$. In particular $\delta$ is sc-smooth at the smooth point $0$.

lean.statement: If $B$ is an sc-smooth germ, then for every $m$ and $k$ there is a relatively open $V \ni 0$ in $\widetilde C$ (namely $N(m+k+s) \cap \widetilde C$) with $\delta(V) \subseteq W_m$ and the level-$m$ map of $\delta$ of class $C^k$ on $V$. The last sentence on one germ: the solution germ is an sc-smooth germ (sc$^k$ for every $k$ on the same sequence of sets) on a diagonal germ $V_m = N(m + t_m) \cap \widetilde C$, $t_m = \sum_{j \le m} s_j$, and a solution germ there.

diff: As in the text, with $V_{m,k}$ depending on $k$. The last sentence holds on one germ: sc$^j$ involves only the levels $\ge j$ of a germ (`isSckGerm_of_levels`), so the $k$-dependent germs $\mathrm{germ}(s_k)$ of Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) can be replaced by one diagonal germ, which shrinks fast with the level ($t_m = 2^{m+1} - m - 2$ for $s_k = 2^k - 1$) but is a germ of neighbourhoods (Findings, Chapter 3, item 250; formerly “in this sense only”, updated in the third addendum of this page). The citation \"Proposition 3.40\" should be Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40), and it is not needed *(book 2017: unchanged, renumbered: "Proposition 3.11" for Theorem 3.11, p. 79)* (Findings, Chapter 3, item 8).

items.title: Theorem 3.35 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition): the germ implicit function theorem on a partial quadrant

book.label: §3.3, Theorem 3.35 (preprint), preprint p. 89
book.statement: Let $\widetilde C$ be a finite-dimensional partial quadrant in $\mathbb R^n$. An sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^k$ has a solution germ of class sc$^k$; if $f$ is sc-smooth so is its solution germ.

lean.statement: For $\widetilde C$ a partial quadrant in a finite-dimensional $P$: if $B$ is sc$^k$ there is $s$ with $\delta$ sc$^k$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s)$; if $B$ is sc-smooth, $\delta$ is an sc-smooth germ (sc$^k$ for every $k$) on **one** germ $N(m + t_m) \cap \widetilde C$ (earlier form: for every $k$ an $s$ with $\delta$ sc$^k$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s)$). In the text's form: for an sc$^0$-contraction germ $f = w - B(a, w)$ of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) on a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$ and **any** representative $(V, \delta)$ of its solution germ ($\delta$ sc$^0$, $\delta(0) = 0$, $f(a, \delta(a)) = 0$ on $V_0$): if $f$ is sc$^k$, $\delta$ is sc$^k$ on a germ $V' \subseteq V$; if $f$ is sc-smooth, $\delta$ is an sc-smooth germ on one germ $V' \subseteq V$.

diff: The last sentence is proved as `IsScSmoothGerm` on one germ (the diagonal germ of V3.31); before the third addendum of this page only for every $k$ on a germ depending on $k$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 2, 250).

In the text's form the hypotheses are on $f$ ($f$ is sc$^k$ iff $B$ is, `isSckGerm_contractionMap_iff`) and any representative of the solution germ is allowed (it agrees with the constructed one near $0$, by the uniqueness of Theorem 3.3.2 (preprint 3.29)); the conclusion holds on a smaller germ $V' \subseteq V$, as for Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) (V3.30), and $\mathbb R^n$ is generalized to a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$ in a finite-dimensional $P$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 251). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 3.4.1 (preprint 3.37): the basic class

book.label: §3.4, Definition 3.4.1 (preprint 3.37), p. 114 (preprint p. 90)
book.statement: A basic germ $f : \mathcal O([0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k} \oplus W, 0) \to (\mathbb R^N \oplus W, 0)$ is an sc-smooth germ such that $P_W \circ f$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ; $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the class of basic germs.

lean.statement: Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7) restated: `IsBasicGerm` (V3.10).

diff: Same notion as Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7).

items.title: Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38): weak stability of basic germs

book.label: §3.4, Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38), p. 114 (preprint p. 90) (proof pp. 113–117 (preprint pp. 90–93))
book.statement: For a basic germ $f$ and the principal part $s$ of an sc$^+$-section with $s(0) = 0$ there is a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi : U \triangleleft (\mathbb R^N \oplus W) \to U' \triangleleft (\mathbb R^{N'} \oplus W')$ covering an sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi$ such that $(\Phi_*(f + s))^1$ (levels raised by one) is a basic germ; $n - N = n' - N'$.

lean.statement: Given $f$ basic with contraction $B$ and the data `StabilityData` (the $W$-component $s$ of the sc$^+$-germ, $s(0) = 0$, and an sc-Fredholm splitting $W = C \oplus X = R \oplus Z$ of $1 + D_2s(0)$, which exists by Proposition 1.1.11 (preprint 1.10)): with the **linear** base change $\psi(a, w) = ((a, (1 - P_1)w), P_1w)$ and fibre change $\Psi(q, w) = ((q, (1 - P_2)w), L^{-1}P_2w)$, the germ $(\Phi_*(f + s))^1 = \Psi \circ (f + s)^1 \circ \psi^{-1}$ on $\psi(U_{m+1})$ is a basic germ with contraction $\hat B = L^{-1}P_2(B - S)$; zeros correspond under $\psi$; and $\dim C = \dim Z$.

diff: The coordinate change is linear, so a pair of sc-isomorphisms replaces a general strong bundle isomorphism; the text's $\tau : Z \to C$ is not applied (new target $(Q \oplus Z) \oplus X^1$). The index raise is a change of sc-structure (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 60–61).

\"$S$ is an arbitrarily small contraction on every level $m \ge 1$\" needs the operator-norm continuity of the derivative of $s$ on level $m + 1$ and the mean value inequality (item 62). Only the $W$-component of $s$ enters; $B$ is used only through Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7) (item 63).
The linear coordinate change is a strong bundle isomorphism of the index-raised structures (`StabilityData.linIso_isStrongBundleIso`, V3.76).

items.title: Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40): local regularity and compactness

book.label: §3.5, Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40), p. 118 (preprint p. 94) (proof pp. 118–123 (preprint pp. 95–98))
book.statement: Let $f = h + s : U \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $h$ a basic germ, $s$ an sc$^+$-germ with $s(0) = 0$, $S = \{f = 0\}$. There are relatively open neighbourhoods $U \supset O(0) \supset O(1) \supset \cdots$ of $0$ on level $0$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{C_0}(S \cap O(m)) \subseteq C_m$.

lean.statement: Let $B$ be an sc$^0$-contraction germ on $\widetilde C \oplus W$ with **$\widetilde C$ closed**, $\mathbf s$ sc$^0$ into $W^1$ with $\mathbf s(0) = 0$, and $S$ any set of solutions of $w = B(a, w) - \mathbf s(a, w)$ in $U_0$. There are nested open $O(i) \ni 0$ in $E_0$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{E_0}(S \cap O(i)) = \iota_i(K_i)$ for compact $K_i \subseteq E_i$; in particular $\mathrm{cl}(S \cap O(i)) \subseteq E_i$. For a basic germ plus an sc$^+$-germ this gives the local Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12).

diff: Stronger: the closures are compact in $E_i$, which Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) needs and Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, item 12). Weaker hypotheses: of $f$ only the $W$-component, with $B$ sc$^0$ and the contraction estimate, and $\mathbf s$ sc$^0$ into $W^1$ (item 14).

**$\widetilde C$ closed** is a hypothesis because the theorem is proved for convex $\widetilde C$; it holds for partial quadrants. The induction left to the reader needs existence, bound and continuity of the lifts together (item 13); the $O(i)$ are one level ahead of the text's.

items.title: Corollary 3.5.3 (preprint 3.41): the linearization at nearby solutions

book.label: §3.5, Corollary 3.5.3 (preprint 3.41), p. 122 (preprint p. 98) (proof pp. 121–125 (preprint pp. 98–100))
book.statement: For $f = h + s : U \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $h$ basic, $s$ an sc$^+$-map, $s(0) = 0$, $Df(0)$ surjective: there is $U' \subseteq U$ relatively open on level $0$ such that (1) solutions in $U'$ are on level $1$; (2) at such solutions $Df(a, w) : E \to F$ is a surjective Fredholm operator of index $n - N$.

lean.statement: For the data of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) ($f := h$ basic, $s$ the $W$-component of the sc$^+$-germ) with $D(h + s)(0)$ surjective: there is $r > 0$ such that every zero $x$ of $h + s$ in $U_0$ with $|x|_0 < r$ is $\iota(x_1)$ with $x_1 \in U_1$, and $D(h + s)(x_1) : E_0 \to F_0$ is a surjective Fredholm operator of index $\dim P - \dim Q$.

diff: The $\mathbb R^N$-component of the sc$^+$-map is absorbed into $h$ (as in Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), Findings item 85). The Fredholm property with index holds at every $x \in U_1$ small on level $1$, not only at solutions; $Df(x) = Df(0) + S(x) + K(x)$ with $\|S(x)\| \le \varepsilon$ and $K(x)$ compact; surjectivity from $\dim\ker \le n - N = \mathrm{ind}$; the detour through level $2$ is not needed (item 71).

items.title: Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42): solutions of the push-forward are on level 1

book.label: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42), p. 126 (preprint p. 101)
book.statement: (In the setting after Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38), $g = \Phi_*f$, $\delta$ the solution germ of $P' \circ g^1$.) There are $\varepsilon'_0, \tau'_0$ such that a solution $(a', w')$ of $g = 0$ with $|a'|_0 \le \varepsilon'_0$, $|w'|_0 \le \tau'_0$ has $w' = \delta(a')$, and $|\delta(a')|_0 \le \tau'_0$ if $|a'|_0 \le \varepsilon'_0$.

lean.statement: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $r > 0$ such that every zero $x'$ of $g = \Phi_*(f + s)$ in $\psi(U)$ with $|x'|_0 < r$ has its $X$-component on level $1$ with $|\cdot|_1 < \varepsilon$.

diff: The formal statement is the regularity Theorem 3.5.6's (preprint 3.43) proof uses (solutions near $0$ lie on level $1$ and are small there), proved from the lifts of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) and the linearity of $\psi$; the identification $w' = \delta(a')$ is made inside Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 65).

items.title: Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43): local germ-solvability I

book.label: §3.5, Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43), p. 126 (preprint p. 102) (proof pp. 126–131 (preprint pp. 102–106))
book.statement: Let $f = h + s$ with $Df(0)$ surjective and $K = \ker Df(0)$ in good position to $C$, $g = \Phi_*(f)$. Then $K' = \ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C'$, there are a good complement $Y'$ and a $C^1$ map $\tau : V \to Y'_1$, $V$ relatively open in $K' \cap C'$, with (1) $\tau$ an sc-smooth germ; (2) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$; (3) after shrinking $U$, $\varphi(\{f = 0\}) = \{g = 0\} = \{y + \tau(y) \mid y \in V\}$.

lean.statement: For an sc-smooth germ $g$ with $g(0) = 0$ whose index-raised germ $g^1$ is basic (`ShiftedBasicData`), $\widetilde C$ a partial quadrant, $Dg(0)$ onto, $K' = \ker Dg(0)$ in good position, and the regularity hypothesis of Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42): there are a good complement $Y = Z \oplus W$, $V$ relatively open in $K' \cap C'$ and $\tau : V \to Y$ of class $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, every $y + \tau(y)$ a zero in $U$, every zero in $U$ near $0$ of this form; and (1) for every $k \ge 1$ a relatively open $V_k \subseteq V$ containing $0$ and a $C^k$ map $\tau_k : V_k \to E_k$ with $\iota_k\tau_k = \tau$ on $V_k$.

A gap in the text's proof of (3) is filled: the $\widetilde K$-component of a solution lies in $\widetilde C$, because $|z| \le \varepsilon|k|$ near $0$ (item 66). $H$ is $C^j$ near $0$ by Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34) for $g^1$ and Proposition 1.2.3 (preprint 1.18) for germs (item 67).

items.title: Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52): the linearization at a zero is Fredholm of index $n - N$

book.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), p. 135 (preprint p. 110)
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (of the index $n - N$ of the basic germ, as the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) uses).

lean.statement: For a section $f$ with $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ and $f(x_0) = 0$: in the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) centred at $x_0$, with the filling germ $g$ (a derivative family $Dg$ on a germ $G \subseteq U$) and the local sc$^+$-germ $s$, $Dg(0) : E \to F$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, $T_0O = Dr(0)E$ and $K_0 = \rho(0)F$ are sc-subspaces, and $Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is an sc-Fredholm operator; for **every** conjugation of $g - s$ to a basic germ $h : O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ (`ConjugationData`), both are Fredholm of index $n - N$ on every level. In particular $n - N$ does not depend on the conjugation. For an sc-Fredholm section the same holds in **every** strong bundle chart around a zero $y$: at the point $z$ over $y$, $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $n - N$ on every level.

diff: Proved in sc form, in charts: $T_0O$, $K_0$ (and $T_zO$, $K_z$ in any chart) with the induced sc-structures stand for $T_xX$, $Y_x$, which carry no linear structure here (G.7). Two steps the text leaves out: that $D(g - s)(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1}Dh(0)D\psi(0)$, the conjugate of the basic germ's linearization, is sc-Fredholm (the criterion of V1.8: $\Gamma(0)$ preserves the levels and $Dh(0)$ is regularizing), and the sc-structures of $T_0O$, $K_0$ (Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47) at the smooth point $0$, the closed graph theorem). No tameness is assumed. In other charts the levels are transported by the chart change at smooth points (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 239). Formerly level $0$ only (G.22, Findings item 48); updated in the third addendum of this page. (2026-11-09: $T_xX$ now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at smooth points, gap G.7 closed (V2.19); this statement is not restated with it.)

The first formal statement (`proposition_3_6_5_preprint`, kept for the theorems that use it) gives the index as “$n - N$ for some $n, N \in \mathbb N$”, which every integer satisfies. `proposition_3_6_5_index` names the conjugation data and identifies $n$, $N$ with the dimensions of the conjugating basic germ, for every conjugation (Findings, Chapter 3, item 120). Updated after the first edition of this page.
In every other strong bundle chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of the same index, and onto at a zero in good position (V3.96). Updated in the second addendum of this page.

**Germs.** The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): an sc-Fredholm germ whose filling and sc$^+$-section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13); $Dg(0)$ is the value at $0$ of a derivative family of the filling germ, the same for every family on every germ. The forms for germ data on the whole chart are the `_wholeChart` declarations of the same names (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 289, 310, 331). Hence “restated” (formerly “narrower”, for that hypothesis): what remains is the reading in charts.

items.title: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53): good position of an sc-Fredholm germ

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111)
book.statement: An sc-Fredholm germ $(f, x)$ of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ is in good position if (1) $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is surjective and (2) if $d_X(x) \ge 1$, $\ker f'(x)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_xX$ in $T_xX$.

lean.statement: In the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (`IsGoodPositionAtGerm`, at $Dg(0)$ for a derivative family $Dg$ of the filling germ $g$): $Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is onto and $\ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C_0O = T_0O \cap C$ inside $T_0O$ (`IsInGoodPositionIn`); `IsGoodPositionAt` is the case of a whole-chart filled version. For a section (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm f x₀`): the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at $x_0$ with the germ in good position in that chart. With the text’s sc-complement (`IsGoodPositionAtScGerm`; for a section `StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermSc`, in a tame chart): the kernel has a good sc-complement inside $T_0O$ ($T_m = N_m \oplus P_m$ on every level). At a zero of an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data the two forms agree.

chips: sc-complement form: the same at zeros
diff: Stated in a chart centred at $x$, not in $T_xX$ (the transport of $C_xX$ to $T_xX$ is not formalized, Chapter 2 gap). The case distinction $d_X(x) \ge 1$ is dropped: at an interior point (2) holds trivially (Findings, Chapter 3, item 50), and for tame germ data good position in a tame chart at a zero with $d_X = 0$ is the surjectivity of the linearization (V3.100).

At a zero, the linearization and the two conditions do not depend on the chart (V3.78); Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero from a chart not centred there is V3.79, in any chart of the germ data V3.107. The form in a tame chart (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame`), which the theorems of §3.6 assume and conclude, is V3.103.

The sc form needs the kernel smooth and a closed good complement in $E$. At a zero $\ker Dg(0)$ is the image under $D\psi'(0)$ of the basic germ's smooth kernel, and the good position of the kernel in $E$ comes from the transport from $T_0O$, so V3.20 applies (Findings, Chapter 3, item 212). “$T = N \oplus P$ an sc-splitting of $T$” is written in $E$; its equivalence with an sc-splitting of the sc-Banach space $T_0O$ is not formalized, nor is the upgrade from good position inside $T$ alone (items 211, 214). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the germ data are the text’s (V3.13), and the condition in the chart is read at $Dg(0)$, the value at $0$ of any derivative family of the filling germ (the same for all, `IsGoodPositionGerm.forall_isGoodPositionAtGerm`); the whole-chart forms are `IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermScWholeChart` (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 280, 320, 330).

items.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54): the solution set as a graph (part (3) of the proof)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), p. 136 (preprint p. 111) (proof pp. 136–140 (preprint pp. 111–115))
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ and $(f, x)$ in good position. There is an open $V \ni x$ such that $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ has: (1) at every $y \in S$, $(f, y)$ is in good position; (2) $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners. The proof shows (3): $\psi\varphi(S) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$ for the $\sigma$ of Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47) applied to $\Psi_*(g) = h + t$.

lean.statement: `theorem_3_6_8_book`, for an sc-Fredholm section with germ data in tame charts (`IsScFredholmSectionTame2021`, V3.103) and a zero $x_0$ in good position (`IsGoodPositionGermTame2021`): there are an open $V \ni x_0$ and $d$ such that (1) every zero $y \in V$ is in good position, with $f'(y)$ onto of index $d = \dim\ker f'(y)$ in every strong bundle chart (`IsSurjLinOfIndex`); and (2) $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, and is tame. The proof's graph description (3) is `theorem_3_6_8_graph`, in the chart at $x_0$: a tame chart $\varphi$ centred at $x_0$, the conjugating sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$ with its inverse, a basic germ $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ with the data of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) and $D(h + t)(0)$ surjective with kernel $K$ in good position, $K$ a smooth subspace; a **closed** good complement $Y$; $V'$ relatively open in $K \cap C'$, $\sigma : V' \to Y$ $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$, every $v + \sigma(v)$ a zero of $h + t$, and $C^k$-lifts $\sigma_k : V_k \to E'_k$ near $0$ for every $k$ (Theorem 3.5.11 (1) (preprint Corollary 3.47)); and an open $V_x \ni x_0$ on which $\psi\varphi$ is injective, $f(y) = 0 \iff (h + t)(\psi\varphi(y)) = 0$, and $\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x \mid f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$.

chips: (3): a step in the chart at $x_0$
diff: "Tame strong bundle" is read as germ data in tame charts (V3.103; Findings, Chapter 3, item 382). The graph description (3) is a step of the proof, stated with the open set $V_x$ of the chart at $x_0$; it is not combined with the $V$ of (1) and (2), which would need a shrinking of $V'$ (items 50, 85, 86, 190–192). The forms first proved for (1) and (2) are V3.82 and V3.85; the choice of $Y$ with the projection property is V3.77 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 383).

Tameness enters through $(1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0$ (Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35)), for the base retraction of the chart at $x_0$; the text's $C' = T\psi(0)C$ is proved by the sign argument; the $\mathbb R^N$-component of $t$ is absorbed into $h$; $D(h + t)(0)$ is identified with $D(\Psi_*g)(0)$ by uniqueness on level $1$; the unspecified $V$ is made explicit (items 50, 85, 86). The closedness of $Y$, the smoothness of $K$ and the lifts of $\sigma$ are recorded for Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) (items 93, 94). (2026-11-09: the closedness of $Y$ is not an added hypothesis, the book's good complement being an sc-complement, `hasTangentGermProperty2021_iff`, `lemma_3_6_9`.)

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55): good position along a graph

book.label: §3.6, Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55), p. 139 (preprint p. 114) (proof §3.8.4 (preprint §3.8.3), pp. 160–164 (preprint pp. 132–135))
book.statement: $C \subseteq E$ a partial quadrant, $N$ a finite-dimensional smooth subspace in good position with good complement $Y$, $V \subseteq N \cap C$ relatively open, $\tau : V \to Y_1$ of class $C^1$ with $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$. Then for $v$ in a relatively open $V' \ni 0$: (1) $v + \tau(v) \in C_1$; (2) $Y$ is a topological complement of $N_v = \{n + D\tau(v)n\}$; (3) there is $\gamma_v > 0$ with $n \in C_x \iff n + y \in C_x$ for $n \in N_v$, $y \in Y$, $|y|_0 \le \gamma_v|n|_0$, $x = v + \tau(v)$.

lean.statement: `lemma_3_6_9` (`lemma_3_6_9_relOpen`, V3.80, with the book's good complement): for a partial quadrant $C = T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)$, a finite-dimensional $N$ in good position (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21)) with good sc-complement $Y$, $V$ relatively open in $N \cap C$ with $0 \in V$, and $\sigma$ with values in $Y$, $C^1$ on $V$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$: there is $\rho > 0$ such that for $v \in V$ with $|v| < \rho$ and $z = v + \sigma(v)$, $z \in C$, $Y$ is a good complement of $N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n\}$ with respect to $C_z$, and $N_v$ is in good position to $C_z$; the constant does not depend on $v$. The form first recorded here: `lemma_3_6_9_preprint`, in the model $\mathbb R^n \oplus W$, for $\tau$ on all of $N \cap C$ and a closed good complement.

diff: Proved in full in V3.80 (`lemma_3_6_9_relOpen`: $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V$, any presentation of $C$), with the book's good complement in `lemma_3_6_9` (2026-11-09: “$Y$ closed” is implied by the sc-complement, `Chapter3/GoodComplementClosed.lean`); the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`lemma_3_6_9_preprint`).

$\tau$ is a map on all of $N \cap C$ (the text: on a neighbourhood $V$). The form used in Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) — $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V \subseteq N \cap C$, any presentation of $C$, and the good position of $N_v$ — is `lemma_3_6_9_relOpen` (V3.80): $\sigma$ is extended to the cone by a bump. The sc-level of the values plays no role ((1) is $v + \tau(v) \in C$). The constant $\gamma_v$ can be chosen uniformly; the case $v \notin N \cap W$ needs no normal form.

items.title: Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56): the global implicit function theorem, $\partial X = \emptyset$ (from the tangent germ property)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56), p. 140 (preprint p. 115)
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle over an M-polyfold with $\partial X = \emptyset$ and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with surjective linearization at every point of $S = \{f = 0\}$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold without boundary.

lean.statement: Let $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103) at every zero $x$, and $S \ne \emptyset$. Then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension and has degeneracy index $0$ everywhere (`theorem_3_6_10`, V3.86; with the text's sc-complement, `theorem_3_6_10_sc`). The step first recorded here: if $X$ is without boundary and $S \ne \emptyset$ has at every point the regular data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25), then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of an $n$-dimensional manifold without boundary.

diff: Proved in full in V3.86; the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`theorem_3_6_10_of_tangentGerm`, from the tangent germ property).

Formalized here is the second step of the text's proof: from the tangent germ property of $S$ to the manifold structure (Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), with $d_S = 0$ by Lemma 2.4.6 (preprint 2.26)). The theorem with the text's hypotheses, through Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) at every zero, is V3.86.

items.title: Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57): the global implicit function theorem, boundary case (from the tangent germ property)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57), p. 140 (preprint p. 115)
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section such that at every $x \in S = \{f = 0\}$ the linearization is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103) at every zero $x$. If $S \ne \emptyset$, $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold, its induced structure is tame and equivalent to a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension, and $S$ is the disjoint union of open and closed parts $S_n$ of dimension $n$ (`theorem_3_6_11`, `theorem_3_6_11_dim`, V3.87; with the text's sc-complement, `theorem_3_6_11_sc`). The step first recorded here: from regular data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) at every point of $S$.

diff: Proved in full in V3.87; the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`theorem_3_6_11_of_tangentGerm`, from the tangent germ property).
As V3.50: the step from the tangent germ property. The theorem with the text's hypotheses is V3.87.

items.title: Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59): injectivity of $P_Y Df(b)$ on $X$ near $0$ (abstract form)

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59), p. 141 (preprint p. 117)
book.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) ($Y = Df(0)X$, $P_Y$ the projection along a finite-dimensional complement $A$), there is a relatively open neighbourhood $O$ of $0$ in $B \cap C$ such that $P_Y \circ Df(b) : X \to Y$ has trivial kernel for $b \in O$.

lean.statement: For a family $b \mapsto L(b)$ of sc-operators $X \to Y$ with $(b, h) \mapsto L(b)h$ continuous on $O \times X_0$ ($O \ni 0$), $L(0)$ injective on $X_0$, and the compactness property on level $0$ (`FamilyCompactness`: $b_j \to b$, $h_j$ bounded, $L(b_j)h_j \to 0$ imply a convergent subsequence of $h_j$): $L(b)$ is injective on $X_0$ for $b \in O$ near $0$.

diff: Formalized for an abstract family with the compactness property that condition (2) of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) gives for $L = P_Y \circ Df|_X$ (the difference $(1 - P_Y)Df(b_j)h_j$ lies in the finite-dimensional $A$). In the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) these hypotheses are derived from the theorem's (`familyCompactness_derivFamOp`, `continuousOn_derivFamOp`; V3.89; Findings, Chapter 3, item 73).

items.title: Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60): uniform lower bounds (abstract form)

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60), p. 142 (preprint p. 118)
book.statement: For a relatively open $\widetilde O \ni 0$ in $C \cap B$ with compact closure in $O$ (Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59)), for every $m$ there is $c_m > 0$ with $|P_Y \circ Df(b)h|_m \ge c_m|h|_m$ for $b \in \widetilde O$, $h \in X_m$.

lean.statement: For a compact $K$, a family of sc-operators $L(b)$ with $(b, h) \mapsto L(b)_mh$ continuous on $K \times X_m$, every $L(b)_m$ ($b \in K$) injective, and the compactness property on level $m$: there is $c_m > 0$ with $c_m|h|_m \le |L(b)h|_m$ for $b \in K$, $h \in X_m$.

diff: The injectivity of every $L(b)_m$ on $K$ is a hypothesis; in the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) it comes from Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59) on level $0$ and `ScOperator.injective_lvl` (V3.89). The step “injective sc-Fredholm of index $0$, hence an sc-isomorphism” is the block index computation there (Findings, Chapter 3, item 73).

items.title: Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61): the inverse of a family of sc-isomorphisms

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61), p. 142 (preprint p. 118) (quoted from [25, Proposition 4.8], no proof)
book.statement: Let $V$ be relatively open in a partial quadrant of a finite-dimensional $G$, $v \mapsto L(v)$ a family of sc-isomorphisms $E \to F$ with $(v, h) \mapsto L(v)h$ sc-smooth and $|L(v)h|_m \ge c_m|h|_m$ for $v \in V$, $h \in E_m$. Then $(v, k) \mapsto L(v)^{-1}k$ is sc-smooth. Operator-norm continuity of $v \mapsto L(v)$ is not assumed.

lean.statement: For a germ $V$ of relatively open neighbourhoods of $0$ in a partial quadrant $\widetilde C$ of a finite-dimensional $G$ and sc-isomorphisms $L(v) : E \to F$ such that $\Phi(v, h) = L(v)h$ is an sc-smooth germ on $V \oplus E$ and $c_m\|h\| \le \|L(v)_mh\|$ for $v \in V_0$: $\Lambda(v, k) = L(v)^{-1}k$ is an sc-smooth germ on $V \oplus F$, with derivative $D\Lambda(v, k)(\delta v, \delta k) = L(v)^{-1}(\delta k - D_1\Phi(v, L(v)^{-1}k)\delta v)$.

diff: Formalized for germs ($V$ a germ around $0$, $V \oplus E$ the product germ), the form Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) uses. The text gives no proof; the differentiability uses the remainder of $\Phi$ along $(\delta v, 0)$ and the compactness of $F_1 \to F_0$ in place of the operator-norm continuity, which is not assumed (Findings, Chapter 3, item 72).
Used in set form in the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) (`famInv_isScSmooth_of`, V3.88).

items.title: Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65): good complements avoid the vanishing coordinates

book.label: §3.8.1, Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65), p. 150 (preprint p. 123)
book.statement: $N^\perp \subseteq \mathbb R^\Sigma \oplus W$ (the text's notation), i.e. a good complement has vanishing coordinates $i \in \Sigma$, where $\Sigma$ is the set of indices vanishing at some nonzero point of $N \cap C$.

lean.statement: For functionals $\ell_i$ cutting out $C$ and a good complement $P$ of $N$: $\ell_i(p) = 0$ for $p \in P$ and $i \in \Sigma$. Consequence: $Q = (\ell_i)_{i \in \Sigma} : N \to \mathbb R^\Sigma$ is onto.

diff: As in the text (its $\mathbb R^\Sigma \oplus W$ is the set where the coordinates in $\Sigma$ vanish), for any family of functionals cutting out $C$.

items.title: Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69): the degeneracy index of $N \cap C$

book.label: §3.8.1, Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69), p. 153 (preprint p. 126)
book.statement: For $N$ smooth, finite-dimensional, in good position to $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ in $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, and $x \in N \cap C$: (1) $d_{N \cap C}(x) = d_C(x)$ if $x \notin N \cap W$; (2) $d_{N \cap C}(x) = \dim N - \dim(N \cap W)$ if $x \in N \cap W$.

lean.statement: In the model: (1) as stated; (2) as $d_{N \cap C}(x) + \dim(N \cap W) = \dim N$, with $N \cap W$ the kernel of $N \to \mathbb R^n$.

diff: (2) additively (natural-number subtraction avoided); proof read off the normal form of Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 20).

items.title: Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70): the degeneracy index along a graph

book.label: §3.8.1, Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70), p. 154 (preprint p. 127)
book.statement: For $N$ in good position to $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ with good complement $Y$ and $\tau : N \cap C \to Y_1$ of class $C^1$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$: $d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(v + \tau(v))$ for $v \in N \cap C \setminus N \cap W$ close to $0$.

lean.statement: In the model: there is $\rho > 0$ such that for $v \in N \cap C$, $|v| < \rho$: $v + \tau(v) \in C$, and if $v \notin N \cap W$, $d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(v + \tau(v))$. The core, in coordinates: the vanishing coordinates of $v + \tau(v)$ are those of $v$.

diff: \"Close to $0$\" is $|v| < \rho/(1 + c)$ (smallness along a segment); the two cases $\dim N = 1$, $\dim N \ge 2$ are unified by a ray decomposition and a mean value estimate; the level $Y_1$ plays no role (Findings, Chapter 3, item 31).

items.title: Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72): the quadrant inverse function theorem

book.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72), p. 165 (preprint p. 136)
book.statement: $C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ a partial quadrant, $U \subseteq C$ a relatively open neighbourhood of $0$, $f : U \to \mathbb R^n$ smooth with $f(U) \subseteq C$, (1) $f(0) = 0$, $Df(0)C = C$; (2) $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$. Then $f$ is a diffeomorphism between relatively open neighbourhoods $U'$, $V'$ of $0$ in $C$.

lean.statement: For $C$ a partial quadrant in a finite-dimensional $V$ and $f$ of class $C^j$, $j \ge 1$, with (1), (2): relatively open $U' \subseteq U$, $V'$ containing $0$ with $f(U') = V'$, $f$ injective on $U'$, and an inverse $g$ of class $C^j$ on $V'$.

diff: For $C^j$, each $j \ge 1$ (smooth = all $j$). Hypothesis (2) is used only through \"$x$ interior iff $f(x)$ interior\" (Findings, Chapter 3, item 27). \"$Df(0)$ is an isomorphism from $\mathbb R^n = C - C$\": surjectivity needs only an interior point of $C$ (item 29).

items.title: Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73): the normalized inverse function theorem

book.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73), p. 165 (preprint p. 137)
book.statement: $U \subseteq C$ relatively open, convex, $0 \in U$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with (1) $f(0) = 0$, (2) $|Df(x) - 1| \le \tfrac12$, (3) $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$. Then $V = f(U)$ is relatively open in $C$ and $f : U \to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77): the inverse is $C^1$

book.statement: $U$ relatively open in $C$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with $V = f(U)$ relatively open, $f : U \to V$ a homeomorphism, $Df(x)$ invertible. Then $g = f^{-1}$ is $C^1$ with $Dg(y) = [Df(g(y))]^{-1}$.

items.title: Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78): the implicit function theorem in partial quadrants

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78), p. 169 (preprint p. 141)
book.statement: $U$ a relatively open neighbourhood of $0$ in $C = [0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k}$, $f : U \to \mathbb R^N$ of class $C^j$, $f(0) = 0$, $Df(0)$ onto, $K = \ker Df(0)$ in good position with good complement $Y$. Then there are $V$ open in $K \cap C$, a $C^j$ map $\tau : V \to Y$ and $\varepsilon, \sigma > 0$ with (1) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, $k + \tau(k) \in U$; (2) $|\tau(k)| \le \sigma$ for $|k| \le \varepsilon$; (3) $f(k + y) = 0$, $|k| \le \varepsilon$, $|y| \le \sigma$ imply $y = \tau(k)$.

lean.statement: For a partial quadrant $C$ in a finite-dimensional $V$, $f : U \to F$ ($F$ any normed space) of class $C^j$, $j \ge 1$, with the hypotheses: $V'$ relatively open in $K \cap C$, $\tau : K \to Y$ of class $C^j$ on $V'$ with (1) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, **$k + \tau(k) \in U$ and $f(k + \tau(k)) = 0$**; (2); (3) for $y \in Y$ with **$k + y \in U$**.

diff: **Two clauses the text omits are included**: $f(k + \tau(k)) = 0$ in (1) (the content of the theorem) and $k + y \in U$ in (3) (needed for $f(k + y)$ to be defined) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 22).
Only the convexity of $C$ and its nonempty interior are used (normalized form), the quadrant entering through good position (item 23); $\tau$ is $C^j$ on the whole $V_0$ without shrinking (item 24).

items.title: Lemma 3.8.23 (preprint 3.79): the contraction region

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.23 (preprint 3.79), p. 170 (preprint p. 142)
book.statement: There are $a, b > 0$ such that on $(B_K(a) \oplus B_Y(b)) \cap C \subseteq U$ the map $B(k, \cdot)$ is a $\tfrac12$-contraction; so $f(k, y) = f(k, y')$ forces $y = y'$.

lean.statement: In the normalized data: constants $\varepsilon$, $a$, $b$ with $\varepsilon a \le b$, the region $R = \{|k| \le a, |y| \le b\} \cap C \subseteq U$ with $\|DB\| \le \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$ on it; the mean value inequality on $R$; a fixed point $y$ with $(k, y) \in R$ is $\tau(k)$.

diff: As in the text, with the constant $c_0 = \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.24 (preprint 3.80): the fixed point set $X_k$

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.24 (preprint 3.80), p. 170 (preprint p. 143)
book.statement: Replacing $a$ by a smaller number, $|B(k, y)| \le \varepsilon|k|$ for $|y| \le \varepsilon|k|$, so $B(k, \cdot)$ maps $X_k = \bar B_Y(\varepsilon|k|)$ into itself and has a unique fixed point $\tau(k)$; with $c(a) = (1 + \varepsilon)\max_{B((1+\varepsilon)a)}|DB|$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.25 (preprint 3.81): continuity of $\tau$

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.25 (preprint 3.81), p. 171 (preprint p. 144)
book.statement: $\tau : B_K(a) \cap C \to B_Y(b)$ is continuous and satisfies $|\tau(k)| \le \varepsilon|k|/2$ and $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \varepsilon|k - k_0|$.

lean.statement: $|\tau(k)| \le \varepsilon|k|/2$ and $\tau$ is continuous on $V_0$; for all $k, k_0 \in V_0$, $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \frac{\varepsilon}{1 + \varepsilon}|k - k_0| \le \varepsilon|k - k_0|$, so $\tau$ is $\frac{\varepsilon}{1 + \varepsilon}$-Lipschitz on $V_0$. (An older form with the constant $1 + 2\varepsilon$ is kept for the proofs that use it.)

diff: The text's constant $\varepsilon$ holds on all of $V_0$; its proof omits a case distinction. It uses the point $(k, \tau(k_0))$, which lies in the region of the contraction when $|k_0| \le 2|k|$; otherwise $|k| < 2|k_0|$ and the same argument with $k$ and $k_0$ exchanged applies. Either way $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \tfrac12|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| + c_0|k - k_0|$ with $c_0 = \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$, which gives the sharper constant $\varepsilon/(1 + \varepsilon)$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 216; revises item 25, which had only $1 + 2\varepsilon$). The older estimate is kept for `continuousOn_τ` and Lemma 3.8.26 (preprint 3.82) (item 217). Formerly narrower; updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.26 (preprint 3.82): $\tau$ is of class $C^j$

book.statement: If $f$ is of class $C^j$, $j \ge 1$, then $\tau$ is of class $C^j$ on a possibly smaller neighbourhood of $0$, with $D\tau(k) = (1 - D_2B(k, \tau(k)))^{-1}D_1B(k, \tau(k))$.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): the implicit function theorem, interior case (first form)

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: Let $X$ be an M-polyfold with $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle and $f(x_0) = 0$. Then $f'(x_0) : T_{x_0}X \to Y_{x_0}$ is sc-Fredholm. If it is surjective, there is an open $U \ni x_0$ such that $S(f, U) = \{y \in U \mid f(y) = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of a smooth manifold of dimension the Fredholm index, $f'(y)$ is surjective at every $y \in S(f, U)$, and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$.

lean.statement: `theorem_3_1_22_book`, for $d_X \equiv 0$, an sc-Fredholm section with germ data in tame charts (V3.103) and $f(x_0) = 0$: $f'(x_0)$ is sc-Fredholm in every strong bundle chart around $x_0$ ($\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ the restriction of an sc-operator to sc-subspaces); if $f'(x_0)$ is surjective (`IsLinSurjAt`, the text's hypothesis), there are an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d$ such that at every zero $y \in U$, $f'(y)$ is surjective and Fredholm of index $d = \dim\ker f'(y)$, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a $d$-dimensional manifold without boundary. `theorem_3_1_22_book_ker` adds the last clause: at every $y \in S(f, U)$ on level 1 and through every strong bundle chart around $y$, the kernel of the intrinsic linearization $f'(y) = \Phi_y^{-1} \circ \mathrm{Lin}(\varphi(y)) \circ T\varphi(y) : T_yX \to Y_y$ (`StrongBundle.linIntr`, the same map for any two strong bundle charts, `linIntr_chart_independent`) is $Ti(T_yS(f, U))$ (`ker_linIntr_eq_subTangentRange`). The chart form is kept (`theorem_3_6_8_ker_eq_tangent`, V3.99). The forms first proved are kept: `theorem_3_1_22`, with good position for "surjective" and the filler condition at the nearby zeros, and the first clause on every level, in the chart at $x_0$ and in every strong bundle chart (`theorem_3_1_22_linearization_sc`, `StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm`, V3.46, V3.96).

diff: The last clause holds in $T_yX$ (`theorem_3_1_22_book_ker`, 2026-11-12), with the intrinsic $f'(y)$ (`StrongBundle.linIntr`; V3.78 has its chart forms). It is stated at the points of $S(f, U)$ on level 1, which include the smooth points where the text states it; $T_yS \subseteq T_yX$ is read through $Ti$ (injective, Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21); V2.78). The binder $f(y) = 0$ of the last clause is redundant (it follows from $y \in S(f, U)$) and is kept because `linIntr` takes it. Everything else is the text's statement with its hypothesis "$f'(x_0)$ surjective" (`IsLinSurjAt`) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 384).

The forms first proved read "surjective" as good position (the same at $d_X = 0$, V3.100) and took the filler condition at the nearby zeros, a theorem since (V3.102); the forms with the text's hypotheses are V3.95, V3.101. The first clause is proved on every level, in the chart at $x_0$ by Propositions 3.1.10, 1.1.11 and 3.1.5 in sc form and in every strong bundle chart (V3.46, V3.96). Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis (V3.103, V3.104) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 154, 174, 180, 190–192, 235, 236).

items.title: Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23): the implicit function theorem, boundary case

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23), p. 103 (preprint p. 77)
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $f'(x)$ surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$. Then there is an open $U \ni x$ such that $S(f, U)$ consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold of $X$, with a uniquely determined structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners, the induced one of Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21).

lean.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $U \ni x$ and $d$ such that every zero in $U$ is in good position in a tame chart and a smooth point, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (`theorem_3_1_26'`, V3.95), $d$ being the Fredholm index at every zero in $U$ (`theorem_3_1_26_index`, V3.97). The forms first recorded here: with the nearby zeros in good position as a hypothesis (`theorem_3_1_26_of_nearby`), or under `IsGoodPositionGermFilled` at $x$ (`theorem_3_1_26`).

diff: Proved in full in V3.95, V3.97; the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`theorem_3_1_26_of_nearby`, `theorem_3_1_26`).

Hypotheses of these two forms: the good position of the zeros near $x$ (which is Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54), now a theorem, V3.94), or the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82, a consequence of good position, V3.102). The form with the text's hypotheses is V3.95, with the dimension as the Fredholm index V3.97 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 153, 155, 170, 180).

Tameness of the bundle is read as germ data and good position in tame charts (V3.103), as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, 3.6.6 of the preprint (3.50, 3.51, 3.53) and the 2017 text read it; the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 asks no tameness, and the 2021 text does not define “tame strong bundle”, so for the 2021 text this is our reading (gap G.79). Added after the first edition of this page; updated in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24): the solution set when every zero is in good position

book.label: §3.1, Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24), p. 104 (preprint p. 78)
book.statement: If at every zero $x$ of the sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a tame strong bundle $f'(x)$ is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then the solution set $S = \{f = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and that of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103) at every zero $x$, and $S = \{f = 0\} \ne \emptyset$. Then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension (`IsManifoldWithCornersLoc`, V3.72). The same with good position in the text's sense (sc-complement, V3.47) at every zero, which for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data is the same hypothesis (`corollary_3_1_27_sc`).

diff: **No hypothesis is added** (Findings, Chapter 3, items 156, 157): the global hypothesis, good position at every zero, supplies at every point the nearby good position that the local theorems need. “Tame strong bundle” is read as good position in a tame chart (V3.103), as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.6 of the preprint (3.50, 3.53) and the 2017 text read it, the 2021 text not defining the phrase (gap G.79); $S \ne \emptyset$ is needed by the formal charts (for $S = \emptyset$ the statement is empty). The text names no dimension; the formal one is locally constant (V3.87). Added after the first edition of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) with the text's notion of good position is `corollary_3_1_27_sc`; for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data that hypothesis is equivalent to the project's (`forall_isGoodPositionGermSc_iff`; Findings, Chapter 3, item 213). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms and by open subsets

book.label: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), p. 105 (preprint p. 80); §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 114
book.statement: Used without statement: in the proof of Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), “$X' = \psi(X)$ is tame”; in the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), the chart $\psi \circ \varphi$ onto $\psi(O)$ is a chart of the tame M-polyfold $X$.

lean.statement: For an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : U \to U'$ between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants and a tame retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O$, $\psi \circ r \circ \psi^{-1}$ is a tame retraction of $U'$ onto $\psi(O)$, so $(\psi(O), C', E')$ is a tame retract; on the way $d_{C'} \circ \psi = d_C$, $Dr'(\psi(x)) = D\psi(x)Dr(x)D\psi^{-1}(\psi(x))$, and sc-isomorphisms carry sc-subspaces and sc-splittings. The restriction of a tame retraction to an open subset is tame; an open subset of a tame retract, and the model of a chart restricted to an open set, are tame retracts.

diff: Condition (1) of Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34) is Theorem 1.3.5 (preprint 1.25); condition (2) is transported at the smooth points, where $D\psi(x)$ is an sc-isomorphism, using $D\psi(x)E_x \subseteq E'_{\psi(x)}$ (the one-sided sign argument) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 95, 151). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) with locally constant dimension

book.label: §3.2, Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), p. 106 (preprint p. 81)
book.statement: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) for a fixed dimension $n$: a subset with the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to an $n$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, with the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$.

The dimension may vary from point to point (the solution set of Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57) has locally constant, not constant, dimension; Findings, Chapter 3, item 152); the proof is that of V3.24. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: The re-centring lemma

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 84
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27): $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every $v_0 \in V$. With the data $(\psi, N', Y', V', \tau)$ at $x_0 = \varphi^{-1}(v_0 + \delta(v_0))$, the map $w \mapsto \pi\varphi\psi^{-1}(w + \tau(w))$ has an invertible linearization at $0$, so it is a local diffeomorphism and $\delta$ is regular near $v_0$.

lean.statement: For two graph descriptions of one set $S$ — in a chart $\chi_1$ the graph of $\sigma_1 : V_1 \to Y_1$ over $K_1$ with $\sigma_1$ of class $C^1$ on all of $V_1$, in a chart $\chi_2$ centred at $y = \chi_1^{-1}(v_0 + \sigma_1(v_0))$ the graph of $\sigma_2$ over $K_2$ with $\sigma_2(0) = 0$, $D\sigma_2(0) = 0$ and $C^k$-lifts into level $k$ near $0$ ($K_i$ finite-dimensional, smooth, in good position, $Y_i$ closed complements) — $\dim K_1 = \dim K_2$, and for all $m$, $k$, $\sigma_1$ is $C^k$ into $E_{1,m}$ on a relatively open neighbourhood of $v_0$.

chips: onto by Sard, not by symmetry
diff: The text's step needs $\delta$ differentiable at $v_0$, which fails for general sets (V3.24, first counterexample); here $\sigma_1$ is $C^1$ on $V_1$, which V3.74 arranges by shrinking. The re-centring step as stated, for every pair of data, does not hold as we read it (`not_theorem_3_2_3_recentreStep`: the curve $\{(t^3, t)\}$ in $\mathbb R^2$, the datum `CE.germData_bad` at $(1, 1)$; added 2026-11-09) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 82, 150).

The linearization of $\beta = \pi_1 \circ \chi_1\chi_2^{-1} \circ (1 + \sigma_2)$ at $0$ is injective by the chain rule for the transition and its inverse on level $1$ and the tangency of the graph to the retract; its surjectivity comes from the dimension count by Sard's lemma in fixed dimension, since the symmetric argument would need $\sigma_1$ differentiable into level $1$ at $v_0$ (item 159). The inverse $\beta^{-1}$ is $C^k$ by Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77) with weak hypotheses (V3.90), not by Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72), which would need $d_C(x) = d_C(\beta(x))$. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: The regularity conditions from the data, by re-graphing and shrinking

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 84; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 115
book.statement: The proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) shows that $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every point of $V$ (so that the charts $\pi\varphi$ are compatible); the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) constructs the data at every zero “proceeding as above”.

lean.statement: `exists_isRegular`: let $D$ be data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) of dimension $n$ for $M$ at $x$, and let every point of $M$ in an open $U \ni x$ have data of some dimension. items.title: Good complements whose projection maps the partial quadrant into itself

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 83
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) the set $\Sigma = \{v + y \in C \mid v \in V, y \in Y\}$ is asserted to be relatively open in $C$; the retraction $t(v + w) = v + \delta(v)$ is defined on it.

lean.statement: If the finite-dimensional $N$ is in good position to the partial quadrant $C$ of $E$, there is a continuous projection $\pi : E_0 \to N$ with $\pi(C) \subseteq N \cap C$ whose kernel $Y$ is a good complement of $N$; $Y$ is closed and `ProjectsInto C N Y` ($z \in C$, $k \in N$, $z - k \in Y$ imply $k \in C$). The property is carried by continuous linear isomorphisms respecting the cones.

items.title: Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39): composition with a given conjugation

book.label: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39), p. 116 (preprint p. 93)
book.statement: If the sc-germ $g$ is equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi$ to a basic germ and $s$ is an sc$^+$-germ, there is a strong bundle map $\Psi$ such that $((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1$ is a basic germ.

lean.statement: Let $g : U \to F$ be sc-smooth and conjugated to a basic germ $h$ (conjugation data $\Phi$, V3.13, V3.46), and $s : U \to F_1$ sc-smooth into $F^1$ with $s(0) = 0$. With $t = \Phi[1]_*s$ and $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ there are data of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) for $t_W$ such that $\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t$ near $0$, $\Gamma = \Lambda \circ \Phi^1$ is a strong bundle isomorphism of the shifted structures $E^1 \triangleleft F^1$ with $\Gamma_* = \Lambda_* \circ \Phi^1_*$, and $(\Gamma(u, (g + s)^1(u)))_2 = (\Lambda_*(h + t))^1(\gamma(u))$ near $0$, a basic germ; so $(g + s)^1$ is conjugated to a basic germ. Also $\Gamma = (\Lambda_0 \circ \Phi)^1$.

chips: index raise of an iso: proved

items.title: The linearization at a zero in charts, and its chart independence

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111); §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38), p. 57 (preprint p. 42)
book.statement: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) is stated with $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ and the partial cone $C_xX$; Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38) asserts that $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ do not depend on the chart (Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30)). The linearization is defined at the centre of a chart, through a filler.

lean.statement: In a strong bundle chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}$ at every level-$1$ point $z$ of the retract; at a zero it takes values in $K_z = \rho(z)F$ and equals $Dg(z)$ on $T_zO$ for every $g$ sc$^1$ on $U$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$, and for every sc$^1$-germ $g$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$ with $z$ in its germ, $Dg(z)$ the value of its derivative family (`linAt_eq_germDeriv`; at a centre: $Tf(0)$ of Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5), also for a filling germ). For two strong bundle charts of $P$ and an sc-smooth section, at a zero $y$ with level-$1$ points $z$, $z'$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\varphi'(y)$: isomorphisms $A : T_zO \to T_{z'}O'$, $\Gamma : K_z \to K'_{z'}$ with $\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z')A$ and $A$ respecting the partial quadrants; so surjectivity, the Fredholm property and index, and the good position of the kernel do not depend on the chart.

diff: The text does not prove the chart independence of $f'(x)$ or of good position; this is its chart form at zeros (what gap G.13 of Chapter 2 leaves open). Only the fibre derivative of the transition survives at a zero, so away from zeros the linearization is not chart independent. Of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) only the sc-smoothness of the transition on $[0]$ is used; level-$1$ points suffice; no tameness (Findings, Chapter 3, items 110–116). Added after the first edition of this page. (2026-11-09) Gap G.13 is closed in part: $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are defined in $T_xX$, independent of the chart (`reducedTangentFiber_eq`, `partialConeFiber_eq`); this statement is not restated with them.

For filling germs (the germ reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11)) $Dg(z)$ is meaningful only for $z$ in the germ; the consumers use it at the centre and at the level-$1$ lifts of nearby zeros, which lie in the germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 278, 284). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero, from a chart not centred there

book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54): at every zero $y$ near $x$, $f'(y)$ is surjective with kernel in good position, “so that, proceeding as above”, the construction can be repeated at $y$.

diff: The hypothesis is on $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$, not on $\ker Dg(z)$: condition (3) of the filler holds at its centre only, so $\ker Dg(z)$ need not lie in $T_zO$. A dense part of $K_z$ in the range suffices because the range of the linearization in the centred chart is closed (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 111, 117). Added after the first edition of this page.

In the germ reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) the point $z$ must lie in the germ of $g$; the dense form needs the closed range in the target chart, which Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) for germs gives in the tame chart of the germ data, so it is stated there. items.title: Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), given the family of sc-isomorphisms

lean.statement: In coordinates $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $C = \widetilde C \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$: for $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, an open $V_o \ni 0$ with $(b, 0) \in U$ for $b \in V_o \cap \widetilde C$, sc-isomorphisms $L(b)$ with $L(b)h = (Df(b, 0)(0, h))_Y$ and lower bounds $c_m$ on $V_o \cap \widetilde C$, and condition (3) (`DerivCondition`): on $U' = U \cap (V_o \oplus X)$ the push-forward $k = \Phi_*(f - f(0))$ is a basic germ with contraction $H(b, x) = x - L(b)^{-1}(f(b, x) - f(0))_Y$, $\Phi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the identity, and $f - f(0)$ is conjugated to a basic germ.

chips: in the coordinates of the proof

items.title: Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58): the basic germ criterion

book.label: §3.7, Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), p. 140 (preprint p. 116) (proof pp. 140–145 (preprint pp. 116–120))
book.statement: Under (1) $Df(x)$ sc-Fredholm of constant index at smooth points, (2) a splitting $E = B \oplus X$ with $B \supseteq \ker Df(0)$, $Y = Df(0)X$ and a compactness condition, (3) a uniform estimate on $D_2f$: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ.

lean.statement: `theorem_3_7_1_general`: for an sc-splitting $E = B \oplus X$ with $B$ finite-dimensional, $U$ relatively open in a partial quadrant $C$ with $0 \in U$ and $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, with (1) $Df(x)$ sc-Fredholm at every smooth $x \in U$, of the same index at any two (`derivOpAt`); (2) $\ker Df(0) \subseteq B$, $X \subseteq C$ and the compactness condition (`CompactnessCondition371`); (3) the estimate on $D_2f$ (`DerivCondition371`): there is an open $V \ni 0$ such that $f - f(0)$ is conjugated on $U \cap V$ to a basic germ. The target splitting $F = Y \oplus A$ is constructed as in the proof (`exists_targetSplitting371`). The proof reduces to the coordinates of the text's proof, the form first proved (`theorem_3_7_1`, kept, with the conclusions of V3.88): the coordinates $E \cong B \oplus X$ (`ScBanach.splitScIso`) carry $C$ onto $(C \cap B) \oplus X$ with $C \cap B$ a partial quadrant in $B$ (`splitScIso_preimage`, `isPartialQuadrant_of_isScSplitting`); the hypotheses pass to the conjugate $T \circ f \circ S^{-1}$ (`isScFredholm_of_conj`, `compactnessCondition_conj`, `derivCondition_conj`), and the conclusion passes back (`IsConjugateToBasicGerm.of_scIso`).

diff: Condition (3) is printed for $h \in E_m$; $D_2f$ is the derivative along $X$, so it is read for $h \in X_m$: $\|Df(b)h - Df(b + x)h\|_m \le \varepsilon\|h\|_m$ for $b \in B$, $\|b\| < r$, $x \in X_{m+1}$, $\|x\|_m < r$ and $b, b + x \in U_{m+1}$, with $r$ depending on $m$ and $\varepsilon$, as in the text.

In (2), "for $b \in B \cap U$ small enough" is read with one radius for all levels, the text's order of quantifiers (Findings, Chapter 3, item 385); since $B \subseteq E_\infty$ is finite-dimensional this is no restriction. The limit of the convergent subsequence lies in $X_m$ because $X_m$ is closed.

A smooth point $x \in U$ in (1) is a point of $U \cap E_\infty$, and $Df(x)$ is the sc-operator built from the derivative (`derivOpAt`); "constant index" is equality of the indices at any two smooth points.

The form in the coordinates of the proof is kept (`theorem_3_7_1`): there (1) is used only at the points $(b, 0)$, and "$B \supseteq \ker Df(0)$, $Y = Df(0)X$" is replaced by the bijectivity it implies; the text's "injective sc-Fredholm of index $0$, hence an sc-isomorphism" is the block index formula, and Lemmas 3.7.2, 3.7.3 (preprint 3.59, 3.60) are applied with their hypotheses derived from (2) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 73). book.statement: For $U$ relatively open and convex in a partial quadrant $C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with $\|Df - 1\| \le \tfrac12$, $f(0) = 0$ and $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$: $f(U)$ is relatively open and $f : U \to f(U)$ is a smooth diffeomorphism (Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77): the inverse is differentiable with $Dg = [Df \circ g]^{-1}$).

items.title: Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18): parametrized perturbations

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: Let $P : Y \to X$ be a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section. If $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ defines an sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle $\pi^*(P) : \pi^*Y \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.

lean.statement: For any strong bundle $P : Y \to X$, an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and sc$^+$-sections $s_1, \dots, s_n$: with $\mathbb R^n$ the M-polyfold with the constant sc-structure and the translation charts, $\pi(r, x) = x$, and $\pi^*P$ the pull-back strong bundle with the natural structure of Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), $F(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ (computed in $P^{-1}(x)$) is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$. items.title: The linearization of the parametrized section

book.label: §3.1, after Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 101 (preprint p. 75)
book.statement: The linearization of $\tilde f(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ at $(0, x_0)$ is $(h, u) \mapsto f'(x_0)u + \sum_i h_ie_i$, $e_i = s_i(x_0)$.

lean.statement: In the product chart $(r \mapsto r - r_0) \times c$ of $\pi^*P$, $c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ with $0$ in its retract, at the centre: $D(\hat F \circ (1 \times r))(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = D(\hat G \circ r)(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, $\hat G = \hat f + \sum_i r_{0,i}\hat s_i$; in the chart form of the linearization, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_{f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i}(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, and at $r_0 = 0$, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta r, \xi) = \mathrm{Lin}_f(0)\xi + \sum_i\delta r_i\hat s_i(0)$.

book.statement: For every zero $y$ near $x$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective; “property (4) follows from Corollary 3.41 and from Lemma 3.55”.
