items.title: The index of the linearization at a zero, in every chart

book.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), p. 135 (preprint p. 110); Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)); “the linearization $f'(x_0)$ is a sc-Fredholm operator” (Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19)).

lean.statement: `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`: in every strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point over $\varphi(y)$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is onto, Fredholm, $\mathrm{ind} = \dim\ker = d$. For an sc-smooth section and the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at a zero $x_0$ with conjugation data of $g - s$ to a basic germ $O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$: in every chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of index $n - N$, onto if the germ is in good position; so `IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 (n − N)` at a zero in good position. For an sc-Fredholm section in good position, in the chart of Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53): $\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Tf(x_0) = \dim\ker Tf(x_0) = n - N$ for every conjugation. In sc form: for an sc-Fredholm section, a zero $y$ and **any** strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$ (a smooth point), $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, Fredholm on every level of the index $n - N$ of every conjugation of every germ datum at $y$; under `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d` it is onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level. In the chart of Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero in good position, $Dg(0)$ and $f'(x_0) = Tf(x_0)$ are sc-Fredholm and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level.

chips: sc-Fredholm on every level, in charts
diff: Proved in sc form, in every chart: the level-$0$ conjugation between the linearizations in two charts (V3.78) is realised by bounded operators on the ambient spaces that preserve the levels at smooth points (derivatives of the sc-smooth transition maps, and the fibre part of the strong bundle transition, sc$^0$ on $Y[0]$), so the regularity of the linearization in the chart of the germ (V3.46) passes to every chart; then the criterion of V1.8. Tameness is not used. $T_xX$ itself carries no linear structure here (G.7), so the operator is read in charts. The passage to every chart is the chart independence at zeros, which the text does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, items 170, 236, 239). Added in the second addendum of this page with the level-$0$ Fredholm property only (G.22); updated in the third addendum. (2026-11-09: $T_xX$ now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at smooth points, gap G.7 closed (V2.19); this statement is not restated with it.)

**Germs.** The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): the germ data of the sc-Fredholm section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13, V3.16), and Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) enters at the centre of the chart of the germ datum, where $\mathrm{Lin}(0) = Dg(0)$ on $T_0O$ for the filling germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 284, 310, 314, 330). `theorem_3_1_22_linearization_sc` gives the conclusions in the chart at $x_0$, and `linAt_isScFredholm_of_isSurjLinOfIndex` with `IsGoodPositionGerm.exists_isSurjLinOfIndex` in every chart. Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the hypothesis): the index on every level, and the surjectivity on every level at a zero in good position, in every chart, go beyond the text’s statement.

items.title: The dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74); §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 115
book.statement: The solution set $S(f, U)$ has the structure of a smooth manifold “whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index” (Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19)); with $d = \dim\ker f'(x)$ the solution set has the $d$-dimensional tangent germ property (proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54)).

lean.statement: For an sc-smooth section and a zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): the data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) at $x_0$ have a dimension $d$ with `IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 d`, also the regular data of Theorem 3.6.8 (2) (preprint 3.54). For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data: an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d$ with every zero $y \in U$ in good position in a tame chart, `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`, and $S(f, U)$ a tame $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (`theorem_3_1_26_index`; without boundary if $d_X \equiv 0$, `theorem_3_1_22_index`); under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57), regular data at every zero whose dimension is the index at the zeros of their chart domain (`theorem_3_6_11_index`). For an sc-Fredholm section, at a zero $y$ with `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`, in every chart $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is moreover sc-Fredholm and onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level.

chips: at every zero, in every chart
diff: $d = \dim\ker D(h + t)(0) = n - N$ for the conjugation from which the chart of the tangent germ data is built, and $n - N$ is the index of $f'(x_0)$ for the same conjugation (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)); the proofs of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) had to expose that conjugation (`_conj` forms). The index is stated at every zero near the point and in every chart; the text states no dimension in Theorems 3.1.26 and 3.6.11 (preprint 3.23 and 3.57) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 170). Added in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).
That $d$ is the index on every level of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, in every chart, is V3.96 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 239). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

(2026-11-09) The dimension as a submanifold (Definition 4.2.1, Remark 9.1.1): near a zero in good position the solution set is a smooth submanifold with $\dim T_y(S \cap V) = d$ at a zero where $f'(y)$ is onto of index $d$ (`hasDimAt_solutionSet_inter`), an $n$-dimensional submanifold with $n$ the index near $x_0$ (`theorem_3_6_8_isSubmanifoldOfDim`), and globally when every zero is in good position with index $d$ (`isSubmanifoldOfDim_solutionSet`) (`Chapter9/MathlibSolutionSets.lean`).

items.title: The Fredholm index along the solution set and along paths (Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2))

book.label: Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), pp. 237–240 (preprint pp. 200–201); Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), p. 240 (preprint p. 201)
book.statement: Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1): at a smooth point $x$, $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$ is the Fredholm index of $(f - s)'(x)$ for a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$; it does not depend on $s$. Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2): over a tame M-polyfold, if $x_0$, $x_1$ are smooth points connected by an sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$, then $\mathrm{ind}(f, x_0) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x_1)$. In Chapter 3 the statement along the solution set is implicit in Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54).

lean.statement:
For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $V_x 
i x_0$ and $d$ with `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d` at every zero $y \in V_x$, so $\mathrm{ind}\,f'(y) = \dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(x_0)$. With Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54): every zero in $V_x$ in good position in a tame chart, and regular data of dimension $d$ at $x_0$ with chart domain $V_x$. In sc form: at every zero $y \in V_x$, in **every** strong bundle chart around $y$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO 	o K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, onto on every level and of index $d$ on every level; at any zero of an sc-Fredholm section, in every chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm with the same index on every level (`StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm`). **Without good position, with the text’s hypotheses**: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and $f(x_0) = 0$, there are an open $V 
i x_0$ and $i \in \mathbb Z$ such that at every zero $y \in V$, in every strong bundle chart around $y$, $f'(y)$ is Fredholm of index $i$ (`IsLinOfIndex`; `index_locally_constant_tame`), and in sc form $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm of index $i$ on every level (`theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_general_tame`); neither good position, nor surjectivity at $x_0$, nor bump functions are assumed (the first forms, for $X$ admitting sc-smooth bump functions (Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9)): `index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions`, `theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_general`). **Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1)** (`StrongBundle.IsIndexAtLocal f x i`, with the text’s locally defined section): there are an open $V 
i x$ and an sc$^+$-section $s$ of the restriction $P|V$ (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`) with $(f|_V + s)(x) = 0$ and $(f|_V + s)'(x)$ Fredholm of index $i$ in every strong bundle chart of $P|V$; for an sc-Fredholm section the index is unique (`IsIndexAtLocal.unique`), at a zero it is the index of $f'(x)$, and it exists at every smooth point (`exists_isIndexAtLocal`). The reading with an sc$^+$-section on all of $X$ (`StrongBundle.IsIndexAt`; unique, `IsIndexAt.unique`; existing at every smooth point if $X$ admits bump functions, `exists_isIndexAt`) implies it, and is the same notion when $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions (`isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt`). **Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2)** (`proposition_6_2_2_local`): if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data, then for every sc-smooth path $\varphi : \mathbb R 	o X$ there is $i$ with $\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t)) = i$ for all $t$, and any two values of the index at $\varphi(0)$ and $\varphi(1)$ agree (`proposition_6_2_2_local'`); if $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions, the same holds for the global reading (`proposition_6_2_2`). **On $[0, 1]$** (`proposition_6_2_2_interval`): $[0, 1]$ is a tame M-polyfold with boundary (`unitIntervalPolyfold`, two charts onto $[0, 1) \subseteq [0, \infty)$, degeneracy index $1$ at $0$ and $1$), and for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and an sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] 	o X$, $\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t))$ (local sections, Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1)) is one integer for all $t$; in the text's form, $\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(0)) = \mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(1))$ (`proposition_6_2_2_interval'`); with the 2021 definitions, `proposition_6_2_2_interval_2021def`. The proof reparametrizes: $\varphi \circ \sin^2 : \mathbb R 	o X$ is sc-smooth (`exists_rn_reparam`), and the statement on $\mathbb R$ applies; paths on $\mathbb R$ are the special case `proposition_6_2_2_interval_of_rn`.

diff: Updated (2026-11-09): **paths on $[0, 1]$**: the project now has the M-polyfold $[0, 1]$ (`Chapter3/UnitIntervalPolyfold.lean`), and Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) holds for sc-smooth paths $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$ (`proposition_6_2_2_interval`, `Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsInterval.lean`), by the reparametrization $\varphi \circ \sin^2$ on $\mathbb R$. The form on $\mathbb R$ is kept (`proposition_6_2_2`, `proposition_6_2_2_local`). Tameness of $X$ is not used. The hypotheses on $f$ are the text's in the project's reading of tameness (V3.103); the part of gap G.65 concerning Proposition 6.2.2 is closed (Findings, Chapter 3, item 381).

**Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) is proved with the text’s hypotheses** (fifth addendum of this page; in the fourth, with bump functions), by the text’s device run on the restriction $P|V$ of $P$ to the domain $V$ of a strong bundle chart around $\varphi(t_0)$ (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`), for each $t_0$: an sc$^+$-section $S$ of the pull-back to $\mathbb R \times V$ with $\tilde f + S = 0$ along the graph of the path near $t_0$ (the text’s $s(t, x) = R(x, f(\varphi(t)))$ in the chart, with no cut-off, since the chart covers $V$), the local constancy of the index of $\tilde f + S$ along its zero set (stabilizing sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$ in the product chart, again without cut-off, and the implicit function theorem), the index count $\mathrm{ind}(\tilde f + S)'(t, x) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x) + 1$ through the slice $S(t, \cdot)$ (`isIndexAt_of_pullback_isLinOfIndex`), and the connectedness of $\mathbb R$ (`proposition_6_2_2_local`). No bump functions are assumed (“we do not need a sc-smooth partition of unity”, preprint p. 202); tame germ data are the project’s reading of the text’s tameness (V3.103), as in V3.94, where they are no narrowing. With bump functions the proposition holds for the global reading of Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) as well (`proposition_6_2_2`, the form of the fourth addendum, whose section along the path is cut off by a bump; `exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path`) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340–349, 360–367).

**Formerly “narrower”.** The path was $\varphi : \mathbb R \to X$, not $[0, 1] \to X$, since $\mathbb R \times X$ is the product of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) and the project had no M-polyfold $[0, 1]$; a path on $[0, 1]$ that extends sc-smoothly to $\mathbb R$ was covered. Since 2026-11-09 every path sc-smooth on $[0, 1]$ in the sense of M-polyfolds with boundary is covered; the text's tame M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ is still not used, the reparametrized path on $\mathbb R$ replacing it.

Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) has no row of its own. It is `IsIndexAtLocal`: the text’s locally defined sc$^+$-section is a section of the restriction $P|V$ to an open $V \ni x$ — the restriction of a strong bundle to an open set, which the text uses without comment, is constructed (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`, whose atlas consists of the charts of $P$ inside $V$) — and the text’s $f - s$, $s(x) = f(x)$, is written $f + s$, $(f + s)(x) = 0$. It is well defined, two local sections being compared on the intersection of their domains (`IsIndexAtLocal.unique`), and it exists at every smooth point without bump functions, through the section $-R(\cdot, f(x))$ on a chart domain (`exists_isIndexAtLocal`). The global reading `IsIndexAt` of the fourth addendum implies it, and when $X$ admits bump functions the two agree, the local section being cut off (`isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt`). The independence of $s$ is proved from the germ data and Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), without the text’s appeal to Proposition 1.1.11 (preprint 1.10), for which the project has no lemma that the linearization of an sc$^+$-section is compact (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340, 364, 367).

Along the solution set the formal proof combines the good position of the nearby zeros (V3.94), the local constancy of the dimension (V3.85) and dimension = index at each zero (V3.97); the text’s proof of Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) uses the step of V3.82 for an extended section, which along solution sets is repaired by V3.93 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 171, 188). Added in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The sc form (the index of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, on every level, in every chart) is proved as well; that $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm at every zero in every chart, with the level-$0$ index on every level, is `StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm` (V3.96), cited here since the fifth addendum. **The local constancy without good position holds with the text’s hypotheses** (tame germ data, no bump functions; `index_locally_constant_tame`, in sc form `theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_general_tame`), by the text’s device for Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) on the restriction $P|V$ to a chart domain: finitely many sc$^+$-sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$, which on $P|V$ need no cut-off, put the parametrized section of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) into general position at $(0, x_0)$, its index is constant along its solution set (the case above), at $(0, y)$ it is $k + \operatorname{ind} f'(y)$, and the index at a zero is the same for $P$ and $P|V$, through the germ datum (Findings, Chapter 3, items 240–242, 360–363). The first proof, for M-polyfolds admitting bump functions (Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) for the sections), is kept (`index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions`). The candidate counterexample of items 188 and 243 is excluded under tame germ data by Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54). Without tame germ data the question is open: $\operatorname{ind} f'(y) = \operatorname{ind} f'(x_0)$ iff the block $C(z) = (1 - \rho(z))Dg(z)|_{\ker Dr(z)}$ of the filling has index $0$, which condition (3) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) gives at $z = 0$ only (items 243, 343). Updated in the third, fourth and fifth addenda of this page.

book.statement: $U$ can be chosen such that for $y \in S(f, U)$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$ is the tangent space.

items.title: Good position is surjectivity at a zero with $d_X = 0$

book.label: §3.6, after Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), p. 136 (preprint p. 111); Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24), preprint p. 79
book.statement: “In case $\partial X = \emptyset$, the requirement that $(f, x)$ is in good position just means that $f'(x)$ is surjective”; the kernel condition is “an empty condition if $d_X(x) = 0$” (Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24)).

items.title: Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 and 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53) in a tame chart

book.label: §3.6, Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.50, 3.51), p. 135 (preprint p. 110); Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111)
book.statement: (3.50) For an sc-smooth section $f$ of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and a smooth point $x$: $(f, x)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if there is a strong bundle chart $\Phi : \Phi^{-1}(V) \to K$ around $x$ covering $\varphi : (V, x) \to (O, 0)$, “where $K \to O$ is a tame strong local bundle”, in which the local section has a filling $g$ near $0$ and a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ and $g - s$ conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ. (3.51) An sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle is sc-Fredholm if it is regularizing and an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point. (3.53) Good position is defined for an sc-Fredholm germ of a tame strong bundle. A strong bundle retraction is tame when its base retraction $r$ is (preprint p. 49).

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsTameChart`: a strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas whose base retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame (Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34)). `IsScFredholmGermTame f x` (“tame germ data”): $x$ smooth and the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) in the text’s germ reading (V3.13) in a tame chart. `IsGoodPositionGermTame f x`: the same data with the germ in good position in that chart (V3.47). `IsScFredholmSectionTame f`: an sc-Fredholm section (V3.16) with tame germ data at every smooth point. Each implies the form without tameness; good position in a tame chart gives tame germ data; `IsGoodPositionGermFilled` (V3.82) is stated in a tame chart. A retraction agreeing on its domain with a tame one is tame, so a compatible chart whose base retraction is the identity of $U$ is tame.

chips: tame chart of the germ data
diff: Updated (2026-11-09): **which text the tame reading follows.** The reading in a tame chart is the wording of Definition 3.6.3 in the preprint (3.50) and in the 2017 text, “where $K \to O$ is a tame strong local bundle”. The 2021 Definition 3.6.3 (p. 135) says “strong local bundle”, without “tame”, while Theorem 3.6.8 and the later theorems say “tame strong bundle”, a phrase the 2021 text does not define (it defines a tame strong bundle retraction, p. 65); for the 2021 text the tame-chart reading is our reading of that phrase. With the 2021 filling it is `IsScFredholmGermTame2021`, the 2017 germ (`isScFredholmGermTame2021_iff_2017`). Germ data in a chart centred at a point of the interior of $C$ are tame germ data after shrinking the chart (`isScFredholmGermTame_of_chart_interior`), so there the theorems hold for the plain 2021 notion; charts with $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) \ge 1$ are open (gap G.79; Findings, Chapter 3, item 382).

These are the hypotheses of the implicit function theorems of §3.6 (V3.48, V3.68–V3.70, V3.80–V3.82, V3.84–V3.87, V3.94–V3.102). They were first proved with “tame strong bundle” read as: the base retraction of **every** strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies that (V3.104), so those first statements were vacuous; the proofs used the tameness only for particular charts, and the repair changed the statements, not the arguments (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192, 198).

Whether germ data in some chart (V3.13) can be moved to some compatible tame chart when the atlas consists of tame charts (Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) $\Rightarrow$ Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50)) is open. It cannot be done by re-centring a chart of the tame atlas: whether a filling exists in a chart depends on the chart ($\ker Dr(0) \cong \ker\rho(0)$ is necessary, `IsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv`), and the trivial bundle with the one-chart tame atlas of `evenBundleChart` has sc-Fredholm sections with tame germ data in compatible charts but none in the atlas chart (`tame_atlas_no_germData_in_atlas_chart`). The preprint and the 2017 text build the tame chart into Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50); the 2021 text asks it of the bundle in the theorems (“tame strong bundle”), see the first entry (Findings, Chapter 3, items 199, 350–353). Updated in the fourth addendum of this page.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the three notions carry the germ data of the text (V3.13, V3.45); the earlier whole-chart forms are `IsScFredholmGermTameWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermTameWholeChart`, `IsScFredholmSectionTameWholeChart`, and the non-vacuity witnesses satisfy both readings (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 304, 330). For Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) the comparison is that of V3.47. Hence “hypotheses explicit” again (“restated” in the third addendum).

(2026-11-12) With the 2021 definitions as printed (germ data in any strong bundle chart) the conclusion does not hold as we read it, also over an M-polyfold without boundary (`theorem_3_6_8_untamed_not`, `theorem_3_1_22_untamed_not`; V3.130, gap G.79 settled).

(2026-11-12) The open question of the third entry is answered in the negative: a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ of a tame strong bundle need not have germ data in a tame chart (`isScFredholmGerm2021_not_tame`, V3.131).

items.title: A non-tame retraction onto a product with a point: the earlier tameness hypothesis cannot be met

book.label: no counterpart in the text (Definitions 2.5.2, 2.6.4 (preprint 2.34, 2.50), pp. 53–54, 67–68 (preprint pp. 39–40, 51–52))
book.statement: Not in the text. Definition 2.5.2 (1) (preprint 2.34) asks a tame retraction to preserve the degeneracy index, $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$; Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) asks of compatible strong bundle charts only that their transition maps be sc-smooth.

lean.statement: For an sc-Banach space $W$, the constant retraction $c : (a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)$ of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of $\mathbb R \oplus W$ (sc-smooth, with retract $\{(1, 0)\}$), and every sc-smooth retraction $r$ of a nonempty relatively open $U$ in a partial quadrant $C$: the product retraction $c \times r$, with retract $\{(1, 0)\} \times r(U)$, is not tame. At $((0, 0), u)$, $u \in r(U)$, the degeneracy index is $1 + d_C(u)$, at its image $((1, 0), u)$ it is $d_C(u)$.

diff: The retraction-level half of the argument that the hypothesis under which the theorems of §3.6 were first proved, “the base retraction of every compatible strong bundle chart is tame”, fails for every strong bundle over a nonempty base: from a compatible chart $(\varphi, U, R, \Phi)$, the chart $(1, \varphi)$ onto $\{1\} \times O$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ (the retraction above with $W = 0$) has the transition maps of the first composed with affine maps, hence is compatible with every chart the first one is. That chart and its compatibility are not formalized (sc-calculus for affine maps). So the earlier statements were vacuous, and they are replaced by those with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190, 199). Added after the repair of the tameness hypothesis.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) for tame germ data

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), p. 98 (preprint p. 71); recalled after Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51), p. 135 (preprint p. 110)
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section of the tame strong bundle and $s$ an sc$^+$-section, then $f + s$ is an sc-Fredholm section.

lean.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103) and $s$ an sc$^+$-section, then $f + s$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data: at every smooth point the germ data of $f + s$ lie in the tame chart of those of $f$ (filling germ $g + \hat s \circ r$, sc$^+$-germ $\hat s_1 \circ r + t_0$, the same conjugation; V3.17).

diff: Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) for the tame reading of Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.50, 3.51) (V3.103); the proof of V3.17 does not change the chart (Findings, Chapter 3, item 195). Added after the repair of the tameness hypothesis.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) for tame germ data

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: Let $P : Y \to X$ be a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section. If $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle $\pi^*(P) \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.

lean.statement: In the setting of V3.91: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103) and $s_1, \dots, s_n$ are sc$^+$-sections, then $F(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$ with tame germ data. On the way: the product chart $(r \mapsto r - r_0) \times c$ (V3.92), with base retraction $1 \times r$ on $\mathbb R^n \times U$, is tame when $r$ is ($\mathbb R^n$ carries the identity retraction, so $d(a, u) = d_C(u)$, and minimal subspaces and tangent spaces are products); so $\tilde f$ has germ data in the tame product charts, and V3.105 adds $\tilde s$.

chips: product of tame charts is tame
diff: The tame form of V3.91, which is what the implicit function theorems of §3.6 need when applied to $F$; the tameness of the base $\mathbb R^n \times X$ (`prod_rn_isTame`, V3.91) is a different statement (Findings, Chapter 3, item 195). Added after the repair of the tameness hypothesis.

items.title: Good position in any chart of the germ data

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111); proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 115
book.statement: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) defines good position through $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ and $C_xX$, presupposing that it does not depend on the chart; the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) concludes good position at the nearby zeros “proceeding as above”.

lean.statement: (a) In the setting of V3.79 (a zero $y$, a chart $c$ around $y$ not necessarily centred, an sc$^1$-germ $g$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ on $O$ near $\varphi(y)$ with $z$ in its germ, $Dg(z)$ mapping $T_zO$ onto $K_z$, $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$ in good position to $C_{\varphi(y)}$ inside $T_zO$): for **every** datum of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at $y$ (a compatible chart $c'$ centred at $y$, a filling germ $g'$ with a derivative family $Dg'$), the germ is in good position in $c'$ at $Dg'(0)$; with only $\rho(z)k$ in the range for every smooth $k$, under the hypothesis that $Dg'(0)$ is Fredholm. (b) If $(f, y)$, $f(y) = 0$, is in good position in some chart and has tame germ data, it is in good position in that tame chart.

chips: every chart of the germ data
diff: V3.79 gives the good position in the chart that Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) provides at $y$; (a) gives it in every chart carrying germ data, and (b) applies (a) at $z = 0$ in the chart of the given good position. This is how the good position of the nearby zeros (V3.94) and the good position from surjectivity (V3.100) are obtained in tame charts (Findings, Chapter 3, items 193, 194). Added after the repair of the tameness hypothesis.

In the germ reading (b) needs no Fredholm input: in the chart of the given good position, centred at $y$, (a) applies at $z = 0$, which lies in every germ, and $K_0$ is the whole target, so the form with all of $K_z$ in the range suffices. The whole-chart form of (a) is `isGoodPositionAt_of_chart_dense` (Findings, Chapter 3, item 301). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Definitions 3.1.4 and 3.6.1 (preprint 3.4 and 3.48): the 2021 filling

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4), p. 91 (preprint p. 64); §3.6, Definition 3.6.1 (preprint 3.48), p. 134 (preprint p. 109)
book.statement: For $K = R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$ covering the sc-smooth retraction $r$ with $r(0) = 0$, an sc-smooth section germ $(g, 0)$ fills $(f, 0)$ if (1) $f = g$ on $O$ near $0$, (2) $y$ near $0$ with $g(y) = \rho(r(y))g(y)$ lies in $O$, (3) the linearization of $[1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ at $0$ restricted to $\ker Dr(0)$ is an isomorphism onto $\ker\rho(0)$. The 2017 text asks $r$ to be tame; the 2021 text does not.

lean.statement: The same, as a germ on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods inside $U$, with $r(0) = 0$ a condition. It is the filling of V3.7 plus $r(0) = 0$ (automatic when $0 \in O$); the 2017 filling (tame $r$) implies it; the identity retraction gives fillings.

diff: The 2021 change brings the text to the germ reading of V3.7, which never asked for tameness.

book.label: no counterpart in the text (Definition 3.1.4, p. 91, and its 2017 form)

items.title: Definitions 3.1.11, 3.1.16 = 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.11, 3.14 = 3.50, 3.51) with the 2021 filling

book.label: §3.1, Definitions 3.1.11, p. 96, and 3.1.16, p. 97 (preprint 3.11, 3.14, pp. 69–70); §3.6, Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, p. 135 (preprint 3.50, 3.51, p. 110)
book.statement: $(f, x_0)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if, in a strong bundle chart centred at the smooth $x_0$, the principal part has a filling $g$ and an sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ makes $g - s$ conjugate to a basic germ; an sc-Fredholm section is sc-smooth, regularizing, and an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point.

lean.statement: The same with the 2021 filling; the 2021 germ is the project's sc-Fredholm germ, the 2021 section the project's sc-Fredholm section, the 2017 germ the germ with tame germ data; graph sections are witnesses.

diff: Whether every 2021 sc-Fredholm germ has germ data in a tame chart is gap G.79 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 353). (2026-11-09) In part: 2021 germ data in a chart centred at a point of the interior of $C$, i.e. with $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) = 0$, give tame germ data and the 2017 germ (`IsScFredholmGermInterior.isScFredholmGermTame`, `IsScFredholmGermInterior.isScFredholmGerm2017`), and a 2021 sc-Fredholm section with such data at every smooth point has tame germ data (`isScFredholmSectionTame_of_interior`); the case $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) \ge 1$ is open. items.title: Closed convex cones and extreme rays (p. 145)

book.label: §3.8.1.3, p. 145 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: A closed convex cone $P$ in a finite-dimensional $N$: closed, convex, $P \cap (-P) = \{0\}$, $\mathbb R_+P = P$; an extreme ray is $\mathbb R_+x$, $x \in P \setminus \{0\}$, with $y, x - y \in P$ implying $y \in \mathbb R_+x$.

lean.statement: The same definitions, with witnesses; and for $N$ in good position with $N \cap C$ pointed, $N \cap C$ is carried onto $[0, \infty)^{\dim N}$ by a linear isomorphism.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.4

book.statement: If $N \cap C$ is a closed convex cone: (1) $y \in N^\perp$ has $y_i = 0$ for $i \in \sigma_a$, $a$ an extreme-ray generator; (2) $\Gamma$ is the union of the $\sigma_a$ over extreme-ray generators; (3) $y_i = 0$ for $y \in N^\perp$, $i \in \Gamma$.

items.title: Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36): the quantitative solution germ

book.label: §3.3, Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36), p. 113 (preprint p. 89)
book.statement: Decreasing sequences $(\varepsilon_i)$, $(\tau_i)$ with: $\delta$ on $\{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_0\}$ a continuous solution, unique for $|w|_0 \le \tau_0$; $\delta(a) \in W_i$, $|\delta(a)|_i \le \tau_i$ for $|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i$; $\delta : \{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i\} \to W_i$ of class $C^i$.

lean.statement: `remark_3_3_8`: for an sc⁰-contraction germ $f(a, w) = w - B(a, w)$ that is sc-smooth, on a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$, there are $\delta$ and decreasing positive sequences $(\varepsilon_i)$, $(\tau_i)$ such that $\delta(0) = 0$; on $\{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_0\}$, $\delta$ is continuous with $|\delta(a)|_0 \le \tau_0$ and $f(a, \delta(a)) = 0$; a solution $w$ with $|w|_0 \le \tau_0$ is $\delta(a)$; $\delta(a) \in W_i$ and $|\delta(a)|_i \le \tau_i$ for $|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i$; and $\delta : \{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i\} \to W_i$ is of class $C^i$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.1 (preprint 3.62): a closed convex cone is the closed convex hull of its extreme rays

book.label: §3.8.1, Lemma 3.8.1 (preprint 3.62), p. 145 (preprint p. 121)
book.statement: A closed convex cone $P$ in a finite-dimensional vector space $N$ is the closed convex hull of its extreme rays (a version of the Krein–Milman theorem, cited from the literature).

lean.statement: `lemma_3_8_1`: for a closed convex cone $P \ne \{0\}$ in a finite-dimensional space, $P$ is the closure of the convex hull of the union of its extreme rays (`extremeRays`; an extreme ray is a set, `IsExtremeRay`, equivalent to the project's generator form, `IsClosedConvexCone.isExtremeRay_rayOf_iff`). `not_lemma_3_8_1_zero`: the statement for every closed convex cone does not hold as we read it, at $P = \{0\}$. `lemma_3_8_1_zero_union`: with $0$ adjoined to the extreme rays it holds for every closed convex cone.

diff: As printed the lemma does not hold as we read it for $P = \{0\}$: $\{0\}$ is a closed convex cone without extreme rays, and the closed convex hull of the empty family is empty (`not_lemma_3_8_1_zero`; Findings, Chapter 3, item 386). items.title: Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10): the section $u \mapsto (1 - p)(u - t(u))$ is sc-Fredholm

book.label: §4.1, Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), pp. 179–181 (preprint pp. 151–153)
book.statement: The section $u \mapsto (u, \mathbf f(u))$, $\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))$, of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm.

lean.statement: `lemma_4_1_11`: in the setting of Proposition 4.1.9 (an sc⁺-retraction $t$ onto $O \ni 0$, $N = T_0O$ in good position, $Y$ a good sc-complement (`hsplit : E.IsScSplitting N Y`), $p$ the projection onto $N$ along $Y$), the section $u \mapsto (u, (1 - p)(u - t(u)))$ of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ (`LocalBundle.bundle`, `LocalBundle.sec`, one chart with the identity strong bundle retraction) is sc-Fredholm in the sense of 2021 Definition 3.1.16 (`IsScFredholmSection2021`), on all of $U$. Regularizing: $u = (1 - p)(u - tu) + tu + p(u - tu)$. Germ at a smooth $e$: the chart centred at $e$ (`LocalBundle.centred`), whose retraction is pointwise the identity, so the principal part fills itself (`isFilling2021_of_R_eq_self`); $s(v) = (1 - p)(e - t(v + e))$ is the text's $s$, and $g - s = (1 - p)v$ is conjugated to the basic germ $(a + b, w) \mapsto (b, w)$ (`isConjugateToBasicGerm_qOp`), with the splitting $E \cong (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$, $B$ smooth, $W = Y \cap \ker L$ (`exists_splitData`, `isScSubspace_splitW`).

diff: The text's "good sc-complement" is the hypothesis `hsplit : E.IsScSplitting N Y` together with the project's `IsGoodComplement`, which keeps only the algebraic splitting; it is a hypothesis of the text, not an added one (satisfiable wherever Proposition 4.1.9 applies, with the closed complement chosen there). No witness of the full data of Proposition 4.1.9 is built.

In the proof, $B$ must lie in $Y_\infty$ for $E = (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$ to be an sc-splitting; such $B$ exists, since $L(Y \cap E_\infty) = L(Y)$ (`map_le_map_smooth`). The text gets "$C \cap (T_0O \oplus B)$ is a partial quadrant" from good position; here it comes from the corner coordinates on $T_0O \oplus B$, which vanish on $W$. The slips of the printed proof (Findings, item 57) do not enter. Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9), its only use, is proved directly (V4.20).

items.title: Lemma 4.4.8: the Poincaré lemma for sc-forms (p. 199)

book.label: §4.4, Lemma 4.4.8, p. 199 (proof §4.5.3, pp. 202–204) (2021)
book.statement: (New in the 2021 edition.) Every $x \in X$ has open neighbourhoods $V(x) \subseteq U(x)$ such that every closed $[\omega] \in \Omega^k_\infty(U(x))$, $k \ge 1$, has $[\tau] \in \Omega^{k-1}_\infty(V(x))$ with $d[\tau] = [\omega]$ on $V(x)$. The proof applies Lemma 4.5.2 in a chart to $B_\delta(x) \cap C$, working with $C^i \subset E^i$ on the levels.

lean.statement: `lemma_4_4_8 A x`: there are open $V \subseteq U \ni x$ such that for every $k$ every $a \in \Omega^{k+1}_\infty(U)$ with $da = 0$ has $b \in \Omega^k_\infty(V)$ with $db = a|_V$. $U$, $V$ are Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds (`restrictOpen`, bundled as `BundledMPolyfold.openSub`); forms restrict to open subsets, commuting with $d$ (`formRestrict`, `extD_formRestrict`, `formsInftyResOpen`, `formsInftyResOpenOpen`), and "$[\omega] = [\tau]$ on $V$" of (4.7) is `FormsInftyEqOn` (`formsInftyEqOn_of_iff`). The proof is the text's: a chart $\varphi$ and retraction $r$ with $r(B_\delta \cap C) \subseteq B_\varepsilon$ (`exists_poincareChart`), $V(x) = \varphi^{-1}(B_\delta(\varphi x))$, the M-polyfold $O^m$ as the $m$-th lift (`LocalModel.liftEquiv`), Lemma 4.5.2 on $B_\delta(\varphi x) \cap C$ about a smooth centre on every level (`LocalPoincare`, `hasPoincare_lift`, `localPoincare`), and $d(j^*\tau) = (r \circ j)^*\omega$ on the direct limits (`exists_primitive_of_factor`, `lemma_4_4_8_of_local`).

diff: $U(x)$, $V(x)$ are Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds (nonempty, as they contain $x$); "$d[\tau] = [\omega]$ on $V(x)$" is $db = a|_V$; the text's degrees $k \ge 1$, $k - 1$ are $k + 1$, $k$. In the proof Lemma 4.5.2 is applied to the convex set $B_\delta(\varphi(x)) \cap C$, which need not contain $0$, and the remark after Lemma 4.5.2 (a centre $(0, w_0)$) does not cover it; Lemma 4.5.2 is therefore used with the homotopy about any smooth centre, which the same proof gives (V4.96; Findings, Chapter 4, item 177).

items.title: Lemma 4.5.2: the local Poincaré lemma on a convex relatively open set (p. 202)

book.label: Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.2, p. 202 (proof §4.5.3, pp. 202–204) (2021)
book.statement: (New in the 2021 edition.) For $U$ a relatively open convex neighbourhood of $0$ in $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ and a closed sc-form $\omega$ on $U$ of degree $k \ge 1$, there is an sc-form $\tau$ on $U$ with $d\tau = \omega$ on $U^1$; $\tau$ is given by the homotopy formula $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^{k-1}\omega(ty)(y, v)\,dt$.

lean.statement: `hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`: for a local model $M$ with $M.O$ relatively open in the partial quadrant and convex, $0 \in M.O$, and every $k$, every $\sigma \in \Omega^{k+1}(O)$ with $d\sigma = 0$ has $\tau \in \Omega^k(O)$ with $d\tau = \iota^*\sigma$ on $O^1$ (`MPolyfold.HasPoincare`); `hasPoincare_relOpen` is the same about any smooth centre $c \in M.O$. The primitive is the homotopy form $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^k\,\omega(c + t(y - c))(y - c, v)\,dt$ (`homotopyForm`, `relOpenForm`), sc-smooth by the sc-smoothness of parametric integrals over $[0, 1]$ (`isScSmooth_intervalIntegral`, `isSck_intervalIntegral`, `scDeriv_intervalIntegral`, by sc-induction through the tangent map) (`isScSmooth_homotopyForm`); `ambientD_homotopyForm` and `lemma_4_5_2` give $d\tau = \omega$ in the chart, with the local $d$ the `deltaFun` of the derivative and the identity $d_r = $ the ambient $d$ on a relatively open set (`retractD_eq_ambientD`).

diff: The text's degrees $k \ge 1$, $k - 1$ are $k + 1$, $k$; "$d\tau = \omega$ on $U^1$" is $d\tau = \iota^*\omega$ for $\iota : U^1 \to U$, and "closed" is $d\omega = 0$. The printed case is the centre $c = 0$ (`hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`); any smooth centre is allowed (`hasPoincare_relOpen`), which Lemma 4.4.8 needs (V4.95). No hypothesis is added: the hypotheses (convex, relatively open, a smooth centre) are satisfiable, e.g. $D = C = $ the whole space with $c = 0$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 177).

items.title: Definitions 5.3.1 and 5.5.2 (preprint 5.9 and 5.29): sc-smooth bump functions

lean.statement:
`AdmitsBumpFunctions`: $f(x) 
e 0$ and $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U$. `AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak`: Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29) as written, implied by the first. `HasBumpAt`: $x$ is a bump point if every open $U 
i x$ carries an sc-smooth $f$ with $f(x) 
e 0$ and $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U$; the pointwise reading is “every point is a bump point”, and the weak reading follows from “the bump points are dense” (`admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense`). On an sc-Banach space the weak reading gives a bump point at every smooth point (`AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth`); on M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert spaces the pointwise reading holds (`admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`).

diff: Proposition 5.5.3's (preprint 5.30) proof needs $g(x) \ne 0$; without translations a bump cannot be moved to $x$. Whether the weak reading suffices is open at non-smooth points: on an sc-Banach space the weak reading gives a bump at every smooth point (`AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth`; translation by a non-smooth vector does not preserve the levels), on Hilbert models both readings hold everywhere (`admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`), and the weak reading is the density of the bump points (`HasBumpAt`; one direction formalized) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 41, 160–163). On an sc-Banach space this is now settled at every point: a bump at one point is moved to any other by a smooth vector close to the difference, so the bump points are all points or none, and the weak and pointwise readings agree (`MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_iff_admitsBumpFunctions_scPolyfold`; Findings, Chapter 5, item 180); for a general M-polyfold the question stays open. Updated in the fourth addendum of this page.

items.title: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, the allowable sections, and the metric $\rho$

book.label: §5.3, preprint p. 174
book.statement: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$: the $s \in \Gamma^+(P)$ with $\operatorname{supp}(s) \subseteq U$ and $N(s(x)) \le 1$ for all $x$, a metric space for $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, not complete.

lean.statement: `allowableSections N U`; `sectionDistAt`: $N(s(x) - s'(x))$ in the fibre $(Y_{0,1})_x$. `allowableDist`: $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, finite ($\rho \le 2$); for an auxiliary norm $N$ a metric on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ (`allowableMetric`), with $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ iff $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le \varepsilon$ for all $x$. Not complete for the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ with $N(x, v) = |v|$ and $U = \mathbb R$ (`TrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections`); complete for $U = \emptyset$, for every bundle and auxiliary norm (`completeSpace_allowableSections_empty`), and over a point with fibre $\mathbb R^k$ (`TrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point`).

diff: The text’s “$(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is not complete” does not hold as we read it without a hypothesis: for $U = \emptyset$ the space is a point, and over a point with finite-dimensional fibre it is the closed unit ball of $\mathbb R^k$. It is read as “not complete in general” and proved by an example: the allowable sections $s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))$ form a $\rho$-Cauchy sequence whose pointwise limit has fibre part $|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})$, not differentiable at $0$, while the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is $C^1$. That non-completeness holds whenever $U$ contains a non-isolated point over which $Y_{0,1}$ is nonzero (the text’s setting) is expected by the same mechanism and not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153; gap G.42).

Only Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1) is used for the metric axioms (symmetry and subadditivity of the fibre norms, $N$ vanishing only at $0_x$); the density statements of Theorems 5.3.5 and 5.3.10 (preprint 5.13 and 5.18) are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ (`allowableDist_le_iff`; V5.30, V5.39). Hence still “restated”; before the fourth addendum of this page $\rho$ was used pointwise only and the metric space was not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, item 47).

items.title: Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12)

book.label: §5.3, Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12), p. 217 (preprint p. 174)
book.statement: If $s$ is in the completion of $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, the solution set of $f + s = 0$ is still compact, provided $f$ has a compact solution set and $U$ is adapted to $N$.

lean.statement: `remark_5_3_4`: if $\operatorname{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ is compact and $s$ vanishes off $U$ with $N(s) \le 1$, the zeros of $f + s$ lie in $\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$, with compact closure. As stated (`remark_5_3_4_completion`): with the points of the completion represented by sections $s$ with values in $Y_{0,1}$ that are uniform $N$-limits of allowable sections (`IsInAllowableCompletion`), for $f$ continuous and $U \supseteq f^{-1}(0)$ with $\operatorname{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ compact, the solution set of $f + s$ is closed, hence compact; for $f$ sc-Fredholm with compact solution set, with the $U$ of Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) (`remark_5_3_4_of_isScFredholmSection`).

diff: The closedness of the solution set, which the remark does not discuss, is proved for every $s$ in the completion by a chart argument: Lemma 5.1.2's (preprint 5.2) bound turns $N(s - s') \le \varepsilon$ into a level-$0$ bound in a chart, and $f + s'$ is continuous for allowable $s'$ (Findings, Chapter 5, item 130; before, only the compact closure, item 27). “Adapted” is read as properness. The completion is represented by sections, uniform $N$-limits of allowable sections; the metric space $(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is V5.21 (fourth addendum), and that every $\rho$-Cauchy sequence has such a limit section is not formalized (items 131, 153). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19): perturbation into good position, relative to $\partial X$

Cubes in $\mathbb R^n$ with $n \ge 2$ and other bounded domains (where, as we read it, a regular boundary is presupposed) are not done; hence narrower.

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Definition 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27), p. 263 (preprint pp. 219–220)
book.statement: An orientation of $(f, x)$, $x$ smooth, is a choice of one of the two orientations of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$. The objects of a category are the sets $\mathrm{Or}^f_x = \{o_x, -o_x\}$; for smooth $x$, $y$ in the same path component the morphisms are the two bijections $\pm o_x \mapsto \pm o_y$ and $\pm o_x \mapsto \mp o_y$.

lean.statement: At a chart point the members of $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ are Fredholm (`ChartPoint.isFredholm_of_mem_linSet`); `ChartPoint.detLin` is the pull-back of $\mathrm{DET}(T_zO, K_z)$ to $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and `ChartPoint.Or` the type of its orientations, with exactly two elements (`ChartPoint.exists_two_or`); for $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, $o \mapsto o(L)$ is a bijection onto the two orientations of $\det(L)$ (`ChartPoint.orEquivRay`). Between two two-element types there are bijections, and one value determines a bijection (`nonempty_equiv_of_two`, `equiv_eq_of_apply_eq_of_two`).

items.title: Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28): the neighbourhoods $U(x)$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28), p. 263 (preprint p. 220) (proof pp. 263–264 (preprint pp. 220–221))
book.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section $f$, every smooth $x$ has open neighbourhoods $U' \subseteq U$ with (1) $U'$ is sc-smoothly contractible in $U$ to $x$ (2021 and 2017; the preprint: (1) $U$ is sc-smoothly contractible); (2) $\{y \in \operatorname{cl}_X(U) \mid f(y) = 0\}$ compact; (3) for every sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to U$ an sc⁺-section $s : U \times [0, 1] \to Y$ with $s(\varphi(t), t) = f(\varphi(t))$; (4) for $t_0 \in [0, 1]$, $y_0 \in U_\infty$ and a smooth $e_0 \in Y_{y_0}$ an sc⁺-section $q$ with $q(y_0, t_0) = e_0$. The proof contracts $U = r(V')$, $V'$ convex, by $(t, y) \mapsto r(ty)$.

lean.statement: `proposition_6_6_3` (bump functions): open $U \subseteq W$ in the domain of one chart of the atlas with (1′) any two sc-smooth paths in $U$ with the same end points are sc-smoothly homotopic in $W$ with the end points fixed (`IsScHomotopyRel`); (2) $\{y \in \operatorname{cl}(U) \mid f(y) = 0\}$ compact (`exists_nhds_isCompact_zeros`); (3) for every sc-smooth family $\Phi : \mathbb R^n \to X$ with $\Phi([0, 1]^n) \subseteq W$ an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R^n \times X$ with $(f + S)(q, \Phi(q)) = 0$ for $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$, depending on $q \in [0, 1]^n$ only through $\Phi(q)$ (`exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_family`); (4) $\pi^*P$ has sc⁺-sections through all smooth fibre points (`hasScPlusSectionsThrough_pullback_rn_of_bump`). $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and $\pi^*P$ are paracompact (`MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_prod`, `paracompactSpace_pullbackSpace`). `proposition_6_6_3_three_interval`, `proposition_6_6_3_four_interval`: (3) and (4) for paths $[0, 1] \to X$ with sc⁺-sections over the M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$, with $(f + S)(t, \varphi(t)) = 0$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$. `proposition_6_6_3_three_cube`, `proposition_6_6_3_four_cube`: (3), (4) for families $[0,1]^n \to X$ over the M-polyfold with corners $[0,1]^n \times X$ (`cubePolyfold`). (2026-11-13) `proposition_6_6_3_one`: in addition an open $U' \ni x$ in $U$ and an sc-smooth contraction $H : [0, 1] \times X \to X$ of $U'$ in $U$ to $x$ (`IsScContraction`: sc-smooth on $[0, 1] \times U'$, $H(0, \cdot) = x$, $H(1, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$, $H(t, x) = x$), (1) as printed in 2021. `exists_isScHomotopyI`, `proposition_6_6_3_interval`: (1′) for paths $[0, 1] \to U$ with sc-smooth homotopies $[0, 1]^2 \to W$ with the end points fixed (`unitSquarePolyfold`).

The preprint's (1), "$U$ is sc-smoothly contractible", would need $r(V') \subseteq V'$ for $U = r(V')$; it is not formalized, and nothing here shows that it fails. The sections of (3) and (4) are global sc⁺-sections of the pull-back, made with bump functions, in place of sections over $U \times [0, 1]$ after "assuming $X = U$" (the text assumes partitions of unity from §6.3 (preprint §6.2) on); (3) is stated for families, as the homotopies of Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) need it. items.title: Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29): the sections $s_1, \dots, s_k$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the section $F$, preprint p. 221; Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) and the paragraph after it, preprint p. 222
book.statement: With $s(\varphi(t), t) = f(\varphi(t))$ and $F(t, y, \lambda) = f(y) - s(y, t) + \sum\lambda_is_i(y, t)$ on $[0, 1] \times X \times \mathbb R^k$, there are finitely many sc⁺-sections $s_1, \dots, s_k$ with (P): for every fixed $t$, $F_t$ is at $(\varphi(t), 0)$ in general position to the boundary of $X \times \mathbb R^k$. lean.statement: `lemma_6_6_4` ($X$ tame, bump functions, $f$ with tame germ data): for an sc-smooth $\Phi : \mathbb R^n \to X$ and an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P$ with $(f + S)(q, \Phi(q)) = 0$ for $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$, finitely many sc⁺-sections $s_1, \dots, s_k$ of $\pi^*P$ such that $F(\lambda, (q, y)) = f(y) + S(q, y) + \sum\lambda_is_i(q, y)$ is in general position at $(0, (q, \Phi(q)))$ for all $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$ (`exists_sections_isGeneralPositionGerm_of_isCompact`; the points $(0, (q, \Phi(q)))$ are zeros of $F$, `isZeroAt_paramSection_zero`). `lemma_6_6_4_propertyP`: the same sections also give (P), the general position of every slice $F_q$ at $(0, \Phi(q))$ (`isGeneralPositionGerm_slice`). On $[0,1]^n$ itself: `lemma_6_6_4_propertyP_cube`. There are sc⁺-sections over $[0,1]^n \times X$ such that, for **every** $q \in [0,1]^n$, the slice $F_q$ is in general position at $(0,\Phi(q))$ (P) and $F$ is in general position at $(0,(q,\Phi(q)))$. The two are equivalent at every $q$ (`isGeneralPositionGerm_cubeSlice_iff`). `lemma_6_6_4_cube`: general position of $F$ on $[0,1]^n$ for an sc-smooth $\Phi : [0,1]^n \to X$, with $S$ from Proposition 6.6.3 (3) in `lemma_6_6_4_cube_family`.

(2026-11-12: on $[0,1]^n$ itself, (P) and the general position of $F$ hold at every $q$, boundary points included, and are equivalent there. items.title: Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30): the kernels along a family of zeros

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30), p. 265 (preprint p. 222)
book.statement: The solution set $S$ of $F = 0$ near $(t, \varphi(t), 0)$ is a smooth manifold with boundary with corners containing $\{(t, \varphi(t), 0)\}$; by (P) the projection $\pi : S \to [0, 1]$ is a submersion, and its fibres $S_t$ are manifolds with boundary with corners. $L_t = T_{(\varphi(t),0)}S_t = \ker F_t'(\varphi(t), 0)$, and $L$ is a smooth vector bundle over $[0, 1]$.

lean.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and a continuous family $y_q$ of zeros in good position, read in one chart at continuously varying level-$1$ points, the kernels of the linearizations form a continuous family of subspaces of the model space (`exists_subspaceFamily_linKer`, from local frames, `exists_local_frame_linKer`), of dimension the index (`StrongBundle.IsSurjLinOfIndex.finrank_linKer`). The derivative of an sc-smooth family of zeros $\mathbb R^n \to X$, read in a chart, lies in the kernel of the linearization (`hasFDerivAt_scDeriv_rn`, `fderiv_mem_linKer`). `lemma_6_6_5_isManifold`, `lemma_6_6_5_isSubmanifoldOfDim`: near $(0, (q, \Phi(q)))$, $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$, the solution set of $F$ is a Mathlib manifold with boundary and corners and a submanifold of dimension the index. `lemma_6_6_5_submersion`: at these points the tangent space is $\ker F'$ (in the product chart) and $d\pi$ maps it onto $\mathbb R^n$ (`exists_mem_linKer_sliceProj_eq`). `lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold`: the fibres $S_q$ near $(0,\Phi(q))$ are Mathlib manifolds with boundary and corners. `lemma_6_6_5_submersion_nhds`: at every zero near the family, $d\pi$ maps $\ker F'$ onto $\mathbb R^n$. `lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle`: over an open connected $V \supseteq [0,1]^n$, the spaces $L_q = \ker F'(0,(q,z_q)) \cap \{dq = 0\}$ form a smooth family of subspaces (`SmoothSubspaceFamily`) and a Mathlib $C^\infty$ vector bundle (`ContMDiffVectorBundle`), with frames $DS(z_q)b_i$ that are $C^\infty$ into every level (`exists_local_smooth_frame_linKer`). On $[0,1]^n$ itself, at every $q$, boundary points included: `lemma_6_6_5_isManifold_cube`, `lemma_6_6_5_isSubmanifoldOfDim_cube` (the solution set), `lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold_cube` (the fibre $S_q$ is a manifold with boundary and corners near $(0,\Phi(q))$), `lemma_6_6_5_submersion_cube` (in the chart $(\lambda \mapsto \lambda) \times (\chi_q \times \varphi_c)$, the tangent space of $S$ is $\ker F'$, $d\pi$ maps it onto $\mathbb R^n$, and its reduced part onto the reduced tangent space of $[0,1]^n$ at $q$). (2026-11-13) `lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle_interval`: for a path ($n = 1$), $L$ is a smooth vector bundle over Mathlib's manifold with boundary $[0, 1]$ itself (model $\mathcal R^\partial 1$), the pull-back of `lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle` along the inclusion (`SmoothSubspaceFamily.comp`, `contMDiff_unitIntervalToOpens`).

diff: The kernels along the family form a continuous family of subspaces: near a zero in good position the kernel is the tangent space of the solution set (Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54)), the range of the derivative of an sc-retraction; this is what the continuation of orientations uses. (2026-11-09, 2026-11-12: the solution set near the family is a manifold and $\pi$ is a submersion near the family; the fibres $S_t$ near the family are manifolds; $L$ is a $C^\infty$ vector bundle over a neighbourhood of $[0,1]^n$, with frames $DS(z_q)b_i$ that are $C^\infty$ into every level (`lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold`, `lemma_6_6_5_submersion_nhds`, `lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle`).) The remaining differences are decision D2 and the reading in one chart containing $\Phi([0,1]^n)$, which is the text's "$X = U$"; gap G.62 closed (Findings, Chapter 6, items 48, 126).

Also for families on the M-polyfold $[0,1]^n$ itself, whose corners then appear in those of the solution set (`Chapter6/GapP1_CubeLemmas.lean`): there $\pi$ is a submersion in the corner sense at the points over $\partial[0,1]^n$, and the fibres there are manifolds with corners (`lemma_6_6_5_submersion_cube`, `lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold_cube`), read at the chart level: $d\pi$ on $\ker F'$ and on its reduced part, not as a Mathlib submersion of manifolds with corners. The smooth bundle $L$ is over a neighbourhood of $[0,1]^n$ in $\mathbb R^n$ (decision D2).

items.title: Continuous families of subspaces and their determinant lines

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), pp. 264–266 (preprint pp. 222–223); the bundles $\tilde L$, pp. 266–273 (preprint pp. 224–227)
book.statement: $L = \bigcup_{t \in [0,1]}\{t\} \times L_t$ and $\lambda(L) = \bigcup_t\{t\} \times \lambda(L_t)$ over $[0, 1]$; an orientation of one line $\lambda(L_t)$ determines, by continuation, those of all the others, in particular one of $\lambda(L_0)$ determines one of $\lambda(L_1)$. lean.statement: `SubspaceFamily`: a family of $n$-dimensional subspaces of a normed space spanned near every point by a continuous frame; `SubspaceFamily.det`: the line bundle $b \mapsto \lambda(L_b)$, with the frames as trivializations (`SubspaceFamily.Frame.pretriv`, `SubspaceFamily.Frame.coordChange_continuousOn`). Families and orientations restrict along continuous maps (`SubspaceFamily.comp`, `LineOrientation.comp`); over $[0, 1]$ an orientation of $\lambda(L_0)$ is continued to $\lambda(L_1)$ (`SubspaceFamily.transport`, `SubspaceFamily.transport_eq`), injectively (`SubspaceFamily.transport_injective`), and over a simply connected, locally path-connected base the continuation along a path depends only on its end points (`SubspaceFamily.transport_comp`).

book.statement: The proofs of Lemmas 6.6.8, 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33, 6.34) and of Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) use that "as $\tau$ varies, the bundle varies continuously", and that the data of the exact sequences at the end points vary continuously.

items.title: Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38): orientable sections

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38), p. 274 (preprint p. 229)
book.statement: An sc-Fredholm section $f$ over a tame $X$ is orientable if, for any two smooth points $x$, $y$ in the same path component, $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ does not depend on the class $[\varphi] : x \to y$.

lean.statement: `IsOrientableSection`: $\Gamma_f([\varphi]) = \Gamma_f([\psi])$ for any two morphisms $x \to y$ of $PX$ (classes for `scPathSetoid`); `isOrientableSection_iff_exists`: equivalently, there is $y \mapsto o_y$ with $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for every $[\varphi] : x \to y$.

diff: "Smooth points in the same path component" is read as smooth points joined by an sc-smooth path; for points not so joined there is nothing to check (gap G.56; Findings, Chapter 6, items 42, 73). (2026-11-09) The reading is justified: for smooth points, "same connected component", "same path component" and "joined by an sc-smooth path" are equivalent (`mem_pathComponent_iff_exists_scPath`; gap G.56 closed; Findings, Chapter 6, item 124).

book.statement: "An equivalent version": $f$ is orientable if there is a map $y \mapsto o_y$, $y \in U_\infty$, $o_y$ an orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, y)$, such that every smooth $x$ has an orientable neighbourhood $U(x)$ on which $y \mapsto o_y$ is one of the two continuous orientations.

items.title: Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40): orientations of sc-Fredholm sections

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40), p. 274 (preprint p. 229)
book.statement: An orientation of $f$ assigns to every smooth $y$ an orientation $o^f_y$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, y)$ such that, for every smooth $x$ and every orientable neighbourhood $U(x)$, the restriction to $U_\infty$ is one of the two continuous orientations.

lean.statement: `IsSectionOrientation`: a map $y \mapsto o_y$ on $X_\infty$ whose restriction to every orientable neighbourhood of every smooth point is a continuous orientation; equivalently $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for all $[\varphi] : x \to y$ (`isSectionOrientation_iff`). $f$ has an orientation iff it is orientable (`exists_isSectionOrientation_iff`); two orientations that agree at a point agree on the smooth points joined to it by sc-smooth paths (`IsSectionOrientation.apply_eq_iff`), and there are exactly two on each such class (`IsSectionOrientation.exists_two`).

items.title: Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the natural orientation of the solution set

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) and its proof, preprint p. 229; the paragraph after it, pp. 274–276 (preprint pp. 229–230)
book.statement: Over a tame $X$, for a proper sc-Fredholm section $f$ with $(f, x)$ in general position to $\partial X$ at every zero and an orientation $o^f$ of $f$, the solution set $S = f^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners with a natural orientation. Proof: $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ is oriented by $o^f_x$ since $f'(x)$ is onto, and the local prolongation of this orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one. For $f$ not generic, a small perturbation $s$ supported near the zero set orients $S_{f+s}$.

lean.statement: `theorem_6_6_18` ($X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data, proper, in general position at every zero, $o$ an orientation of $f$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40), `SectionOrientation`): $S$ is a compact manifold with boundary with corners in general position (`SolutionSetInGeneralPosition`) with the natural orientation given by $o$ (`IsNaturalSolutionOrientation`): at every zero $o_x$ orients $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$, the orientations read in two charts correspond under the tangent map of the transition (`tangentOrAt_toChartOr`), and along every sc-smooth path of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood they form an orientation of the kernel line bundle. In Mathlib's language $S$ is a compact `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant d) ∞` (`theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`). As a Mathlib manifold $S$ carries the natural orientation (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`, `Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation.lean`): a tangent orientation of the Mathlib manifold $S$ of `theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`, continuous in every chart of the maximal atlas (`TangentOrientation.IsContinuous`, `Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation.lean`), such that at every zero $x$ and in every chart of $X$ at $x$ the tangent map of $S \hookrightarrow X$ (`derivIn`) is an isomorphism $T_xS \cong \ker f'(x)$ under which a basis is positive iff its image is positive for $o_x$. It is built in corner charts (`solOr`, chart independent by `solReadOr_chartChange`) and is continuous through the kernel line bundle (`isLineOrientation_solKer`, `isContinuous_solOr`); the bump functions are the standing hypothesis of §6.6, as in `theorem_6_6_13` (V6.57). The perturbation paragraph: an orientation of $f$ is one of $f + s$ (`isSectionOrientation_sectionAdd`, with $\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$), so $S_{f+s}$ is oriented by it (`theorem_6_6_18_sectionAdd`), for the dense set of perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`). The forms first recorded: `theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet` ($X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data, `StrongBundle.IsProper`, general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero): $S$ is compact, a smooth submanifold in general position with the induced structure of a tame manifold with boundary with corners (the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18); Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) for good position, `MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGoodPositionAt`), and $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ in a chart (`tangentSpace_solutionSet_eq_linKer`). At a zero, $f'(x)$ (`ChartPoint.linZero`) lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and is onto (`ChartPoint.linZero_mem_linSet`, `ChartPoint.linZero_surjective`, `ChartPoint.map_ker_linZero`), so $o_x \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$ gives a ray of $\det f'(x) \cong \lambda(\ker f'(x)) = \lambda(T_xS)$, the tangent orientation (`ChartPoint.tangentOr`, `tangentOrAt`). `theorem_6_6_18_hyp`: moreover, for an orientation $o$ of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)) and every sc-smooth path $\gamma$ of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$, the kernels $\ker f'(\gamma_q)$ form a continuous family of subspaces (`tangentFamily`, `exists_tangentFamily`), and the tangent orientations of $o$ form an orientation of its line bundle (`isLineOrientation_tangentOr`, `isLineOrientation_tangentOr_of_isSectionOrientation`). The Fredholm side is the push-forward for the datum $S = 0$, $k = 0$ (`isStabKernels_zero`, `stabSign_of_surjective`, `stabRayEquiv_zero`), which along a path of zeros is the continuation between tangent orientations (`IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr`, `ChartPoint.stabRayEquiv_eq_tangentOr`, `cont_tangentOr`).

diff: Updated (2026-11-09): the theorem in the book's shape (`theorem_6_6_18`, `Chapter6/OrientationMainClean.lean`), with the chart independence of the tangent orientations in the statement (gap G.68 closed), the perturbation paragraph (`Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation.lean`; gap G.69 closed) and $S$ as a Mathlib manifold with corners (`theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`; gap G.67 in part). The orientation of $S$ as a manifold is formalized: a continuous tangent orientation of the Mathlib manifold $S$ which at every zero is $o_x$ transported along the tangent map of $S \hookrightarrow X$ (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`; gap G.67 closed). It uses the sc-smooth bump functions that §6.6 assumes (2021 p. 274), as `theorem_6_6_13` does; they exist on Hilbert models (`MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`). The forms first recorded are kept (`theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet`, `theorem_6_6_18_hyp`) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 92, 93, 123).

"A natural orientation" is read as the tangent orientations with their continuity along the sc-smooth paths of zeros in a chart, and "the local prolongation of the orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one" as the identity of continuation and push-forward along such paths; intermediate points are reached by the paths $s \mapsto \gamma(t\kappa(s))$, which stay in $\gamma([0, t])$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 91).

"A natural orientation" of the manifold $S$ is read as a continuous orientation of its tangent spaces (`TangentOrientation.IsContinuous`), not as an oriented atlas: for the quadrant model the two differ, since in dimension 1 $[0, 1]$ has no atlas of quadrant charts with positive chart changes (a chart at $0$ increases, a chart at $1$ decreases), and in dimension 0 every atlas is oriented while a tangent orientation is a sign at every point. An oriented atlas follows whenever the positive charts cover $S$ (`isOrientedAtlas_positiveCharts`) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 92, 127).

Tame germ data is the standing hypothesis of Chapter 5; the orientation $o$ exists iff $f$ is orientable (V6.60). "Proper" is the text's hypothesis; the proof uses only the compactness of $S$, which for sc-Fredholm sections is equivalent to it (V5.10), so nothing of the hypothesis is lost (Findings, Chapter 6, item 90).

items.title: Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): the orientation over $X \times [0, 1]$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42), p. 276 (preprint p. 230)
book.statement: For an oriented $(f, o)$ and an sc⁺-section $s$ of $Y \to X \times [0, 1]$, $\hat f(x, t) = f(x) + s(x, t)$ has a natural orientation from $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$: for $L = (f - t)'(x)$ oriented by $h = (a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, the operator $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ on $T_{(x,t)}(X \times [0, 1])$ is oriented by $\tilde h = (e \wedge a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$ (2021; the preprint puts $e$ last), $e$ the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$, and $\tilde L$ lies in the linearization space of $\hat f$ at $(x, t)$.

lean.statement: `SectionOrientation.prodFirst hX hbump hf o hS` (`Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f.lean`) is an orientation (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)) of $\hat f = \tilde f + S$ over $\mathbb R^1 \times X$; in the product chart point over a chart point $p$ of $X$ its value at $\hat L = $ `prodLin` $L$ is $h \mapsto e \wedge h$ (`extConjDetFirst`) of $o(L)$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (`ChartPoint.prodOrFirst₀_apply`, `toChartOr_prodFirstFun`). `isSectionOrientation_prodFirstFun`: $(t, x) \mapsto e \wedge o_x$ (`prodFirstFun`) is carried by every push-forward of $\tilde f$: a push-forward datum of $f$ along $\gamma$ lifts to one of $\tilde f$ along $(\tau, \gamma)$ (sections `liftProd`, stabilized kernels $\mathbb R \times \Lambda$, `IsStabKernels.prodLift`, `SubspaceFamily.prodLine`, continuation commuting with $e \wedge \cdot$, `SubspaceFamily.cont_prodLine`), and the lifted push-forward maps $e \wedge o$ to $e \wedge$ (push-forward of $o$) with no sign (`IsPush.prodLift`); the chart of $X$ plays no role (`prodOrOf_orTransfer`). At a point: `extDetFirst`: the 2021 map $h \mapsto \tilde h$, $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes d^* \mapsto (e \wedge (a_1, 0) \wedge \dots \wedge (a_n, 0)) \otimes d^*$ (`extDetFirst_wedge_tmul`), is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ind}\,L}$ times the sign-normalized `extDetN` (`extDetFirst_eq_indSign_smul_extDetN`); the index being locally constant (`eventually_indSign_eq`), it pulls continuous orientations back (`isLineOrientation_extPullFirst`). `ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOrFirst`: an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L) = e \wedge o(L)$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$; on $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ the 2021 map is the map of the first form times one constant sign $(-1)^{\mathrm{ind}(f, x)}$ (`exists_extConjDetFirst_eq_sign_smul`). The form first recorded, with $e$ last and the sign $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$: `extOp`: for Fredholm $L$, $\tilde L = L \oplus 0 : E \times \mathbb R \to F$ is Fredholm (`isFredholm_extOp`) with $\ker\tilde L = \ker L \times \mathbb R$ and $\operatorname{coker}\tilde L = \operatorname{coker}L$ (`finrank_ker_extOp`, `extE`, `range_extOp`, `extCoker`). `extDet`: $h \mapsto \tilde h$, $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes d^* \mapsto ((a_1, 0) \wedge \dots \wedge (a_n, 0) \wedge e) \otimes d^*$ with $e = (0, 1)$, an isomorphism $\det(L) \cong \det(\tilde L)$ (`extDet_wedge_tmul`); in local determinant charts its coordinate is $(-1)^{\dim F/R(P) + \dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ times a continuous nowhere-zero function (`coord_extDet`). `extDetN` $= (-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ `extDet` pulls continuous orientations back along $L \mapsto \tilde L$ (`coord_extDetN`, `isLineOrientation_extPull`, `LineOrientation.extPull`) and agrees with `extDet` for $L$ onto (`extDetN_eq_of_surjective`); `extConjOp`, `extConjDet`, `existsUnique_extConjOr`: the same after the swap of the factors. In charts: for $\hat f = \tilde f + S$, $\tilde f(t, y) = f(y)$, $S$ an sc⁺-section of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R \times X$, and the product chart point (`ChartPoint.prodPt`, `ChartPoint.prodT`, `ChartPoint.prodK`), $\hat L(\sigma, v) = Lv$ (`ChartPoint.prodLin`) lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(\hat f, (t, x))$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (`ChartPoint.prodLin_mem_linSet`, through the $t$-constant lift `constLift`); an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L)$ the image of $o(L)$ for **every** $L$ (`ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOr`, `ChartPoint.prodOr`, `ChartPoint.prodOr_apply`), and $o \mapsto \hat o$ is injective (`ChartPoint.prodOr_injective`). items.title: Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1): groupoids, $\mathrm{mor}(x, y)$ and the orbit space $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226)
book.statement:
A *groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is a small category consisting of the set $X$ of objects, denoted by $x$, and the set $\mathbf X$ of morphisms (arrows), which are assumed to be invertible, and the following five structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$. (1) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ assign to every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X$ its source $s(\varphi) = x$ and its target $t(\varphi) = y$. (2) The associative multiplication (composition) map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $m(\varphi, \psi) = \varphi \circ \psi$, is defined on the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X = \{(\varphi, \psi) \in \mathbf X \times \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) = t(\psi)\}$, so that if $\psi : x \to z$ and $\varphi : z \to y$, then $\varphi \circ \psi : x \to y$. (3) For every object $x \in X$ there exists the unit morphism $1_x : x \to x$ in $\mathbf X$, a 2-sided unit for the composition: $\varphi \circ 1_x = \varphi$ and $1_x \circ \psi = \psi$ for all $\varphi, \psi \in \mathbf X$ satisfying $s(\varphi) = x = t(\psi)$; these define the unit map $u : X \to \mathbf X$, $u(x) = 1_x$. (4) For every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there exists the inverse morphism $\varphi^{-1} : y \to x$, a 2-sided inverse: $\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_y$ and $\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_x$; these define the inverse map $\iota : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $\iota(\varphi) = \varphi^{-1}$.

After the definition: $\mathrm{mor}(x, y) \subset \mathbf X$ is the set of all morphisms $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = x$ and $t(\varphi) = y$. The *orbit space* $|X| = X/\sim$ is the quotient of the set of objects by the equivalence relation $x \sim y$ if and only if there exists a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; the class of $x$ is $|x| := \{y \in X \mid y \sim x\}$, and $\pi : X \to |X|$, $\pi(x) = |x|$, is the quotient map.

lean.statement: `GroupoidStr Obj Mor`: types of objects and morphisms with the maps `src`, `tgt`, `comp`, `unit`, `inv` and the laws `src_comp`, `tgt_comp`, `comp_assoc` on composable pairs $s(\varphi) = t(\psi)$, `src_unit`, `tgt_unit`, `comp_unit` ($\varphi \circ 1_{s(\varphi)} = \varphi$), `unit_comp` ($1_{t(\varphi)} \circ \varphi = \varphi$), `src_inv`, `tgt_inv`, `comp_inv` ($\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_{t(\varphi)}$), `inv_comp` ($\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_{s(\varphi)}$) (fields of the structure). `mor x y` and `morOn A` (the morphisms with source and target in $A$) are sets of morphisms; `Isomorphic x y` is the existence of $\varphi : x \to y$, `orbitSetoid` the equivalence relation, `OrbitSpace` $= |X|$ its quotient and `π` the projection, with $\pi(x) = \pi(y) \iff x \sim y$ (`π_eq_π_iff`). `saturation A` $= \pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$, `IsSaturated A`, equivalent to: $s(\varphi) \in A \Rightarrow t(\varphi) \in A$ (`isSaturated_iff`). `Ob`, `instGroupoid`: the same data as a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Groupoid`, whose isomorphism relation is `orbitSetoid` (`orbitSetoid_eq`).

diff: A structure of maps on types; the laws are required on the composable pairs $s(\varphi) = t(\psi)$, and the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value, never used (Findings, Chapter 7, item 1).

Not in the definition: the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$, used from Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) on, and the bridge to Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Groupoid`, so that "full" and "faithful" (2017 p. 232, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)) are Mathlib's `Functor.Full`, `Functor.Faithful`.

items.title: Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2): the isotropy group $G_x$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 288 (2017 p. 226)
book.statement: For fixed $x \in X$ we denote by $G_x$ the isotropy group (stabilizer group) of $x$, defined by $G_x = \{\varphi \in \mathbf X \mid \varphi : x \to x\}$.

lean.statement: `Isotropy x`: the morphisms $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = t(\varphi) = x$, a group with $g h = g \circ h$ (`Isotropy.val_mul`), unit $1_x$ (`Isotropy.val_one`) and inverse $\iota$ (`Isotropy.val_inv`). `isotropyEquivVertexGroup`: $G_x$ is isomorphic to the opposite of Mathlib's vertex group $x \to x$; `isotropyEquivAut`: $G_x \cong \mathrm{Aut}(x)$.
