items.title: Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3): ep-groupoids

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227)
book.statement: An *ep-groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ consists of a groupoid equipped with M-polyfold structures on the object set $X$ and the morphism set $\mathbf X$ having the following properties. (1) (étale) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms. (2) The unit map $u$ and the inverse map $\iota$ are sc-smooth. (3) (Properness) Every point $x \in X$ possesses an open neighborhood $V(x)$ of $x$ in $X$ such that the map $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper. Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is in a natural way an M-polyfold in view of Lemma 2.8 in [38], and we require (4) the multiplication map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$ is sc-smooth. In particular, all the structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$ are sc-smooth maps.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid Obj Mor` extends `GroupoidStr` by M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor` on the Hausdorff paracompact spaces $X$, $\mathbf X$ and the conditions (1) `isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`; (2) `isScSmoothMap_unit`, `isScSmoothMap_inv`; (3) `exists_isProperMap`: every $x$ has an open $V \ni x$ such that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V) \to X$ is a proper map (Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction); (4) `isScSmoothComp`, i.e. `IsScSmoothComp`: $m$ is sc-smooth on $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ with the sub-M-polyfold structure of Part I (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`). (4) is equivalent to the sheet form `IsScSmoothCompSheet`: for every sheet $\sigma$ of $s$ over $V$, $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t(\psi)), \psi)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$ (`isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`); $s$ and $t$ are sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_src`, `isScSmoothMap_tgt`).

diff: As for every M-polyfold of the project (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are Hausdorff and paracompact (a standing hypothesis).

(3) is existential per point. The universal form "for every open $V \ni x$" does not hold for the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$, while every smaller open neighbourhood of a good one works (V7.4, V7.59) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 3, 103).

"Lemma 2.8 in [38]" cites the paper *A General Fredholm Theory III*, an external reference, not a misprint; its statement in the book is Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15; preprint 2.46), which the formalization uses. The proofs use the equivalent sheet form of (4) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 4).

items.title: Properness and its sequential form

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227; used on pp. 292–346 (2017 pp. 230–254)
book.statement: Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) asks that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ be proper. The proofs use this in the form: if $s(\varphi_k) \in \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ and $t(\varphi_k)$ converges in $X$, then, "after perhaps taking a subsequence", $(\varphi_k)$ converges in $\mathbf X$ (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 230; Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230); Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), p. 307 (2017 p. 238); Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), 2017 p. 248; Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), 2017 p. 254), or through the compactness of preimages of compact sets (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), p. 342 (2017 p. 251)). After Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) (p. 289 (2017 p. 227)) the text points out that this properness differs from that of classical Lie groupoids, which requires $(s, t) : \mathbf X \to X \times X$ to be proper, a requirement too weak for some of the constructions.

lean.statement: For $t$ restricted to $s^{-1}(Q)$, between metrizable spaces: Mathlib's properness is equivalent to the sequential criterion (`isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`, `exists_tendsto_subseq_of_isProperMap`, `isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`, `isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed`; for M-polyfolds `MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`) and to the compactness of preimages of compact sets (`MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage`). Properness passes from $\mathrm{cl}\,V$ to $\mathrm{cl}\,V'$ for $V' \subseteq V$ (`isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono`); a proper restriction has closed images $t(s^{-1}(Q'))$ for $Q' \subseteq Q$ with $s^{-1}(Q')$ closed (`isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`), forces $Q$ to be closed in the presence of units (`isClosed_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`), and has finite fibres when $t$ is locally injective (`finite_setOf_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`).

items.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
book.statement: Since $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of an ep-groupoid has an extension to a local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ satisfying $\hat\varphi(x) = y$, defined as follows: there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi) \subset \mathbf X$ and $U(x), U(y) \subset X$ such that $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to U(y)$. In the case that $\varphi$ is smooth, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; more generally $T\hat\varphi : TU(s(\varphi)) \to TU(t(\varphi))$. $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$; only in the case that $\varphi$ is smooth is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): associated to a smooth morphism $\varphi$ we have the so-called associated local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, as well as its tangent $T\varphi$.

items.title: The levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228)
book.statement: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are equipped with the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset X_2 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} X_k$ and similarly for $\mathbf X$; $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_k$. For $x$ in the M-polyfold $X$, $ml(x) \in \mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$ is the largest non-negative integer $m$, or $\infty$, such that $x \in X_m$. Since the source and target maps are local sc-diffeomorphisms and therefore preserve the levels, $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; consequently the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0}|X_k|$ of the orbit space. The degeneracy indices $d_X : X \to \mathbb N$ and $d_{\mathbf X} : \mathbf X \to \mathbb N$ are invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7)), so $d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$; in particular $d_X(x) = d_X(x')$ if $x \sim x'$.

items.title: Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6): tame ep-groupoids; $\mathbf X$ is then tame

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 228
book.statement: The ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is called *tame* if the object space $X$ is a tame M-polyfold as introduced in Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19). In a tame ep-groupoid not only $X$ is a tame M-polyfold but also $\mathbf X$ is a tame M-polyfold. This follows from the facts that $\mathbf X$ is locally sc-diffeomorphic by $s$ to $X$ and the tameness condition is invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms.

items.title: Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1): the natural representation of $G_x$

items.title: Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5): natural representations of finitely many isomorphic objects

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), pp. 297–298 (2017 pp. 233–234) (proof pp. 297–305 (2017 pp. 234–236))
book.statement: Let $(X, \mathbf X)$ be an ep-groupoid and $Y = \{y_1, \dots, y_k\}$ a finite set of distinct objects in $X$ which are mutually isomorphic. Denote by $\mathbf Y = (Y, \mathbf Y)$ the full subcategory associated with $Y$, whose morphism set is $\mathbf Y$. Then, given a neighborhood $V$ of $Y$ in $X$, there exists a functor $f$, which associates with the objects $y$ in $Y$ mutually disjoint connected open neighborhoods $U(y)$ contained in $V$, and with a morphism $\psi : y \to y'$ in $\mathbf Y$ an sc-diffeomorphism $f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$. The set of morphisms $\mathbf U = \{\varphi \in \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) \text{ and } t(\varphi) \in \bigcup_{y \in Y}U(y)\}$ decomposes into the union of connected components $\mathbf U(\psi)$, $\psi \in \mathbf Y$, and the following holds true. (1) The isotropy group $G_y$ for $y \in Y$ acts via the natural action on $U(y)$. (2) For $\psi \in \mathbf Y$ the maps $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms. (3) If $\psi : y \to y'$ and $z \in U(y)$, then $f(\psi)(z) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(z)$.

lean.statement: `NaturalRepFinite Y V` (the datum of Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8), V7.26): sets $U(y)$, $y \in Y$, open, connected, containing $y$, contained in $V$ and pairwise disjoint; maps $f(\psi)$, for $\psi$ between points of $Y$, that are sc-diffeomorphisms $U(s(\psi)) \to U(t(\psi))$ with inverse $f(\psi^{-1})$, with $f(\varphi \circ \psi) = f(\varphi) f(\psi)$ and $f(1_y) = \mathrm{id}$; open connected pairwise disjoint sets $\mathbf U(\psi) \ni \psi$ whose union is the set of morphisms between points of $\bigcup_y U(y)$; (1) at each $y$ a natural representation on $U(y)$ whose action is $g \mapsto f(g)$; (2) $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$ and $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(t(\psi))$ sc-diffeomorphisms; (3) $f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ on $U(s(\psi))$ (fields of the structure). `proposition_7_1_15_2017`: for a finite set $Y$ of mutually isomorphic objects and an open $V \supseteq Y$ such a datum exists; `proposition_7_1_15_of_mem_nhdsSet`: for every neighbourhood $V$ of the set $Y$. The construction: `NatRepFinite.transportRep` (a natural representation transported along a sheet), `NatRepFinite.Star`, `NatRepFinite.exists_star`; `NatRepFinite.emptyNaturalRepFinite` for $Y = \emptyset$.

items.title: Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6): $|U(x)|$ and $G_x\backslash U(x)$

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), p. 304 (2017 p. 236) (proof pp. 299–306 (2017 pp. 236–237))
book.statement: Let $X$ be an ep-groupoid and $z \in |X|$. We fix $x \in X$ satisfying $z = |x|$, denote the isotropy group of $x$ by $G_x$ and take an open neighborhood $U(x)$ of $x$ on which we have the natural $G_x$-action $\Phi$, which we abbreviate as $g \ast y := \Phi(g)(y)$ for $g \in G_x$ and $y \in U(x)$. Then the map $\tau : G_x\backslash U(x) \to |U(x)| = \pi(U(x))$, $G_x \ast y \mapsto |y|$, is a homeomorphism. In other words, the obvious functor $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$, which on the object level is the inclusion map and on the morphism level the map $(g, y) \mapsto \Gamma(g, y)$, is a fully faithful functor, which on the orbit spaces defines a homeomorphism between the orbit spaces $|U(x)|_{G_x \ltimes U(x)} = G_x\backslash U(x)$ and $|U(x)| = \pi(U(x))$.

book.statement: Let $X$ be an ep-groupoid and $x$ an object in $X$. items.title: The subgroup $T_x$ of the elements acting trivially

book.label: §7.2, before Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), p. 310 (2017 p. 241)
book.statement: Every point $x$ of the object set possesses a suitable open neighborhood $U(x)$, which can be chosen arbitrarily small, on which $G_x$ acts by the homomorphism $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x))$. We say that $g \in G_x$ acts trivially if there exists an open neighborhood $U(x)$ equipped with the $G_x$-action $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x))$ such that $g$ belongs to the kernel of $\Phi$, i.e., $\Phi(g) = 1$. Clearly $1_x$ always acts trivially, but there might be other elements $g \in G_x$ acting trivially. Since $G_x$ is finite, we can choose $U(x)$ so small that the kernel of $\Phi$ is equal to the subgroup of $G_x$ acting trivially on $U(x)$. We denote by $T_x \subset G_x$ the subgroup of $G_x$ acting trivially on $U(x)$, which, as the kernel of a group homomorphism, is a normal subgroup of $G_x$.

items.title: Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12): the non-effective part $\mathbf X^T$ and the reduced morphisms $\mathbf X^R$

book.label: §7.2, Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), p. 310 (2017 p. 241)
book.statement: The non-effective part $\mathbf X^T \subset \mathbf X$ is the subset of morphisms defined as $\mathbf X^T = \{\varphi \in T_x \subset G_x \mid x \in X\}$. The subset $\mathbf X^R$ of reduced morphisms of $\mathbf X$ is defined as follows. Two morphisms $\varphi$ and $\varphi' \in \mathbf X$ are called equivalent, $\varphi \sim \varphi'$, if the following two conditions are satisfied. (1) $s(\varphi) = s(\varphi') = x$. items.title: The proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

book.label: §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)
book.statement: Consider the open covering $(|U_\lambda|)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of $|X|$. For every $x \in X$ take an open neighborhood $V(x)$ with: (1) there exists an open neighborhood $W(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action such that $V(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subset W(x)$ and $V(x)$ is invariant; (2) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper; (3) there exists a $\lambda$ with $V(x) \subset U_\lambda$; (4) $(\pi^{-1}(|V(x)|) \setminus V(x)) \cap W(x) = \emptyset$. Take a locally finite refinement $(V'_i)_{i \in I}$ of $(|V(x)|)_{x \in X}$, with $V'_i \subset |V(x_i)|$, open $V''_i$ with $V''_i \subset \mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(V''_i) \subset V'_i$ and $|X| = \bigcup_i V''_i$; $U''_i = V(x_i) \cap \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$ is invariant under the $G_{x_i}$-action, with saturation $U_i = \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$. Take a continuous partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ subordinate to $(V''_i)$; $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ has support in $U''_i \subset V(x_i)$. Using the sc-smooth partitions of unity of $X$, approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ by Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) by an sc-smooth $f_i$ supported in $V(x_i)$ with $f_i \ge (\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$; average using the $G_{x_i}$-action, extend to the saturation of $V(x_i)$ and then by $0$ outside, which gives a function $h_i$ compatible with morphisms. The sum $h$ of all $h_i$ is locally finite and always bigger than $0$, and $(h_i/h)$ is the desired partition of unity for the ep-groupoid $X$.

items.title: The tangent data (8.1)–(8.9): $T(X, \mathbf X)$ and its structure maps

book.label: §8.1, (8.1)–(8.9), pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258)
book.statement: The tangent of the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is the pair $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ (8.1), to be equipped with the structure of an ep-groupoid with object M-polyfold $TX$ and morphism M-polyfold $T\mathbf X$. A tangent vector $(\varphi, h) \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ is viewed as a morphism $(\varphi, h) : Ts(\varphi)(h) \to Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.2), so that $s_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Ts(\varphi)(h)$ and $t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.3). If $s_{T\mathbf X}(\psi, k) = Ts(\psi)(k) = Tt(\varphi)(h) = t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h)$ (8.4), which implies $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, the multiplication is $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}(Ts(\varphi)(h))) \in T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ (8.5), where $k = Ts(\psi)^{-1}(Tt(\varphi)(h))$; with the projection $\mathbf p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$, shorter, $k \circ h = Ts(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h))^{-1}Ts(\mathbf p(h))(h)$ (8.6). The unit at $a \in T_xX$ is $1_a = (1_x, h_a)$ with $Ts(1_x)(h_a) = a = Tt(1_x)(h_a)$ (8.7), so $u_{T\mathbf X}(a) = (1_x, Ts(1_x)^{-1}(a))$ (8.8), and the inverse map is $\iota_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, k) = (\varphi^{-1}, T\iota_X(\varphi)(k))$ (8.9).

lean.statement: `tSrc` $= Ts$, `tTgt` $= Tt$, `tUnit` $= Tu$ and `tInv` $= T\iota$ are Part I's tangent maps (`MPolyfold.tangentMap`) of the structure maps, and `tBase` $= \mathbf p$ is the base point (`MPolyfold.tangentProj`). `tComp k h` is defined by choice: if $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ (then $s(\mathbf p(k)) = t(\mathbf p(h))$, `src_tBase_eq`), it is the vector over $\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h) = Ts(h)$ (`tComp_spec`, `tBase_tComp`, `tSrc_tComp`), which exists (`exists_tSrc_eq`) and is unique, since two vectors with the same base point and the same image under $Ts$ are equal (`tangent_ext`); `tComp_eq` characterizes it, which is (8.5). `tUnit_eq`: $Tu(a)$ is the vector over $1_x$ with $Ts(Tu(a)) = a$, which is (8.8).

$TX$ and $T\mathbf X$ are Part I's tangent M-polyfolds, which for $X$ in `Type u` live in `Type (max u 1)` (Findings, Chapter 8, item 2).
(8.5) writes $T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ for $T_{\psi \circ \varphi}\mathbf X$ (possible misprint).

items.title: Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4): strong bundles over ep-groupoids

items.title: Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7): section functors

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), p. 383 (2017 p. 275)
book.statement: An sc-smooth functor $F : Y \to X$ between ep-groupoids is a proper covering functor if (1) the sc-smooth map $F : Y \to X$ between the objects is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism; (2) for every object $x \in X$ the preimage $F^{-1}(x)$ is finite, and there exist an open neighborhood $U(x)$ and mutually disjoint open neighborhoods $U(y)$ of the points $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ such that $F : U(y) \to U(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism and $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigcup_{y \in F^{-1}(x)} U(y)$; (3) the map $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is an sc-diffeomorphism.

items.title: The degeneracy index of $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$ (after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8))

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), pp. 383 ff. (2017 pp. 275–276)
book.statement: The sc-diffeomorphism $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, preserves the degeneracy index, so $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$. The fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times Y$, which has the degeneracy index $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(\varphi, y) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) + d_Y(y)$. Since $F$ and $s$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) + d_Y(s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$, hence $d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = \tfrac12\,d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$: the fibred product lies in a particular position in the full product.

items.title: Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9): $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$, covering functors and geometric lifts

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) and the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ before it, pp. 387–389 (2017 pp. 279–280)
book.statement: $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ is the category whose objects are M-polyfolds and whose morphisms are sc-smooth diffeomorphisms between M-polyfolds. Let $D$ and $C$ be two categories with finitely many objects and morphisms, all morphisms isomorphisms, $C$ with only one object $x$. A covering functor $f : D \to C$ is a functor such that $\mathbf D \to \mathbf C\,{}_s{\times}_f\,D$, $\psi \mapsto (f(\psi), s(\psi))$, is a bijection. A geometric lift of a covering functor $f : D \to C$ consists of two functors $L_D : D \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ and $L_C : C \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ and a natural transformation $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$ of the functors $L_D, L_C \circ f : D \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$.

lean.statement: `MPolyfoldCat`: bundled M-polyfolds (on Hausdorff paracompact spaces) of one universe; `ScDiffeo A B`: sc-diffeomorphisms with their inverses, with `ScDiffeo.id`, `ScDiffeo.comp`, `ScDiffeo.ext`: the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$. For a groupoid $D$ in `Type` and a group $G$ in `Type`, with $C$ = `SingleObj G`: `coveringMap f` maps $\psi : a \to b$ to $(f(\psi), a) \in G \times D$, and `IsCoveringFunctor f` says it is bijective; `IsCoveringFunctor.existsUnique_lift`, `IsCoveringFunctor.lift`: the unique $\psi$ with given $f(\psi)$ and source. `GeometricLift f`: functors `LD`, `LC` into `MPolyfoldCat` and a natural transformation `τ` $: L_D \to L_C \circ f$. `isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`: every functor from an empty $D$ is a covering functor; `CoveringExamples.isCoveringFunctor_id`: a witness.

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), after Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9), pp. 388–390 (2017 pp. 280–281)
book.statement: For a covering functor $f : D \to C$ with a geometric lift $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$: $U(x) := L_C(x)$ and $U(y) := L_D(y)$ for $y \in D = f^{-1}(x)$; $\tau(y) : U(y) \to U(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; for $\psi : y \to y'$, $\varphi_{yy'}(\psi) := L_D(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$ is an sc-diffeomorphism, and $\varphi_{yy''}(\psi \circ \gamma) = \varphi_{y'y''}(\psi) \circ \varphi_{yy'}(\gamma)$. $G_y$ acts on $U(y)$ by $h \ast z := L_D(h)(z)$ and $G_x$ on $U(x)$ by $g \ast z = L_C(g)(z)$, and since $\tau$ is natural, $\tau(y)(h \ast z) = f(h) \ast \tau(y)(z)$: the $\tau(y)$ are equivariant with respect to $f : G_y \to G_x$.

items.title: Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) (Geometric Lift): the proper covering functor of a geometric lift

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) and its proof, pp. 389–391 (2017 pp. 281–282)
book.statement: Associated with a covering functor $f : D \to C$ and a geometric lift $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$ of $f$ there is a natural construction of a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ between two ep-groupoids. book.statement: Let $(W, \mu)$ and $(V, \tau)$ be strong bundles over the ep-groupoids $Y$ and $X$, $P : W \to Y$ and $Q : V \to X$. items.title: Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10): the isomorphism classes over isomorphic objects

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 287
book.statement: Given a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and isomorphic $x$, $x'$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between the isomorphism classes of $F^{-1}(x)$ and of $F^{-1}(x')$: if $F^{-1}(x) = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta_j$ is the decomposition into isomorphism classes, there is a decomposition $F^{-1}(x') = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta'_j$ such that, if $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ and $y' \in F^{-1}(x')$ are connected by an isomorphism, there is a uniquely determined $j$ with $y \in \Theta_j$ and $y' \in \Theta'_j$. (Before the lemma: the objects of $F^{-1}(x')$ reachable by a morphism from $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ are mutually isomorphic, and so are those reachable from the class of $y$.)

items.title: Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids, $\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ and $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$

book.label: §8.2, Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) and the paragraphs after it, pp. 372–373 (2017 pp. 268–269)
book.statement: An sc-differential $k$-form on the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is an sc-smooth map $\omega : \oplus^k TX \to \mathbb R$ on the Whitney sum of the tangent of the object M-polyfold, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric, with $(T\varphi)^*\omega_y = \omega_x$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X_1$; $\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is the vector space of these forms. A form on $X^i$ is a form on $X^{i+1}$, and $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is the direct limit of the directed system $\iota_{i,k} : \Omega^*_{ep}(X^i) \to \Omega^*_{ep}(X^k)$, $i \le k$: two representatives give the same class iff their pull-backs to some $X^l$ agree. The exterior derivative is $d[\omega] := [d\omega]$; $d\omega$ is compatible with morphisms (through $f = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi_0))^{-1}$ and $f^* d = d f^*$), and $d \circ d = 0$.

items.title: Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids

book.label: §9.1, Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the ep-groupoid $X$ is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ with (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) = \{\Theta > 0\}$ contained in $X_\infty$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact in the topology induced from $|X|$; and, at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, (2) an open $U(x)$ and finitely many submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, (3) weights $\sigma_i \in \mathbb Q$, $\sigma_i > 0$, and (4) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ for $y \in U(x)$: a local branching structure.

lean.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples.

book.statement: The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$, the local dimension of $M$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support the manifolds of a local branching structure can be taken $n$-dimensional (2017: are $n$-dimensional); by a footnote (new in 2021) an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if small structures have sheets of one dimension.

lean.statement: A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. items.title: Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: Proposition 9.3, Lemmas 9.6–9.8), the graph representation and tangent slices

book.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413 (2017: Proposition 9.3, p. 302), and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Lemmas 9.6–9.8, pp. 302–305)
book.statement: At a bad point $x$, for a class $\Xi$ of indices with one tangent space $T_xM_i$ there are $i_1, \ldots, i_p \in \Xi$, a partition $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$ and sequences of good points $x^e_k \to x$ with $x^e_k \in M_i$ iff $i \in I^e$. Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11: $L \cap C$ has interior in $L = T_0M_{i_1}$; the $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, are graphs over a cone around $h_0$; the map $a \mapsto a + B_i(a)$ is injective with invertible derivative and its image contains a cone.

lean.statement: Lemma 9.2.9: for an sc⁺-retraction $r$ and a point $x_0$ of its retract with tangent space $T$, a cone $x_0 + s\bar B_T(h_1, \rho)$ lies in $C$ (`ScRetraction.exists_cone`). Lemmas 9.2.10, 9.2.11: near $x_0$ the retract is a graph over a cone in $T$ (`exists_graph_unif`, `exists_graph`), and over a ball of $T$ at interior points (`exists_graph_ball`), the inversion by the inverse function theorem on $T$; all estimates on level $1$ for $1_0^1 \circ r$, brought down to level $0$. The forms first proved, with the graph representation as a hypothesis (`IsGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartAt` for all dimensions at once, `HasGraphChartsAt`, `HasGraphBallAt`), proved on $\mathbb R^m$ by the inverse function theorem, are kept; `HasGraphChartAt` and `HasGraphBallAt` hold at interior points (`hasGraphChartAt_of_mem_interior`, `hasGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior`).

items.title: the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ and oriented tangent spaces, p. 422

book.label: §9.3, the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, p. 422 (2017 p. 310), and Remark 9.3.1 (2017: Remark 9.7)
book.statement: $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is defined like $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ with oriented finite-dimensional subspaces $(L, o)$ of $T_xX$; forgetting orientations is a functor $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. Remark 9.3.1 recalls an earlier notion of orientation.

items.title: Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)

book.label: §9.3, Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313)
book.statement: Four smooth $\beta^{\pm\pm}$ with graphs $G^{\pm\pm}$ define $\Theta$ in two ways; orienting by $\pm(1, 0)$ at the origin gives two orientations which coincide at $(0, 0)$ but are otherwise different; there are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.

lean.statement: For $\beta^{++} = e(s) + e(-s)$ ($e$ = `expNegInvGlue`), $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$ and the two mixed functions, the graphs define a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ by two structures; the orientations $\hat T^1$, $\hat T^2$ given by $\pm(1, \beta')$ coincide at the origin, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$, and no sign choice for the second structure reproduces $\hat T^1$ near the origin. They also coincide wherever $x < 0$. The four sign choices of each structure give four different orientations (`orientedLift1_injective`, `orientedLift2_injective`); a choice on the first structure and one on the second give the same orientation iff all four signs are equal (`orientedLift1_eq_orientedLift2_iff`); so the sign choices give exactly six orientations of $\Theta$ (`example_9_3_5_six`). All orientations of $\Theta$ are classified (`example_9_3_5_classification`): coefficients $a(s, b) \in [0,1] \cap \mathbb Q$ for the four open arcs ($s$ the side of the origin, $b$ the upper or lower arc), with $a(+,\uparrow) + a(+,\downarrow) = a(-,\uparrow) + a(-,\downarrow)$; the orientation is $a\cdot(1,\beta') + (1-a)\cdot(-(1,\beta'))$ on an arc and $A\cdot(1,0) + (2-A)\cdot(-(1,0))$ at the origin, $A$ the common sum. There are infinitely many (`example_9_3_5_infinite`); the six sign orientations are those with integer weights (`example_9_3_5_integral`, `example_9_3_5_integral_ncard`).

lean.statement: (1) `proposition_9_1_9_one`: for $\Theta$ of manifold type, $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold with trivial isotropy (`subsingleton_isotropy_of_isManifoldType`), and $Z = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$, a subspace of $|X|$, carries an M-polyfold structure for which $a \mapsto |a|$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, descended with the text's charts $\Psi_x$ (`MPolyfold.descend`, `isLocalScDiffeo_descend`); any two M-polyfold structures on $Z$ with this property agree (`proposition_9_1_9_one_unique`), which is the reading of "natural". Two choices $c$, $c'$ give $M_c \leftarrow M_{c,c'} \to M_{c'}$, both legs equivalences, a generalized isomorphism of $\mathrm{EP}(\mathcal E^{-1})$ commuting with the maps to $Z$ (`proposition_9_1_9_two_independent`, through `OpenCover.isEquivalence_refineFunctor`). Also `proposition_9_1_9_two`: the full ep-subgroupoid on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has orbit space homeomorphic to $Z$ (`orbitSuppHomeomorph`).

diff: The paracompactness of $|X|$ is not used: Definition 9.1.2 (1) already makes $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact, hence metrizable (Remark 9.1.4, V9.63). "Natural" in (1) is read as the uniqueness of the M-polyfold structure on $Z$ for which $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \to Z$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism; "equivalent orbifold structure" in (2) as a generalized isomorphism of Chapter 10 over $Z$ through the common refinement of two choices. The form with the text's groupoid takes $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \ne \emptyset$, which the M-polyfold structure on an open subset needs (for $\Theta = 0$, $Z = \emptyset$); it is witnessed by the x-axis of $\mathbb R^2$ (`remark_9_1_10_hypotheses_axis`, 2026-11-13) (gap G.95, closed) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 7, 114).

items.title: Remark 9.1.10 (2017: 9.3), the classical manifold and orbifold structures when $d_{|X|} = 0$

book.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.10, p. 405 (2017: Remark 9.3, p. 294)
book.statement: The manifolds and orbifolds of Proposition 9.1.9 are the M⁺-polyfold versions; if $d_{|X|}(z) = 0$ for every $z \in |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$, then $S$ has a natural classical smooth manifold structure in case (1) and a natural classical smooth orbifold structure in case (2). Instead of the paracompactness of $|X|$ it suffices that $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ be metrizable, for example compact.

lean.statement: For $\Theta$ $n$-dimensional (`IsNDimensional Θ n`) with $d_{|X|} = 0$ on $Z = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$: `remark_9_1_10_manifold`: in case (1) the M-polyfold structure of V9.64 has a corner structure of dimension $n$ with degeneracy index $0$, and $Z$ with its interior charted space is a Mathlib manifold, `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞`; $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \to Z$ is a Mathlib local diffeomorphism (`remark_9_1_10_manifold_proj`). `remark_9_1_10_orbifold`: in case (2), for every choice of structures, the object space $\bigsqcup M_x$ and the morphism space of the text's groupoid $M$ are Mathlib $n$-manifolds and $|M| \cong Z$; `remark_9_1_10_orbifold_etale`: source, target, unit, inverse and the equivalence $M \to \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ on objects are Mathlib local diffeomorphisms (`MPolyfold.isLocalDiffeomorph_of_isLocalScDiffeo`). The second paragraph is Remark 9.1.4 (V9.63) and V9.64 (paracompactness of $|X|$ not used).

diff: Hidden hypotheses: $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional: a Mathlib manifold has one model space, while the text's $Z$ may have components of different dimensions (cf. Proposition 9.1.11).

Mathlib has no notion of a classical orbifold (proper étale Lie groupoid); case (2) is stated as: object and morphism spaces Mathlib $n$-manifolds, the structure maps other than the composition Mathlib local diffeomorphisms. The composition $M\,{}_s{\times}_t\,M \to M$ is sc-smooth, as for every ep-groupoid; it is not stated as Mathlib-smooth, since the fibred product carries no Mathlib structure here (gap G.95, closed) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 7, 114).

items.title: Theorems 9.5.4 (2017: 9.2) and 9.5.5, Definition 9.5.6, (9.21) and Lemma 9.5.7, for an integration of forms over the sheets

book.label: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.4, p. 438 (2017: Theorem 9.2, p. 323), Theorem 9.5.5, p. 438 (new in the 2021 edition), Definition 9.5.6, (9.21), Lemma 9.5.7, pp. 439–441
book.statement: For an oriented, tame, compact, $n$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\hat\Theta$ there is a unique linear map $\omega \mapsto \mu^{\hat\Theta}_\omega$ from sc-differential $n$-forms to signed measures on $(S, L(S))$ whose value on measurable $K \subseteq |U(x)|$ is $(1/\#G_x) \sum_i \sigma_i \int_{K_i}\omega|(M_i, o_i)$ for every oriented tame structure (Theorem 9.5.4); with $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ under the local unique continuation property (Theorem 9.5.5). lean.statement: For every integration of forms over measurable subsets of the oriented sheets of a class $S$ with null sets $G$ (`SheetIntegration`: linear in $\omega$, countably additive, zero on null sets, equal (opposite) for two sheets on a common set where their oriented tangent spaces agree (are opposite), invariant under the sc-diffeomorphisms whose tangent maps are those of morphisms, sheets Lindelöf): (9.20) for finite families of oriented sheets (`SheetIntegration.sum_integ_eq_sum_integ`); the local measures (9.21) (`localMeasure`, `localMeasureEff`); Lemma 9.5.7 (`lemma_9_5_7`); `theorem_9_5_4`: for $\Theta$ branched, compact, with an orientation $T$ and, at every point of the support, an oriented tame structure of dimension $n$ with sheets in $S$ describing $T$ (`hcov`), there is exactly one linear map $\Omega \to$ signed measures on $(S, L(S))$ given on measurable $K \subseteq |U(x)|$ by the local formula with $1/\#G_x$, for all such structures; `theorem_9_5_5`: the same with $1/\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ and structures with LUC; Definition 9.5.6 (`branchedIntegral`, `branchedIntegralEff`). (2026-11-13) For the integrals of sc-forms over sheets covered by countably many graph charts (`FormEval.msheetIntegration`, $n \ge 1$; gap G.107): `theorem_9_5_4_full`, `theorem_9_5_5_full`. There is exactly one linear map with the local formula for every oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ (no class condition: the sheets of every oriented tame structure of a compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ have finite $\int|\omega|$, `msheets_of_orientedTameStructure`), under the printed hypotheses with "oriented, tame" read as `hloc`; Definition 9.5.6: `multiBranchedIntegral`, `multiBranchedIntegralEff`. Without boundary, `hloc` comes from $n$-dimensionality and the orientation (`theorem_9_5_4_full_of_degIndex_eq_zero`). items.title: Theorems 9.5.15 (2017: 9.3) and 9.5.16, the canonical boundary measures

book.label: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.15, p. 449 (2017: Theorem 9.3, p. 328), and Theorem 9.5.16, p. 449 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: For an oriented, tame, compact $n$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\hat\Theta$ there is a unique linear map $\omega \mapsto \mu^{\partial\hat\Theta}_\omega$ from sc-differential $(n-1)$-forms to signed measures on $(\partial S, L(\partial S))$ such that, for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$, $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property and an oriented tame structure representing $\hat\Theta$, $\mu^{\partial\hat\Theta}_\omega(K) = (1/\#G_x)\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{K_i}\omega|(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ for measurable $K \subseteq |M^\partial_U|$ (Theorem 9.5.15); with $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ under LUC (Theorem 9.5.16).

lean.statement: `EP.theorem_9_5_15 (hm : 0 < m) hΘ hcpt hT hloc`: for $\Theta$ branched and compact with an orientation $T$ and `hloc` (at every point of $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ an oriented tame structure of dimension $m+1$ describing $T$: "tame, $n$-dimensional", the reading of G.107), there is exactly one linear $\Phi$ from $\Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$ to the signed measures on $(|\mathrm{supp}\,\partial\Theta|, L(\partial S))$, $L(\partial S)$ = `lebesgueSigmaBoundaryH`, with $\Phi\,\omega\,K = (1/\#G_x) \sum_{\partial_1M_i \ne \emptyset} \sigma_i \int_{\partial_1M_i \cap \pi^{-1}K} \omega|(\partial_1M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ for every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$, every oriented tame structure at $x$ describing $T$, and every measurable $K$ with $|K| \subseteq |U(x)|$. `EP.theorem_9_5_16 (hm) (hLUC : X.IsLUC) …`: the same with $1/\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$. The measures are `EP.boundaryMeasure`, `EP.boundaryMeasureEff` (`EP.boundaryMeasure_apply_all`). $n = 1$: `EP.theorem_9_5_15_dim1_all hΘ hcpt hT hloc` and `EP.theorem_9_5_16_dim1_all (hLUC : X.IsLUC) …`, for $\omega \in \Omega^0_{ep,\infty}(X)$, with $\int_{\partial_1M_i \cap \pi^{-1}K}\omega|(\partial_1M_i, o) = \sum_p \pm\omega(p)$ over the finitely many boundary points (`EP.finZeroFormIntegration`; the measure `EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureDim1`, `EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureDim1_apply_all`); Part I's boundary integral of a 1-dimensional sheet is this value (`EpGroupoid.boundaryIntegral_eq_pointInteg`). The class condition of the earlier versions holds for every structure (`EP.boundarySheet_mem_msheets_of_loc`; for $n = 1$ `EP.boundarySheet_finite_of_loc`), through the corner estimate `FormEval.boundaryStratum_inter_mem_msheets` and the tangent comparison `MPolyfold.k1_exists_tangent_eq`. Witnesses with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$: the closed upper hemisphere in $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ ($n = 2$, `E8W.k1_hemisphere_stokes`) and the closed half-circle in $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ ($n = 1$, `K2Arc.k2_arc_hypotheses`).

diff: No hypothesis beyond the text's. "Oriented, tame, $n$-dimensional" is read as in Theorem 9.5.4: an oriented tame structure describing $\hat T$ at every point (`hloc`, G.107); $n$-dimensionality follows from it. items.title: Theorems 9.5.17 (2017: 9.4) and 9.5.18, Stokes' theorem

items.title: Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1) and the remarks around it

book.label: §10.1, Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334)
book.statement: An sc-smooth functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects and an equivalence of categories is an equivalence; equivalences need not be invertible as functors.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth functor is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. $|F|$ is injective for $F$ full, surjective iff $F$ is essentially surjective, continuous, and open when $F$ is open on objects; composites of equivalences are equivalences; the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point has no left inverse on objects.

items.title: Lemma 14.4.5 (2017: 14.6), $\sim_z$ and the $G_a$-action

book.label: §14.4, Lemma 14.4.5, p. 660 (2017: Lemma 14.6)
book.statement: For $a\in A$, $z\in\hat V_a$, $i,i'\in I_a$ and $g\in G_a$: $i\sim_z i'$ if and only if $g(i)\sim_{g*z}g(i')$. Hence $[g(i)]_{\sim_{g*z}}=g([i]_{\sim_z})$.

items.title: Proposition 14.4.6 (2017: 14.5), local constancy of $\sim_z$

book.label: §14.4, Proposition 14.4.6, p. 661 (2017: Proposition 14.5)
book.statement: For $a\in A$ and $z\in\hat V_a$: (1) if $i\sim_{z_0}i'$ then $i\sim_z i'$ for all $z\in\hat V_a$ near $z_0$; (2) if $z_k\in V_a=\hat V_a\cap\partial X$, $i\sim_{z_k}i'$ and $z_k\to z_0\in\mathrm{cl}_X(V_a)$, then $s^{0a}_i=s^{0a}_{i'}$ on an open $Q(z_0)\subseteq U(a)$.

items.title: Lemma 14.4.7 (2017: 14.7), finitely many isomorphic objects

book.label: §14.4, Lemma 14.4.7, pp. 661–662 (2017: Lemma 14.7)
book.statement: Take finitely many isomorphic objects $Y$ and open $Q(x)\ni x$. There are open, connected, mutually disjoint $O(x)\subseteq Q(x)$ and a functor $f$ to sc-diffeomorphisms. The morphisms of $O=\bigcup O(x)$ are the disjoint union of the components $\mathbf O(\psi)$, with: 1. the natural $G_x$-action; 2. $s,t$ on $\mathbf O(\psi)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms; 3. $f(\psi)=t\circ(s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}$; 4. $f(g)=t\circ\Gamma(g,\cdot)=g*\cdot$; 5. $f(\varphi)(g*z)=\gamma_\varphi(g)*f(\varphi)(z)$; 6. the multiplication $\mathbf O(\psi)\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf O(\varphi)\to\mathbf O(\psi\circ\varphi)$ is well defined and an sc-diffeomorphism; 7. the properness property of every $O(x)$.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.lemma_14_4_7 Y hY Q hQo hQ` gives `N : X.NaturalRepFinite Y (⋃ y ∈ Y, Q y)`. That is the Part II structure: open, connected, disjoint $U(y)$, $F$, `sheet`, and (1)–(3) as fields. In addition: $U(y)\subseteq Q(y)$; (4) `NaturalRepFinite.F_isotropy`; (5) `NaturalRepFinite.F_equivariant`, with $\gamma_\varphi=$ `conjIsotropy φ`; (6) `NaturalRepFinite.bijOn_comp`: $m$ maps the fibre product bijectively onto $\mathbf U(\psi\circ\varphi)$; (6) `NaturalRepFinite.comp_srcInv_eq` and `NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_comp`: $m((s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(t\varphi'),\varphi')=(s|\mathbf U(\psi\circ\varphi))^{-1}(s\varphi')$, and $(s|\mathbf U(\psi\varphi))^{-1}\circ s:\mathbf U(\varphi)\to\mathbf U(\psi\varphi)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; (7) $\mathrm{cl}_X U(y)$ proper (`exists_naturalRepFinite_subset`).

diff: Part II's Proposition 7.1.15 takes one open $V\supseteq Y$. The per-object $Q(x)$ and (7) come from applying it to $\bigcup_y W_y\cap Q(y)\cap P_y$, where the $W_y$ are pairwise disjoint (T2) and the $P_y$ have the properness property. Connectedness of $U(y)$ then puts $U(y)$ inside $W_y\cap Q(y)\cap P_y$. (6): the fibre product is parametrised by its second factor ($(\psi',\varphi')\mapsto\varphi'$, inverse $\varphi'\mapsto((s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(t\varphi'),\varphi')$). In that chart, $m$ is the sc-diffeomorphism $(s|\mathbf U(\psi\varphi))^{-1}\circ s$. No M-polyfold structure on the fibre product itself is used. The key identity is proved by connectedness: the image of $\mathbf U(\varphi)$ is connected and contains $\psi\circ\varphi$, so it lies in the component $\mathbf U(\psi\circ\varphi)$ (`NatRepFinite.connectedComponentIn_morOn`).

items.title: The preamble of §15.1: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$

items.title: Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1), the linearization $T(f,\Lambda)$ is well defined

book.label: §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, pp. 684–687 (2017: Theorem 15.1)
book.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ there is a unique section functor $T(f,\Lambda)$ of $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$ with (1) $T(f,\Lambda)(x) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ and (2) $T(f,\Lambda)(y) = \sum_{f(y) = s_i(y)} \sigma_i (f - s_i)'(y)$ for any local sc⁺-section structure.

Chart form `theorem_15_1_1`, model form `theorem_15_1_1_model`. The value: `linearization_eq` (property (2) for any data), `nonempty_localLinData`; property (1): `linearization_eq_zero`.

Functor property: `theorem_15_1_1_functor` (`grfPush`, `toIntr_transportChart`, `linSumIntr_transportChart`): `SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_functor (hf : A.E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f) (hΛ : IsScPlusMultisection A Λ) (φ : A.Mor) (hx : levelVal 1 x = src φ) (hy : levelVal 1 y = tgt φ) : linearization f Λ y = grfPush φ (mem_levelSet_one_of_src hx) hx hy (linearization f Λ x)`. Ingredients: Local section structures are carried along wave 1's local strong bundle isomorphism `E.morIso φ` of the sheet of $\varphi$ (`transSec`, `isScPlusSectionOn_transSec`, `isLocalRepOn_transSec`). The chart $c$ at $x$ is carried to `(E.morIso φ).transportChart c` at $y$. In the carried chart $T\varphi$ is the identity on chart vectors (`chartVec_transport`), and the fibre part composes with $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)$ to that of $c$ (`fiberLin_transport_muLin`). There is an sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda$ with (1) $N(\Lambda)<h$, (2) $\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda\subseteq U$, (3) $T_{(f,\Lambda)}$ onto on $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda\circ f)$, (4) kernels in general position to $\partial X$; $\Lambda$ can be taken structurable.

notFormalized.title: Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2): the weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$
notFormalized.label: §1.1, Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2), pp. 6 ff. (preprint pp. 6–7)
notFormalized.book: With $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, the spaces $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$ of $L^2$ functions whose weak derivatives up to order $m$, weighted by $e^{\delta_m|s|}$, are in $L^2$ form an sc-structure on $L^2(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, "using Sobolev's compact embedding theorem for bounded domains and the assumption that $(\delta_m)$ is strictly increasing".
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V1.42). Formalized in `GapP1_Sobolev1`–`GapP1_Sobolev13` (`example_1_1_3`): for $\delta_0 = 0$ and $(\delta_m)$ strictly increasing, the spaces $H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$ form an sc-Banach space with level $0$ equal to $L^2(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, by Rellich on bounded cylinders (Fourier series), the weight tail estimate, and the density of test functions. The shift map of the 2010 paper on these spaces is not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15): partial cones in place of partial quadrants
notFormalized.label: §1.1, Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15), p. 10 (preprint p. 11)
notFormalized.book: Instead of a partial quadrant $C$ one may take a closed convex partial cone $P$ ($\lambda P \subset P$ for $\lambda \ge 0$) with non-empty interior; for $U$ open in $P$, $\mathrm{sc}^1$ is defined as in Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), with the tangent map on $TP = P^1 \oplus E$, again a closed cone with non-empty interior. Many results should carry over, "but one should check carefully which arguments carry over".
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V1.43). For a closed convex partial cone $P$ with nonempty interior, relatively open $U \subseteq P$ are sc-domains (`IsPartialCone.isScDomain`), so §§1.2–1.3 apply, and $TP = P^1 \oplus E$ is again such a cone (`IsPartialCone.tangentSet`); the chain rule is `remark_1_1_17_chainRule`.

notFormalized.title: Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14): $Df$ need not be norm continuous
notFormalized.label: §1.1, after Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), preprint p. 11
notFormalized.book: "In general, the map $U_1 \to \mathcal L(E_0, F_0)$, defined by $x \mapsto Df(x)$, will not(!) be continuous, if the space of bounded linear operators is equipped with the operator norm."
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V1.13, V1.34), by an example (the text gives none). $X$ is the sc-Banach space of sequences whose level $m$ consists of the $x$ with $(k+1)^m x_k \to 0$, normed by $|x|_m = \sup_k (k+1)^m|x_k|$: every level is a copy of $c_0$, the inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1/(k+1))$, compact, and the finitely supported sequences are smooth points dense in every level. On $E = \mathbb R \oplus X$ the map $f(t, x)_k = \cos(kt)x_k$ is $\mathrm{sc}^1$ with $Df(t, x)(\tau, \xi)_k = -k\sin(kt)x_k\tau + \cos(kt)\xi_k$ (the factor $k$ is absorbed by one level). $(\pi/(n+1), 0) \to 0$ in $E_1$, but $\|Df(\pi/(n+1), 0) - Df(0, 0)\| \ge 2$ (test on the unit vector $e_{n+1}$); since the derivative is unique on $E_1$, no derivative family of $f$ is continuous for the operator norm. Not formalized: that $f$ is sc-smooth (it is), and the shift map of the exposition (§6), which needs Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2) (G.1).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2): classical smooth retractions have submanifold images
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2), p. 22 (preprint p. 18) (proof §2.7.1 (preprint §2.6.1), preprint pp. 54–55)
notFormalized.book: If $r : U \to U$ is a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset of a Banach space $E$, then $O = r(U)$ is a $C^\infty$ submanifold: near each $x \in O$ there are a splitting $E = R \oplus N$ and a diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(O \cap V) = R \cap W$ (the text prints $\psi(0) = x$ for $\psi(x) = 0$).
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V2.108). For a $C^\infty$ retraction $r$ of an open subset of a Banach space, $r(U)$ is near each of its points the image of the closed subspace $R = \operatorname{range} Dr(x)$ under a $C^\infty$ chart, with $\psi(x) = 0$ for the printed $\psi(0) = x$ (`proposition_2_1_2`); the proof conjugates $r$ to the projection $Dr(x)$.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9): sc-smooth bundle retractions and bundle maps
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9), p. 29 (preprint p. 22)
notFormalized.book: A trivial sc-bundle $U \oplus F \to U$; an sc-smooth $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u, v))$, $\rho$ linear in $v$, $R \circ R = R$, is an sc-smooth bundle retraction with bundle retract $B = R(U \oplus F) \to O$; bundle maps $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u, v))$ with \"$p' \circ \Phi = p$\" (read $a \circ p$); the category $\mathcal{BR}$ and the functor $T : \mathcal R \to \mathcal{BR}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page, apart from the categories** (V2.92). Bundle retractions and bundle maps are defined by their shape, $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u)v)$ on $U \oplus F$ and $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u)v)$ with $\rho(u)$, $\phi(u)$ continuous linear, so $p' \circ \Phi = a \circ p$; $Tr$ is a bundle retraction covering $r^1$ and $Tf$ a bundle map covering $f^1$, and the transition maps of $TX$ are bundle maps (V2.94). Before, the tangent retraction $Tr$ (V2.8) and the strong bundle retractions of §2.6 (preprint §2.5) (V2.54) were the instances the theory used. The categories $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal{BR}$, $\mathcal{SBR}$ and their functors are still not formalized (Findings, Chapter 2, item 76).

notFormalized.title: $X_m$ as an M-polyfold for $m \ge 2$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), preprint p. 25
notFormalized.book: For every $m$, the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$ form an atlas on $X_m$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.93). For $m \ge 2$ the structure is the iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$. For every $m$ the identity of points is a homeomorphism $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$, and the level-$m$ lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$ (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, `MPolyfold.shift_level_eq`), so each iterate is $X_m$ with its topology and the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$. Since the fourth addendum the points were known to agree, $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (Findings, Chapter 5, items 142, 146). Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) is proved for every $X_m$ directly (V2.17); Proposition 2.3.17, $T(X^i) \equiv (TX)^i$, for every $i$ is V2.97 (Findings, Chapter 2, item 77).

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18): the linear structure of $T_xX$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21) in $T_aX$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18) and Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) (preprint 2.21), pp. 38–44 (preprint pp. 26–30)
notFormalized.book: $T_xX$ is a vector space with $\lambda[(x, \varphi, h_1)] + \mu[(x, \varphi, h_2)] = [(x, \varphi, \lambda h_1 + \mu h_2)]$, a Banach space through $T\varphi$, an sc-Banach space at smooth $x$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21): $T_aA$ has an sc-complement in $T_aX$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.19, V2.21, V2.25). $T_xX$ is a vector space and for every chart $\varphi$ around $x$, $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is a linear isomorphism and a homeomorphism onto the Banach space $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ (`tangentFiberLinearEquiv`, `tangentFiberContinuousLinearEquiv`), with the text's formula (`definition_2_3_14`); the chart independence is the linearity of the fibre transitions, restrictions of $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\varphi(x))$. At a smooth $x$ the models $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ are sc-subspaces of $E$ with level-preserving transitions, so $T_xX$ is an sc-Banach space through any chart (`isScSubspace_tangentFiberModel`). Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) hold in $T_aX$, the sc-complement read through a chart (`proposition_2_3_19_3_linear`, `proposition_2_3_19_3_sc`, `proposition_2_3_19_4`). Tangent maps of sc-smooth maps are continuous linear on the fibres (`theorem_2_3_16_linear`). Statements elsewhere made in charts for want of this structure (V2.78, V2.99, Chapter 4, Chapter 9) are not restated with it.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19): $p : TX \to X_1$ is open
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19), p. 39 (preprint p. 27)
notFormalized.book: The projection $p : TX \to X_1$ is an open map.

notFormalized.title: Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28): $C_xO$ need not be a partial quadrant
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28), p. 47 (preprint p. 33)
notFormalized.book: Naively one might expect $C_xO$ to be a partial quadrant in $T_xO$; \"however, this is in general not the case\".
notFormalized.instead: **Settled since the first edition of this page, in the negative** (third addendum; V2.33): the claim is false. At every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, tame or not, $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ (with the sc-structure induced from $E$), of dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_C(x)$; the proof reduces it to Flor's theorem on nonnegative idempotent matrices, proved in the needed case. For a non-tame retract only the equality of that dimension with $d_C(x)$ can fail (Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31)). The text gives no example, and none exists (Findings, Chapter 2, item 50).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29): $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ through sc-smooth paths; $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$

notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V2.109). At a smooth $x \in O$, $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ are the closures of the derivatives at $0$ of sc-smooth two-sided and one-sided paths in $O$ through $x$ (`lemma_2_4_9_reduced`, `lemma_2_4_9_cone`), and $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$ (`lemma_2_4_9_tangent`), with the text's proof.

notFormalized.title: The extended faces of a partial quadrant, intrinsically

notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.54, V2.56). A strong bundle isomorphism is the project's `IsStrongBundleIso`, which is an invertible strong bundle map with strong bundle inverse (`exists_isStrongBundleIso_iff`), with identity, inverse and composition. The category $\mathcal{SBR}$ is `SBR` (objects the local strong bundle retracts, morphisms the maps admitting a strong bundle extension in the sense of the text), with `IsStrongBundleMap.isHom` and `IsStrongBundleIso.toIso`; the forgetful functors $\mathrm{forget}[0]$, $\mathrm{forget}[1]$ are `SBR.forget0`, `SBR.forget1`. They land in the category `ScRetr` of sc-smooth retracts, $K[i]$ without its bundle structure, since the category $\mathcal{BR}$ of bundle retracts is not formalized (gap G.5).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) and Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55) in a general presentation of $C$; Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) and $d_X$

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): the dimension is the index; $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$; good position for $d_X \equiv 0$
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
notFormalized.book: The solution set near $x_0$ is a manifold whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index of $f'(x_0)$; at its points $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$; and for $d_X(x) = 0$ good position is the surjectivity of $f'(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (second addendum). The dimension: the dimension $d$ of the solution set near a zero in good position is $\dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)$ at every zero $y$ near it, in every chart (V3.97, with V3.96), also in Theorems 3.1.26, 3.6.11 (preprint 3.23, 3.57), and the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98). The kernel: $D\psi$ maps $\ker f'(y)$, read in the chart at $x_0$, onto the tangent space of the solution graph (V3.99); $T_yS$ as a subspace of $T_yX$ is not formalized (Chapter 2 gap G.13). Good position in a tame chart at $d_X(y) = 0$ is surjectivity, for tame germ data (V3.100), so Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.6.10 (preprint 3.19 and 3.56) hold with “$f'(x)$ surjective” (V3.101). (2026-11-09) $T_yX$ now carries its linear structure and $T_aA$ is a closed subspace of $T_aX$ for every sub-M-polyfold $A$ (gap G.7 closed, V2.19, V2.25); $T_yS \subseteq T_yX$ is not restated with it.

notFormalized.title: The 2021 (untamed) sc-Fredholm germs: tame fillings, and Theorem 3.6.8 for untamed data
notFormalized.label: §3.1 and §3.6, Definitions 3.1.4, 3.6.1 and Theorem 3.6.8, pp. 91, 134–138; with Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27, Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11
notFormalized.book: The 2021 filling asks only for an sc-smooth retraction (no tameness). Theorem 3.6.8 describes the solution set near a zero in good position; its proof (p. 138) uses that the retract is tame. Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27 and Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11 rest on it.
notFormalized.instead: **Settled** (2026-11-12; V3.130, V3.131): read with the 2021 definitions as printed, Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it. A tame strong bundle over $O \cong \mathbb R$ with an sc-Fredholm section in the 2021 sense has a zero in good position whose solution set is a closed half-line, not a sub-M-polyfold (`theorem_3_6_8_untamed_not`; `theorem_3_1_22_untamed_not` for Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26); at that zero the germ has no tame germ data (`not_isScFredholmGermTame_sec_zero`) and is not a 2017 germ (`isScFredholmGerm2021_not_2017`). Corrected form: germ data in a tame chart, the wording of the 2017 text and the preprint and the chart the 2021 proof takes (p. 137): V3.85, V3.94, V3.103; germ data in a chart centred at an interior point of its quadrant are tame (`isScFredholmGermTame_of_chart_interior`). Earlier text of this entry: **Open.** Whether every 2021 sc-Fredholm germ has germ data in a tame chart (Findings, Chapter 3, item 353), and Theorem 3.6.8 and the results resting on it for untamed germ data, are not formalized. The proof step on p. 138 does not go through without a tame chart (V3.115). These theorems are verified with tame germ data (V3.85, V3.94, V3.103); the 2021 corollaries whose proofs do not use tameness are V3.111–V3.114. (2026-11-09) **In part.** Germ data in a compatible chart centred at a point of the interior of its partial quadrant, $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) = 0$, give tame germ data: the chart shrunk into the interior is tame and carries the restricted data (`isScFredholmGermTame_of_chart_interior`, `IsScFredholmGermInterior`); so a 2021 sc-Fredholm section with such germ data at every smooth point has tame germ data (`isScFredholmSectionTame_of_interior`), and Theorem 3.6.8 and the results resting on it hold for it; the hypothesis is satisfiable (`isScFredholmGermInterior_graphSection`). **Open**: germ data in a chart with $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) \ge 1$, which includes every point of $\partial X$ and corner charts at interior points of $X$ (`CornerFilling.zero_not_mem_interior`). **The reading.** Germ data in a tame chart is the wording of Definition 3.6.3 in the preprint (3.50) and in the 2017 text (“a tame strong local bundle”); the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 says “strong local bundle”, and the 2021 theorems' “tame strong bundle” is not defined in the 2021 text, which defines a tame strong bundle retraction (p. 65). For the 2021 text the tame reading is therefore our reading of that phrase (V3.103; Findings, Chapter 3, item 382). (2026-11-12) A local model with untamed germ data is formalized: an sc-smooth family of projections whose rank jumps (`Jump.family`, `Jump.Family.isScSmooth_map`, V3.129) gives a 2021 filling over a non-tame retraction, conjugated to a basic germ and in good position (`UntamedCorner.isFilling2021_g`, `UntamedCorner.isConjugateToBasicGerm_g`, `UntamedCorner.isGoodPositionAtGerm_g`), whose solution set is computed (`UntamedCorner.solutionSet_eq`, `UntamedCorner.theorem_3_6_8_untamed_local`).

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): “$X^1 \ne X$ is possible”
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
notFormalized.book: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (fourth addendum; V4.6), by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give. The 2021 edition (p. 176) adds an example: the space of its Subsection 1.4.4 (a line with a half-plane attached), made an M-polyfold with $X_\infty = X$, for which $1_0^1$ cannot be sc-smooth, since Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) would make $X$ a manifold of constant local dimension; that argument holds as we read it and is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). On the weighted sequence space $X$ of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k+1)^m|x_k|$), $L(t)$ is the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k = 2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t) = 0$ for $t \le 0$. The retraction $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$ of $\mathbb R \oplus X$ is sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss; its retract $O$ consists of smooth points, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)), and the M-polyfold $O$ with its single chart has $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ not sc-smooth. Why an example needs a retraction that loses a level (one with $C^1$ level maps gives none) is an argument, not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10): the section $u \mapsto (1 - p)(u - t(u))$ is sc-Fredholm
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), pp. 179–181 (preprint pp. 151–153)
notFormalized.book: The section $u \mapsto (u, \mathbf f(u))$, $\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))$, of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V4.94), as printed: the section $u \mapsto (u, (1 - p)(u - t(u)))$ of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm in the sense of 2021 Definition 3.1.16 on all of $U$ (`lemma_4_1_11`), with the conjugation of $(1 - p)v$ to a basic germ at each smooth point (`isConjugateToBasicGerm_qOp`). It is still not used: Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9) is proved directly (V4.20–V4.25). The text's proof has a sign slip in $D\mathbf f(u)$, calls $D\mathbf f(u)$ an sc⁺-operator, writes $L(T_0O)$ for $L(Y)$, and omits the interior points of $(T_0O \oplus B) \cap C$ (Findings, item 57).

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14): the local form near $\{d_X = 0\}$
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), p. 184 (preprint p. 157)
notFormalized.book: Near points $a \in A$ with $d_X(a) = 0$ the submanifold $A$ is a smooth finite-dimensional manifold in the classical sense.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V4.32), in the 2021 wording and without tameness. Near $d_A(a) = 0$ the open piece $\{d_A = 0\}$ of $A$ is a smooth submanifold of $A$ that is a manifold without boundary (`remark_4_2_2_dA_zero`, `remark_4_2_2_dA_zero_near`); near $d_A(a) = 1$ the open piece $\{d_A \le 1\}$ is a manifold with boundary, a corner structure with $d \le 1$ (`remark_4_2_2_dA_one`, `remark_4_2_2_dA_one_near`): in a re-centred chart realizing $d_A(a) = 1$, $T_aA$ is in good position unless the boundary coordinate vanishes on it, and then $A$ is near $a$ a graph over $T_aA$ and $d_A(a) = 0$ (the argument of Lemma 9.2.13). The preprint's wording ($d_X(a) = 0$) remains as before (`remark_4_2_2_interior`, `remark_4_2_2_near`) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 61, 165, 176).

notFormalized.title: The open question after Proposition 4.2.3 (preprint 4.15)
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Open Question, preprint p. 159
notFormalized.book: Is a sub-M-polyfold with $A = A_\infty$ and $\dim T_aA$ finite and locally constant a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold? Is the "T" $\{(x, 0) : |x| < 1\} \cup \{(0, y) : 0 \le y < 1\}$ homeomorphic to a retract $O = O_\infty$? Impossible for sc⁺-retracts.
notFormalized.instead: **Nothing to formalize** (a question, not a statement). (2026-11-12) The settled sentence is formalized: `question_4_2_4_scPlus` shows that an sc⁺-retract $(O, E, E)$ is never homeomorphic to the "T", because no neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$ in the "T" is homeomorphic to an open subset of a finite-dimensional space (`not_homeomorph_open`: case $k = 0$; case $k = 1$, three arms on two sides; case $k \ge 2$, a punctured ball is connected), while near each point an sc⁺-retract with $C = E$ is the graph of a map on its finite-dimensional tangent space (`IsScPlus.exists_flat`, the argument of Lemma 9.2.13). The question for sc-retracts that are not sc⁺ is open in the text and not addressed (Findings, item 65). The same holds on the piece $\{d_O = 0\}$ of any sc⁺-retract (`remark_4_2_2_dA_zero`, V4.32).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22): local faces of the chart as global local faces
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22), p. 190 (preprint p. 162)
notFormalized.book: There are precisely $d = d_X(x)$ local faces $F_1, \dots, F_d$ contained in $U$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V4.50). There is a face-structured open $U \ni x$ such that the faces of $U$ through $x$ (the local faces: closures in $U$ of the components of $U \cap \{d_X = 1\}$) are exactly $d_X(x) = n$ distinct sets $\theta_1, \dots, \theta_n$, and near $x$ each $\theta_i$ is the chart face $\psi^{-1}\{\lambda_i = 0\}$ (`theorem_4_2_11_faces`, `exists_faces_chart`, by Lemmas 4.A and 4.C of the exposition); (2) and (3) hold on $U$. For every $\sigma$ the text's $F_\sigma = \bigcap_{i \in \sigma}\theta_i$ agrees near $x$ with $\psi^{-1}(G \cap \bigcap_{i\in\sigma} F_i)$, which carries the properties of (4) (`theorem_4_2_11_preprint`), so (4) is proved for the germ of $F_\sigma$ at $x$, which is what the later chapters use (Findings, items 86, 90; Chapter 4, item 130).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23): chart independence of stratified regularity
notFormalized.label: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166)
notFormalized.book: Regular values of the maps $p_\sigma : A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m$, intrinsic to $A$ and its strata.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V4.93). Stratified regularity of $p = P|_A$ at $z$ (`IsStratRegularPoint`, defined in some product chart) holds in every product chart at $z$, for every data of Definition 4.2.1, every presentation of the partial quadrant and every level-1 lift (`IsStratRegularPoint.stratRegCond`), so it is intrinsic to $A$ and its strata (`isStratRegularPoint_iff_forall`, `isStratRegularValue_iff_forall`). The proof is the transport argument of V4.39: product-chart transitions have first component $w_1 + a - a'$, so their derivatives fix the $\mathbb R^m$-component and carry tangent spaces and minimal subspaces (Findings, items 102, 108).

notFormalized.title: Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25): sc-differential forms and the directed system
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25), p. 195 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: An sc-differential $k$-form is an sc-smooth $\omega : \oplus^kTX \to \mathbb R$, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric; pull-back along $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ gives a directed system with limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09; V4.80–V4.82), in the chart-wise reading. A form is a family $\omega(x)$, $x \in X^1$, of alternating $k$-linear maps on the linear spaces $T_xX$ (gap G.7, closed), sc-smooth in the charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ for every chart $\varphi$ of the maximal atlas; these are the charts the Whitney sum would have as an M-polyfold, and their transitions are sc-smooth (`IsScSmoothRetractMap.whitney`). A covering family of charts suffices (`isScForm_of_cover`). `MPolyfold.scForms` is $\Omega^k(X)$; the pull-back by $X^1 \to X$ (`formLower_mem_scForms`) gives the directed system (4.4) on the bundled lifts $X^i$ (gap G.6, closed), `BundledMPolyfold.formsInfty` is its direct limit $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$, a real vector space, and `formsInftyGraded` is $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$. $\oplus_kTX$ itself is not assembled into an M-polyfold bundle. The preprint writes $\Omega^*_\infty$ for both the limit and the sum; two names are used, as in the 2021 text (Findings, Chapter 4, items 124, 168).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26): the Lie bracket of sc-smooth vector fields
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: (2021) For sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on $X$ the usual formula defines an sc-smooth section $[A, B]$ of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$, proved in Appendix 4.5 (§§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202). The preprint and 2017 texts state an sc-smooth vector field on $X^1$, a section of $T(X^1) \to X^2$, quoted from another paper.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V4.74–V4.77), on an M-polyfold: $[A, B] : X^2 \to TX$, the bracket of the principal parts in any chart, is sc-smooth and covers the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$ (`proposition_4_4_5`, V4.76), independently of the chart (V4.75), by Lemma 4.5.1, whose proof the text leaves to the reader and which is proved by the computation of §4.5.2 in a local model (V4.74) and on M-polyfolds for every sc-smooth map (V4.77); the local model is V4.67–V4.72 (gap G.38, closed). "Section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$" is read as a map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion; the pull-back bundle itself and Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets are gap G.92. The sentence of p. 201 that the bracket at $x \in O_2$ lies on level $1$ does not hold as we read it (V4.73) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 155–157, 161, 162).

notFormalized.title: The exterior derivative, Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27) and the relative complex
notFormalized.label: §4.4, pp. 195–199 (preprint pp. 167–168), Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27)
notFormalized.book: $d : \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^i)$ by the usual formula, $d^2 = 0$; $H^*_{sc}(X) = \ker d/\operatorname{im} d$; the relative complex $\Omega^*_\infty(X) \oplus \Omega^{*-1}_\infty(\partial X)$ with $d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09, 2026-11-10; V4.84–V4.88, V4.90, V4.91). The exterior derivative on an M-polyfold runs in the 2021 direction $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$, the direction item 120 proposed for the preprint: `MPolyfold.extD` is given in charts by the local formula $d(\omega_\varphi)$, does not depend on the chart (`extD_apply`), maps $\Omega^k(X)$ to $\Omega^{k+1}(X^1)$ (`extD_mem_scForms`) and is linear (`extDₗ`). $d \circ d = 0$ is proved (`extD_extD`, by the symmetry of the second derivative); $d$ commutes with $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ (`extD_formLower`) and passes to $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ with $d^2 = 0$ (`formsInftyD`, `formsInftyGradedD_comp_self`); Definition 4.4.6 is `BundledMPolyfold.scDeRham`, read degree by degree. The formula of p. 197 holds with the sign $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ for the text's bracket; with the printed $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ it does not hold as we read it (V4.83). Forms on $\partial X$ are read through the tame boundary $B : bX \to X$ (Theorem 2.7.13): `bForms hP k i` $= \Omega^k(\partial X^i)$ are the sc-forms $\tau$ on $bX^i$ that agree over $B$ (on two local faces through a point the forms coincide on vectors with the same image in $TX$); the definition also lists the agreement of $d\tau$, which follows (2026-11-12; `isFaceCompatible_extD`, `bForms_eq_agreeForms`). $j^* = B^*$ (`jStar`, the pull-back of V4.89) with $dj^* = j^*d$ (`jStar_comp_D`); the relative complex `RelForms`, `relD` ($d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$), `relD_comp_relD` ($d \circ d = 0$) and `relDeRham` ($H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X)$, degree by degree) (V4.90, V4.91). The agreement of $\tau$ implies that of $d\tau$ (`isFaceCompatible_extD`), so `bForms` is the set of agreeing sc-forms (`bForms_eq_agreeForms`) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 120–122, 167, 169, 170, 173).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28): Stokes' theorem
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28), p. 199 (preprint p. 168)
notFormalized.book: For an oriented compact tame smooth $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ whose boundary is a union of faces $F$, and an sc-differential $(n - 1)$-form $\omega$, $\int_N d\omega = \sum_F\int_F\omega$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09, 2026-11-12; V4.92). Stokes' theorem is formalized for classical forms on Mathlib manifolds with boundary with corners. For a compact Hausdorff Mathlib manifold $M$ modelled on $[0, \infty)^{n+1}$ with a continuous tangent orientation $o$ (as Theorem 6.6.18 gives the solution sets, V6.61) and a $C^1$ $n$-form $\omega$ (`ManifoldForm`, `ContMDiffForm`), $\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M}\omega$ (`stokes_of_compactSpace`; `integral_extDeriv_eq_boundaryIntegral` for compact support). $d$ is Mathlib's exterior derivative read in charts, and does not depend on the chart (`ManifoldForm.chartForm_extDeriv`). $\int_M$ is defined through signed charts and a smooth partition of unity and does not depend on these choices (`IntegrationData.integral_eq`); the charts carry a sign since the quadrant model gives $[0, 1]$ no oriented atlas. $\int_{\partial M}$ is the sum of the face integrals in the charts, each face oriented outward vector first as in Definition 9.3.8 (`det_cons_neg_stdFrame_faceFrame`); for $C^1$ forms it does not depend on the choices (`IntegrationData.boundaryIntegral_eq`), the corners are a null set (`chartBoundaryIntegral_eq_sum_openQuadrant`), and chart changes preserve the faces and their induced orientation at the boundary points of degeneracy index $1$ (`exists_face_chartChange`, `orientation_face_chartChange`). The chart-level layer is Stokes' theorem on a quadrant and on a relatively open part of it (`stokes_quadrant`, `stokes_quadrant_inter_open`), with the change of variables $\int_{\varphi(s)}\omega = \pm\int_s\varphi^*\omega$ (`topFormIntegral_image_of_det_pos`, `topFormIntegral_image_of_det_neg`). Forms given only on the boundary are formalized (2026-11-09) as families of forms on the faces of the charts, smooth, compatible under chart changes and agreeing on the corners (`IsChartFaceForm`, `ChartFaceForm`). Every compactly supported one is the face restriction $j^*\beta$ of a smooth compactly supported form on $M$ (`exists_extension`, inclusion–exclusion in box charts glued by a partition of unity). Its integral over $\partial M$ is that of any extension (`ChartFaceForm.integral`, `faceIntegral_eq`), linear, with $\int_{\partial M} j^*\beta = \int_{\partial M} \beta$ (`ChartFaceForm.integral_ofForm`) and $\int_{\partial M} d\tau = 0$ (`ChartFaceForm.integral_d_eq_zero`). $d \circ d = 0$ holds for `ManifoldForm` (`ManifoldForm.extDeriv_extDeriv`) and on the faces (`ChartFaceForm.d_d`), with $j^*d = dj^*$ (`faceRestriction_extDeriv`). In dimension 0 the integral is a signed sum over the points (`ManifoldForm.integral_eq_sum_of_dim_zero`). (2026-11-09) For sc-forms: for a compact $S \subseteq X$ with a corner structure of dimension $n + 1$ (e.g. a compact submanifold in good position of a tame $X$), a continuous tangent orientation and $\omega \in \Omega^n_\infty(X)$, $\int_S (d\omega)|_S = \int_{\partial S} \omega|_S$ (`MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict`, V4.92), with $\omega|_S$ the restriction of V4.92 and $\int_{\partial S}$ the boundary integral of the Mathlib manifold $S$ (outward vector first). On a product end $(a, b) \times N$ the boundary integral of $h(t)\,dt \wedge \beta_N$ is $-(\int h)\int_{\partial N} \beta_N$, also for face data (`ProductEnd.boundaryIntegral_end_sign`, `ProductEnd.faceIntegral_end_sign`). On a manifold with a product end, the pull-back of a form along the end projection is a smooth form after a cut-off, $d$ commutes with it, and an extension of face data can be glued from two ends (`ProductEnd.pullAt`, `ProductEnd.IsEndPullback.extDeriv`, `exists_glued_extension`). (2026-11-12) The faces in their own right: a compact tame M-polyfold has finitely many faces (`finite_setOf_isFace`), and in a face-structured one a face is, near each of its points and in any chart modelled on a tame retract, exactly a coordinate face (`exists_face_eq_coordHyper`). For $S$ face-structured (Definition 2.5.10, the reading of "a union of smooth faces"), every face $F$ has a corner structure of dimension $n$ (`hasCornerStructureOfDim_face`, via the coordinate faces in corner coordinates, `CornerCoords.exists_faceData`), so it is a Mathlib manifold; the induced orientation, outward vector first, exists, is unique and continuous (`inducedOrientation`; the chart changes of the faces are the face restrictions of those of $S$, `FaceChartPair.chartChangeDeriv_face`); and $\sum_F \int_F \omega|_F = \int_{\partial S}\omega$ (`sum_integral_restrictForm_eq_boundaryIntegral`), so Theorem 4.4.7 holds as printed, with the sum over the faces (`MPolyfold.theorem_4_4_7_hyp`, V4.92). The face-structured hypothesis is satisfiable: it holds without boundary (`isFaceStructured_of_forall_degIndex_eq_zero`) and for the quadrants (`isFaceStructured_quadrant`). The preprint and 2017 formulas write $\int_M$ for $\int_N$; the 2021 text writes $\int_N$ (Findings, Chapter 4, items 123, 171, 172, 177).
