(2026-11-12) Also formalized: the wedge product of sc-forms, read classically as $(a\wedge b)(v) = (k!\,l!)^{-1}\sum_\sigma \operatorname{sign}\sigma\, a(v_{\sigma(1..k)})\,b(v_{\sigma(k+1..k+l)})$ since the text uses it without a definition (`formWedge`, `formsInftyWedge`): it is bilinear, associative, graded commutative and unital, and satisfies the Leibniz rule (`extD_formWedge`, `formsInftyD_formsInftyWedge`); $\Omega^*_\infty(X) = \bigoplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$ is thereby a graded $\mathbb R$-algebra (`formsInftyGAlgebra`) on which $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ with $d^2 = 0$ (`formsInftyGradedD_of_mul_of`), the graded differential algebra of p. 198, and $f^*$ is a morphism of graded algebras (V4.87, V4.89); sc-forms on open subsets, with the restrictions $\Omega^k(X) \to \Omega^k(U)$ and $\Omega^k_\infty(X) \to \Omega^k_\infty(U)$ commuting with $d$ (`formRestrict`, `formsInftyResOpen`) and "$[\omega] = [\tau]$ on $V$" of (4.7) (`FormsInftyEqOn`, `formsInftyEqOn_of_iff`); the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 (`lemma_4_4_8`, V4.95) and its local form Lemma 4.5.2 for a convex relatively open $U \subseteq C$ (`hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`, `lemma_4_5_2`, V4.96), with the homotopy operator $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^k\,\omega(c + t(y-c))(y-c, v)\,dt$ about a smooth centre $c$ ($c = 0$ in the text; Lemma 4.4.8 needs a general one, since $B_\delta(x) \cap C$ need not contain $0$), sc-smooth as a parametric integral (`isScSmooth_intervalIntegral`); the agreement of $d\tau$ for forms $\tau$ on $\partial X$ that agree (V4.90); the pull-back of forms on $\partial X$ to the faces of a finite-dimensional sub-M-polyfold $S$ of a second tame M-polyfold along an sc-smooth $G : S \to X$ with $d_S = d_X \circ G$, with $d$ commuting and $(G^*\eta)_S$ extending $(G^*j^*\eta)|_{\partial S}$ (`faceAlongData`, `faceAlongData_formsD`, `isExtendedBy_faceAlongData_formsPullback`), the case $G = p_1$ used for Theorem 6.7.1 (gap G.54). (2026-11-13; `Chapter4/GapP3_K4_BoundaryWedge.lean`, `GapP3_K4_RelWedge.lean`) The wedge product on the relative complex is formalized, so $\Omega^*_\infty(X, \partial X)$ is a differential algebra. On the forms on $\partial X$: the wedge product of agreeing forms is agreeing, and on $\Omega^*_\infty(\partial X)$ it is bilinear, associative and unital with the Leibniz rule (`agreeDFormsInftyWedge`, `agreeDFormsInftyD_agreeDFormsInftyWedge`, `agreeDFormsInftyWedge_assoc`); $j^*$ is multiplicative (`jStar_formsInftyWedge`). On $\Omega^*_\infty(X, \partial X)$ the text gives no product; our choice is the product of the mapping cone of $j^*$, $(\omega, \tau)(\omega', \tau') = (\omega\wedge\omega', (-1)^k j^*\omega\wedge\tau')$ for $(\omega, \tau)$ of degree $k$ (`relWedge`): $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ (`relD_relWedge`, `relGradedD_of_mul_of`) with $d^2 = 0$ (`relGradedD_comp_self`), the product is associative (`relWedge_assoc`, `relGraded_mul_assoc`), so $\bigoplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X, \partial X)$ is an associative ring (`relGradedNonUnitalRing`), and $(1, 0)$ is a unit on the left (`relCast_relWedge_relOne`) but not on the right (`relWedge_relOne`); the projection to $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ is multiplicative (`relFst_relWedge`). The 2021 text of §4.4 (pp. 198–199) defines $f^*$ for sc-smooth maps of M-polyfolds (formalized, V4.89) and, on $\partial X$, only $j^*$ for the inclusion; it does not define a pull-back of forms on $\partial X$ along a general sc-smooth map. Such a pull-back is used only in the proof of Theorem 6.7.1, for $p_1$ on the faces of the solution set $S_F \subseteq \partial X\times[0, 1]$, and that use is formalized (`faceAlongData` above, gap G.54); the general pull-back is not formalized and no statement of Parts I–II depends on it (Findings, Chapter 4, items 158, 167–173, 177, 178).

notFormalized.title: §6.7 (preprint §6.6): the sections admissible for $(N, U)$
notFormalized.label: §6.7 (preprint §6.6), p. 276 (preprint p. 230)
notFormalized.book: For a proper oriented $(f, o)$ over a tame $X$ with bump functions and an auxiliary norm $N$, Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) gives an open $U \supseteq S$ such that every sc⁺-section supported in $U$ with $N(s(x)) \le 1$ has a compact $S_{f+s}$; the distinguished ones, with $(f + s, x)$ in general position at every zero, have oriented solution sets and are called admissible for $(N, U)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09; V6.76). The notion is formalized: `StrongBundle.IsAdmissible f N U s` says $s \in$ `allowableSections N U` and $(f + s, x)$ is in general position at every zero (`Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021.lean`). It is satisfiable for every open $U \supseteq S_f$ (`exists_isAdmissible`). The neighbourhood $U$ of Theorem 5.3.10 is formalized with a margin (`exists_adapted_margin`): $\mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ is compact for every $C > 0$, and $S_{f+s}$ is compact for every allowable $s$; with admissible sections for $(N, U)$ this is `exists_isAdmissible_nbhd`. Admissible sections exist for finitely many norms at once (`exists_admissible_subset`) and for two pairs $(N_0, U_0)$, $(N_1, U_1)$ (`exists_admissible_two`, using `IsAuxNorm.max`). The solution set of an admissible section splits into the clopen index parts $S_k$ (`solPart`, `solutionSet_eq_iUnion_solPart`), each a compact (when $S_{f+s}$ is) Mathlib manifold of dimension $k$, oriented by $o$ (`solPartIsOrientedManifold`, `theorem_6_6_18_oriented_open`). The facts recalled are formalized: Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (V5.38, V5.39) and the tangent orientations of the solution set (V6.61); the orientation of $S_{f+s}$ for a perturbed $f$ is gap G.69 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 101). (2026-11-09) Gap G.69 is closed: an orientation of $f$ is one of $f + s$, so it orients $S_{f+s}$ for the perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`, V6.61).

notFormalized.title: $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is not orientable; the classical case
notFormalized.label: §6.5 (preprint §6.4), preprint p. 218; the opening of §6.6 (preprint §6.5), preprint p. 219
notFormalized.book: The text remarks that $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is known to be non-orientable, though orientable over certain subsets. For a classical Fredholm map $f : U \to F$, the determinant line bundle of the $Df(x)$ is a smooth line bundle over $U$, with precisely two orientations if $U$ is contractible.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized, with a corrected form** (2026-11-12; V6.80, V6.81; `Chapter6/GapP1_DetNonOrientable.lean`, `…Ell2.lean`, `…Transport.lean`, `Chapter6/GapP1_ClassicalDetBundle.lean`). The text gives no hypothesis on $E$, $F$. $\mathrm{DET}(H, H)$ has no orientation for every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space $H$ (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_hilbert`), and $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ has none when $E$ and $F$ are isomorphic to such an $H$ (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_hilbert`) or to $H \times H$ for a Banach space $H \cong \mathbb R \times H$ (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_prod`). In general it has none whenever $E$ and $F$ carry bounded $J$ with $J^2 = -1$ and there is a surjective $T : E \to F$ with kernel of odd finite dimension (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_complexStructure`): along the loop $A_\theta = R'_\theta T R_{-\theta}$, $\theta \in [0,\pi]$, $R_\theta = \cos\theta + \sin\theta J$, of surjective operators the kernels form a Möbius band, and a basis of the kernels is a continuous section of $\mathrm{DET}$ in the chart with $P = 1$ (`continuous_kerDetMk`, `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_kernel_loop`). Orientability depends only on the isomorphism classes of $E$ and $F$ (`nonempty_lineOrientation_det_iff_of_equiv`, through `LineOrientation.conj`). For finite-dimensional $E$, $F$ the remark does not hold as we read it: every operator is Fredholm and $\mathrm{DET}(E,F)$ has exactly two orientations (`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`). The classical case: for $f$ of class $C^1$ on an open $U$ with Fredholm derivatives the lines $\det(Df(x))$ form a topological line bundle with precisely two orientations if $U$ is contractible (`classicalDet_two_orientations`). **Not formalized**: the smoothness of the classical bundle; non-orientability for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces without these structures (Findings, Chapter 6, items 26, 135).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28): sc-smooth contractibility

The preprint (6.28) has one neighbourhood and "(1) $U$ is sc-smoothly contractible" (by $r(ty)$ on $U = r(V')$, $V'$ convex), and its Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36) and property (∗) of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) ask for sc-smoothly contractible neighbourhoods.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-13; V6.32; `Chapter6/GapP3_K4_Contractible.lean`, `GapP3_K4_IntervalHomotopy.lean`). The 2021 text prints (1) as "$U' \subset U$ is sc-smoothly contractible in $U$ to the point $x$", for a second neighbourhood $U'$; the earlier reading of this entry, (1) for $U$ itself, was the preprint's. The 2021 form is proved: for every smooth $x$ and every open $U \ni x$ there are an open $U' \ni x$ in $U$ and an sc-smooth $H$ on the product M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ (`IsScContraction`, `exists_isScContraction`) with values in $U$ on $[0, 1]\times U'$, $H(0, \cdot) = x$, $H(1, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$ on $U'$ and $H(t, x) = x$. In a chart, $H(t, y) = \varphi^{-1} r(\varphi(x) + t(\varphi(y) - \varphi(x)))$ and $U' = \varphi^{-1}(B_\varepsilon(\varphi(x)))$; the text's $\hat r(t, y) = r(ty)$ is this map for $x = 0$; the smoothness of $x$ is used ($\varphi(x)$ must be a smooth point). The preprint's "$U$ contractible" (which needs $r(V') \subseteq V'$) is not formalized, and nothing here shows that it fails; it is a reading point on the preprint, not an item that does not hold. What the proofs of Theorem 6.6.11 and Definition 6.6.12 use is (1′) (V6.48, V6.50, V6.57) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 45, 53, 54, 72, 137).

(2026-11-12) Proposition 6.6.3 (3) and (4) hold for paths $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$ with sections over the M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$: with bump functions, there is an sc⁺-section $S$ of the pull-back of $P$ to $[0, 1] \times X$ whose fibre part is the text's $R(y, f(\varphi(t)))$ (with the sign of `sectionAdd`, cut off outside the chart) and with $(f + S)(t, \varphi(t)) = 0$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$ (`proposition_6_6_3_three_interval`), and $[0, 1] \times X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions, so its pull-back bundle has sc⁺-sections through all smooth fibre points (`proposition_6_6_3_four_interval`); the construction works in any product chart $\chi \times \varphi_c$ of $Q \times X$ (`PullbackChartData.ofProdChart`, `exists_isScPlusSection_prodChart`). The same holds for families $\varphi : [0, 1]^n \to X$ for every $n$, with sections over the M-polyfold with corners $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (`cubePolyfold`, whose degeneracy index counts the coordinates in $\{0, 1\}$; `proposition_6_6_3_three_cube`, `proposition_6_6_3_four_cube`). Lemmas 6.6.4–6.6.5 (preprint 6.29–6.30) are also stated for families on $[0,1]^n$ itself, boundary and corners included: the pull-back of a tame sc-Fredholm section to $[0,1]^n \times X$ is tame sc-Fredholm, with charts of $[0,1]^n$ centred at every point and their mixed partial quadrants (`IsScFredholmSectionTame.paramCube`, `cChart`, `IsConjugateToBasicGerm.quadExtend`); there are sc⁺-sections such that $F$ is in general position at every $(0,(q,\Phi(q)))$, $q \in [0,1]^n$ (`lemma_6_6_4_cube`, `lemma_6_6_4_cube_family`), and near these points the solution set is a manifold with boundary and corners and a submanifold of dimension the index (`lemma_6_6_5_isManifold_cube`, `lemma_6_6_5_isSubmanifoldOfDim_cube`). On $[0,1]^n$, property (P) holds at every $q$, boundary and corners included, and is equivalent to the general position of $F$ at $(0,(q,\Phi(q)))$ (`isGeneralPositionGerm_cubeSlice_iff`, `lemma_6_6_4_propertyP_cube`); the tangent vectors of the family of zeros in reduced directions of $[0,1]^n$ have reduced $X$-components, by a one-sided minimum argument (`mem_minimalSubspaceWith_of_hasFDerivWithinAt`). At these points $\pi$ is a submersion in the corner sense: $d\pi$ maps $\ker F'$ onto $\mathbb R^n$, and its reduced part onto the reduced tangent space of $[0,1]^n$ (`lemma_6_6_5_submersion_cube`; `Chapter6/GapP1_Cube*.lean`). The category $PX$ of p. 272 is also built on $[0, 1]$ as printed (`PathCatI`, `Chapter6/GapP1_PathCategoryInterval.lean`) and is equivalent to the category on $\mathbb R$ (V6.52). (2026-11-13) Proposition 6.6.3 (1′) holds for paths on $[0, 1]$: two sc-smooth paths $[0, 1] \to U$ with the same end points are joined by an sc-smooth homotopy $[0, 1]^2 \to W$ (`unitSquarePolyfold`) with the end points fixed (`exists_isScHomotopyI`; the segment in a chart, sc-smooth on $[0, 1] \times (U \times U)$ in the charts $t$ and $1 - t$, `isScSmoothOn_chartSegment`), and (1) holds as printed in 2021 with parameter $[0, 1]$ (`exists_isScContraction`, G.61); together: `proposition_6_6_3_interval`. For a path ($n = 1$), the bundle $L$ of Lemma 6.6.5 is a smooth vector bundle over the manifold with boundary $[0, 1]$ itself (`lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle_interval`, `Chapter6/GapP3_K4_SmoothLInterval.lean`). **Still read on $\mathbb R$** (decision D2): the smooth bundle $L$ of Lemma 6.6.5 over a neighbourhood of $[0, 1]^n$ in $\mathbb R^n$ for $n \ge 2$ (V6.34; Mathlib has no smooth structure on the cube; estimate 300–600 lines), the stabilized kernels and their continuation for families with sections over $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (V6.42; estimate 400–700 lines), and Remark 6.6.19 over $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ (V6.62; estimate 1,500–2,500 lines) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 71, 102, 122, 124, 138).

notFormalized.label: §6.6, Theorem 6.6.17 (2), p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition)

notFormalized.title: The remarks after Theorem 6.6.17: the orientation bundle, orientability, $\mathbb Z_2$ and $\det_f$
notFormalized.label: §6.6, after Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition)

notFormalized.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the tangent $T\varphi$ as an sc-isomorphism
notFormalized.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227

With the linear structure of $T_xX$ (Definition 2.3.14; gap G.7 closed, V2.19), $T\varphi$ is a bounded linear isomorphism $T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMorCLE`, `definition_7_1_4_linear`), and for smooth $\varphi$ an sc-isomorphism: in charts $T\varphi$ and $T(\varphi^{-1})$ are sc-operators restricting to mutually inverse maps of the sc-subspaces that are $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ and $T_{t(\varphi)}X$ as sc-Banach spaces (`definition_7_1_4_sc`, `tangentMor_chart_sc`, `Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear.lean`). (Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110, 154; Chapter 8, item 112).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017; rewritten in 2021 as Theorem 7.2.14): $\mathbf X^R$ Hausdorff and paracompact
notFormalized.label: §7.2, Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), pp. 313–324 (2017 pp. 242–244)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9): the reduced morphism set $\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure. Proposition 7.10 (2017): every ep-groupoid $X$ possesses an associated reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, and $X_R$ is effective. Since an M-polyfold is a paracompact Hausdorff space (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), these assert in particular that $\mathbf X^R$, with the quotient topology, is Hausdorff and paracompact, for every ep-groupoid $X$. The 2021 edition rewrites this: Remark 7.2.8 (p. 311) says that in general $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ cannot be made an ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.12 (p. 317) proves $T_R$ paracompact for every ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.13 (p. 318) makes it an M-polyfold exactly when it is Hausdorff, and Theorem 7.2.14 (p. 318) builds $X_R$ under the hypothesis that $T_R$ is Hausdorff, characterized in Theorem 7.2.22 (p. 323).
notFormalized.instead: **Closed by the 2021 edition**, in its 2021 form. In the 2017 form, for every ep-groupoid, the statement does not hold as we read it: for $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff (`Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`, formalized after the round-trip audit), and the hypotheses `[T2Space X.ReducedMor] [ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor]` of `reducedPolyfold` were the project's (V7.39, V7.40). The 2021 text is consistent with this: Remark 7.2.8 announces such examples, Appendix 7.6.3 gives Zhou's, of the same kind (V7.82). Paracompactness is now proved for every ep-groupoid (`paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, an instance, V7.77), which also settles the question, left open here, of paracompactness when $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff; the Hausdorff hypothesis is exactly that of 2021 Theorem 7.2.14 (V7.78), and Theorem 7.2.22 characterizes it by LUC and the closedness of $\mathbf X^T$ (V7.81) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 60, 107, 111, 125, 126, 129).

notFormalized.title: Appendix 7.6.3: Zhou's retract and its exact non-effective part
notFormalized.label: §7.6, Appendix 7.6.3, p. 348, and §7.4, p. 331 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Zhou's example: $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the retract of Part I's Subsection 1.4.4 by $(s, f) \mapsto (s, -f)$; $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$ is one point, so $T_R$ is not Hausdorff and (LUC) fails; the example does not satisfy the Zhou condition (p. 331).

For $\mathbb Z/2$ acting by $(t,f) \mapsto (t,-f)$, `ZhouRetract.appendix_7_6_3` computes $\mathbf X^T = (\{1\}\times Y) \cup (\{-1\}\times\{t<0\})$ and $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T)\setminus\mathbf X^T = \{(-1,(0,0))\}$ exactly as the text does. So $T_R$ is not Hausdorff, and (LUC) and (ZHOU) fail (`ZhouRetract.not_isZhou`). The identification $Y\cong\Sigma$ is a homeomorphism (`sigmaHomeo`), and the computation is also stated on $\{0,1\}\times\Sigma$ as printed (`appendix_7_6_3_sigma`) (V7.82, V7.95) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 130, 139).

(VSLUC) and the density of $X_\infty$ pass from $X$ to every $X^i$, giving Propositions 7.4.16 and 7.4.17 (V7.103). notFormalized.title: The Part I facts used in §7.4, and the connectedness of $U(x) \cap X_1$
notFormalized.label: §7.4, Lemma 7.4.4, p. 329, and the proofs of Lemma 7.4.6 to Proposition 7.4.22, pp. 331–340 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The proofs use facts about M-polyfolds: $X_\infty$ dense in every $X_m$; $U(x) \cap X_\infty$ connected for connected open $U(x)$; tangent vectors approximated by tangent vectors at nearby smooth points; sc-smooth maps agreeing near a smooth point in $X_\infty$ have the same tangent there; $(T_xX)_\infty$ dense in $T_xX$. The proof of Lemma 7.4.4 uses that $U(x) \cap X_1$ is connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V7.86, V7.83). Every fact is a theorem for every M-polyfold: `MPolyfold.smoothRegular` (from `denseSmooth`, gap G.73; `smoothConnected`, through smooth paths, `isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage`; `isOpenMap_tangentProj`, gap G.8; `tangentDeterminedSmooth`) and `MPolyfold.denseSmoothTangent`. Every natural representation has $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$ (`NaturalRep.isPreconnected_liftU`, `NaturalRep.subset_closure_inter_levelSet`), so `HasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps` holds for every ep-groupoid (`hasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps`), and so does `HasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps` of Lemma 7.4.4, which is not restated without it (V7.85); every natural representation has every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected (`NaturalRep.levelConnected`), the text's \"by construction\" in Proposition 7.4.18. The §7.4, §7.6 and §8.1 results are restated without these hypotheses (V7.83, V7.89–V7.95, V7.102–V7.104, V8.45, V8.52) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 133, 134, 153).

The exterior derivative is $d[\omega] := [d\omega]$, with $d\omega$ compatible with morphisms and $d \circ d = 0$. notFormalized.title: The graph representation of Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 on a general M-polyfold, and Proposition 9.2.8 as printed
notFormalized.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413 (2017: Proposition 9.3, p. 302), and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Lemmas 9.6–9.8); used in Proposition 9.1.12, p. 408

notFormalized.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (2), p. 301)

notFormalized.title: Definition 9.2.12: the $TM_i$ as smooth submanifolds of $TX$

notFormalized.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311)

notFormalized.title: Example 9.3.5: the classification of all orientations of $\Theta$
notFormalized.label: §9.3, Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313)
notFormalized.book: There are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.

notFormalized.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314)

notFormalized.title: $[0,1] \times X$: paracompact orbit space, partitions of unity; a witness for Corollary 15.3.10 (3)

notFormalized.title: Polyfolds are metrizable (the remark after Definition 16.1.1)
notFormalized.label: §16.1, after Definition 16.1.1, p. 706 (2017: Proposition 16.1)
notFormalized.book: If $|X|$ is paracompact, $Z \cong |X|$ is metrizable (locally metrizable, regular, Hausdorff and paracompact: Nagata–Smirnov).
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-13, Part III wave 2; V16.14): `PolyfoldStructure.metrizableSpace` (`P3H_TangentPolyfold.lean`), from Theorem 7.3.1's `theorem_7_3_1_metrizable`. The metrization step is Part I's `metrizableSpace_of_locally` (Chapter 2), so no Smirnov theorem from Mathlib is needed. In 2017 this was the numbered Proposition 16.1; in the 2021 text it is a remark in prose.

notFormalized.title: Naturality of the structure on $\mathrm{supp}\,\theta$
notFormalized.label: §16.4, Proposition 16.4.3, p. 730 (2017: Proposition 16.6)
notFormalized.book: The manifold (orbifold) structure on $\mathrm{supp}\,\theta$ is induced from the overhead and does not depend on the representative.
notFormalized.instead: For every representative: $\mathrm{supp}\,\theta \simeq_t |\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta|$ and the induced structure (`proposition_16_4_3_manifold`, `proposition_16_4_3_orbifold`, V16.24). Also: the transition homeomorphism `suppTransition` between two representatives (with the cocycle identities), the statement `proposition_16_4_3_naturality_statement` and its case $a' = a$ (`proposition_16_4_3_naturality_self`). Missing: the general case. It needs a generalized isomorphism $X \leftarrow A \to X'$ between the representatives to restrict to the supports ($\Theta$ pulls back along both legs, Theorem 11.3.3) as an equivalence of the sub-ep-groupoids on $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, and that an equivalence of ep-subgroupoids induces local sc-diffeomorphisms of the structures of Proposition 9.1.9 (the structures are existential, so the statement chooses them). Not checked against the trivial-action $\mathbb Z/3$ examples; it presumably holds for manifold type. Estimate 300–450 lines.

notFormalized.title: The tangent projection and the raised polyfolds
notFormalized.label: §16.2, pp. 715 and 717 (2017: §16.2)
notFormalized.book: $(Z,c)^i = (Z_i, c_i)$, and $\tau_Z : T(Z,c) \to Z^1$ with $\tau_Z \circ T\alpha = \alpha \circ |\tau_X|$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-13, Part III wave 4; V16.35, V16.36; `Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold.lean`): the raised structures through `Diagram.liftOne` and `EPLoc.liftOneHom` (`RaisedSpace c`, `raiseMap`, `raiseStructure`, `raise c` with `raise_eq`, the injection `raiseIncl` with image $Z_1$, `raiseN`), and $\tau_Z$ = `tangentProj` with $\tau_Z \circ T\alpha = \alpha^1 \circ |\tau_X|$ (`tangentProj_tangentMap`, from the naturality `EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentProj_tangentHom`). $(Z,c)^1$ carries the topology of $|X^1|$, not the subspace topology of $Z$.

notFormalized.title: The tangent of an effective polyfold is effective
notFormalized.label: §16.2, Theorem 16.2.4, p. 719 (2017: Theorem 16.1)
notFormalized.book: $T$ is a functor on the polyfold category.
notFormalized.instead: $T$ is a functor on PS (`PSCat.tangentFunctor`) and is well defined on sc-smooth maps (`ScMap.tangent`, `theorem_16_2_4`; V16.34). The pull-back of forms is formalized on every class (V16.21). $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ is proved (`tangent_comp`) under `d.tangent.IsEffective`; this hypothesis has no witness, so `tangent_comp` is a conditional form, not a `_hyp` theorem. That $T$ preserves effectiveness, and so that $T$ is a Mathlib functor of `EffPolyfold`, is not formalized. Presumably it follows since the isotropy of $TX$ at $(x,h)$ lies in $G_x$ and morphisms near $(g,h)$ in $TX$ lie over morphisms near $g$. Estimate 60–150 lines. (Until 2026-11-13 this entry was "The tangent functor and the pull-back of forms on the polyfold category"; the morphisms of Definitions 16.1.6–16.1.11, the functor on PS and the pull-back were formalized in Part III wave 3.)

About 300–600 lines.
